News.title: Nursery owner and staff jailed after lacing over 200 children’s food with lead to ‘make it more appealing’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SCHOOL POISON Nursery owner and staff jailed after lacing over 200 children’s food with lead to ‘make it more appealing’







Next

A NURSERY boss has been jailed for life after hundreds of children were poisoned with toxic pigments deliberately added to their school meals.

Li Huifang was handed the crushing sentence after 247 youngsters were found with dangerously high levels of lead in their blood at a nursery in China.

The shocking scandal unfolded at Heshi Peixin Kindergarten in Tianshui, in China’s Gansu province.

Kitchen staff had been adding poisonous, inedible pigments to children’s food to make their meals look more colourful.





More than 20 employees were also exposed to the toxic substances, which can cause severe damage to the brain and nervous system.

A court heard how Li, who operated the kindergarten, and executive principal Zhu Jinglin ordered four kitchen workers to lace meals with harmful chemicals.

The sickening practice was exposed in July 2025 when blood tests revealed widespread lead contamination among pupils and staff.

Reports revealed that inedible pigments containing lead had been added to the food to make meals appear more colourful.

The shocking findings sparked a criminal investigation into the kindergarten’s management and kitchen staff.

Li was sentenced to life behind bars, with the court also ordering the confiscation of 500,000 yuan (£52,000) worth of her personal assets.

Her fellow ringleader Zhu was jailed for 15 years and slapped with a 300,000 yuan (£31,000) fine.

Four kitchen workers involved in preparing the contaminated meals were also handed prison sentences ranging from six to eight years.



The damning verdict brought criminal proceedings against the six defendants to a close following the poisoning scandal.

Lead exposure is particularly dangerous for young children because it can cause lasting damage to the developing brain and nervous system.

The sentencing came just a day after the World Health Organization issued a stark warning about the global threat of lead poisoning.

Health chiefs urged countries to step up efforts to protect children from exposure to the dangerous metal, which affects hundreds of millions of youngsters worldwide.

Bruce Gordon, head of the WHO’s environment department, warned: “Lead poisoning is one of the world’s most serious yet overlooked environmental health threats.”



The organisation said children and adults can be exposed to lead through everyday products, including paint, cookware, cosmetics and spices.

Industrial contamination also remains a major source of exposure to the poisonous substance.

News.title: Dramatic moment cops charge protesters near Eurostar station and fire tear gas as riots across France erupt into chaos
News.content:
Next

THIS is the dramatic moment French riot cops clash with protesters near a Eurostar station as chaos erupts across France.

Shocking footage shows cops striking wild demonstrators with batons as the two groups collide in Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Denis, Paris.



Wearing helmets and stab vests, a wall of police scramble against a surge of activists holding placards as flares and tear gas fills the street with smoke.

The shocking clash struck just steps away from where the Eurostar arrives into the French capital from London.



Metro stations across the country were locked down on Saturday as protests against rising fuel prices and the cost of living erupted.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuez said officials were prepared for hundreds of demonstrations to sweep through several cities.



The worst trouble struck in Paris and Marseille, where officers failed to stop their own buildings being ransacked.

Video showed windows being smashed by youths in masks and hoods, before they threw molotov cocktails inside.



Nearby sports and clothes shops were also looted by gangs as riot police moved in.

More than 100 rioters had already been arrested by 1pm in the French capital, police said.

These were “primarily for carrying weapons or prohibited protective gear”, the force added in an update on X.



“Gangs of unauthorised protesters are roaming around the city, while many are meeting on major squares,” said a police spokesman.

More than 80 marches are expected across the nation with police conducting “enhanced checks to prevent risks”.

A march was due to start in Place de la République – one of the traditional protest squares in the city, and water cannon and other riot control measures were already in place.

Separate footage shows riot cops charging at a crowd of masked protesters in Strasbourg, in the northeast of France.

Police armed with batons launched tear gas towards the group before storming shield-first through a thick cloud of smoke.



The unrest has joined ongoing protests by hundreds of thousands of students which have shut down schools for more than three weeks.

Enraged protesters demand more investment in the education system, criticising a lack of teachers and staff, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

The latest mobilization follows calls on social media to revive the yellow vest movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice.



Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join in.

The CGT, one of France’s major labour unions, also backs the protests calling for higher wages and pensions, lower prices and the protection of public services.

Emmanuel Macron called for calm on Friday as officials warned of further violence and denounced those who joined riots simply to cause havoc.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The French president was blasted for attending a Céline Dion concert with his wife on Friday night as France braced for another day of chaos.

The 48-year-old head of state and Brigitte Macron, 73, were filmed dancing at the pop superstar’s concert in the Paris suburbs.

News.title: Baby-faced hitmen for hire & ‘Call of Duty’ slayings… How twisted Iran-backed ‘Foxtrot Network’ is operating in UK
News.content:
Next

STOOD in the lobby of a Huddersfield hotel off the M62, most guests wouldn’t look twice at the hooded teenager checking in.

But Johannes Natland, the guest at reception, used the 3-star Briar Court as his base while attempting an assassination for a fearsome European crime network back by Iran.



The Norweigan was hired by the Foxtrot Network, a Swedish crime group who use videogame tactics to recruit teenagers, offering them thousands to carry out ‘violence-as-a-service’ (VaaS).

Natland, 19, who was jailed for 20 years yesterday over the failed 2025 plot, was the latest recruit of the group who’ve committed 35 murders since 2022.



Security experts have now told The Sun exactly how Iran-backed Foxtrot pay “child soldiers’ to kill – and how another UK murder plot could still take place.

Swedish investigative journalist Diamant Salihu described how Foxtrot recruits “child soldiers” for contact killings, controlling them on video calls “like they’re playing Call of Duty”.



And former Met Police detective Peter Bleksley warned that preventing future Foxtrot UK murders would be a huge drain on UK security because the killings are carried out by “disillusioned lone wolf” attackers.

Foxtrot is backed by the Iranian regime and is known for deploying children as young as 12 in drug smuggling and violent crime.



The shadowy group are linked to a number of assassinations and explosive attacks in recent years, including an undetonated bomb at the Israeli embassy in Stockholm, a hand grenade attack on a beauty salon in Oslo, and another explosives blast on a restaurant in Strommen, Norway.

All the attacks were committed by boys aged between 12 and 15.

Last year, 18-year-old Atilla Azimov gunned down 20-year-old McDonald’s worker Murad Abdelkader in Stockholm after being instructed by Foxtrot.



Talented football Natland had agreed to shoot an unknown target for 25,000 euro (£21,500) in March last year.

Two days after arriving in the UK from his home in Stavanger, armed police arrested him at the Briar Court hotel, seizing a semi-automatic pistol, a revolver, 12 rounds of live ammo, gloves and £2,000 in cash.

Natland planned the killing on UK soil after receiving a chilling online request which simply said: “Killing in England 270k” (Norweigan kroner is around £21,500).



He’d told his girlfriend, “I’m going on a crazy mission”, but his UK target still remains unknown.

Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb said Natland had been a “good student” from a secure family in Norway, before he fell into drug use and was recruited to “murder for money” by Foxtrot.

Natland’s recruiter, a 17-year-old known as “Generalen”, was convicted in Norway of attempting to “contribute to murder” in May last year.



He’d been arrested after trying to arrange the assassination of the 14-year-old son of a Norweigan police officer, recruiting a 15-year-old and 17-year-old to carry out a knife attack.

When police arrested him, they found details of the Huddersfield murder plot on his phone, allowing UK detectives to stop Natland hours before his planned killing.

The Foxtrot Network and its leader, Rawa Majid, were both sanctioned by the UK government in April 2025, a month after Natland’s arrest.



Majid, aged 40 and known as “The Kurdish Fox”, has fled Sweden and is now thought to be in Iran, where he lives freely in return for Foxtrot carrying out killings on behalf of the country’s regime.

Ali Shehad Ahmed, who is close to Majid, has been accused of being the “Agent 47” who instructs assassins, according to Swedish cops.

Swedish investigative journalist Diamant Salihu said Foxtrot gang leaders control teenage boys “like they’re playing Call of Duty”, using group chats and FaceTime to instruct boys to shoot at gang rivals, detonate explosives or perform contract killings.

In 2024, a 13-year-old Swedish boy opened fire outside Elbit Systems, an Israeli tech firm in Gothenburg.



Nobody was hurt, but it was the latest in a spate of shootings ordered by Foxtrot.

The previous month, Israeli embassies were targeted in Sweden and Denmark.

Salihu told how in another Foxtrot attack in Gavle, Sweden, a 13-year-old listened on AirPods for instructions, before being told, “Now you can shoot”, when he opened fire on six people.

His “controller”, the same Foxtrot leader who instructed Natland in Huddersfield, was known only as Agent 47 – an apparent reference to the Hitman assassination gaming series.



Salihu said: “These are gamified environments where they (Foxtrot) find lonely, vulnerable teenagers that have no links to these networks but are willing to take these jobs and think they’ll earn money.

“It’s like they’re playing Call of Duty – they tell the perpetrators to film on FaceTime so they can see the shootings happen in real time.”

Salihu said Foxtrot perform shootings on Iran’s behalf after the regime “saw its global reach” and used the Swedish gang to target its enemies.

He added that Foxtrot have openly posted on Telegram and other social media for new recruits, using six steps to find new teenage assassins.

He said: “First they use an ad with local recruiters, then that person is identified – sometimes they’re asked to send a passport photo.



“The next step is the job is confirmed and they’re told their destination, then after that they’ll be given guns, money and somewhere to stay.

“The next step is they’re given the target.”

Natland only made it through the first four stages of Foxtrot’s assassination process before he was arrested in his Huddersfield hotel room at 5.15am, wearing only his boxer shorts.

He had previously boasted to his girlfriend that he had got the “bangs in the bag”, took selfies guns and cash on his bed, and had also told a friend: “I’m going to get a lot of money and somebody is going to die.”

Natland had also confided in his girlfriend before leaving for the UK, telling her: “Now I can finally kill someone and it’s perfect as I get money to do it. I can kill someone and life will be wonderful.”



Foxtrot promise big sums of cash to teenage boys knowing they’ll never have to pay out if their recruits are caught.

Giving evidence, Natland said he wanted to look “cool” to his peers but it was just “bravado” and inside he was “terrified”.

Natland told jurors: “I wasn’t an international assassin. I thought people had this impression and expected me to be this guy. I knew I wasn’t.”

Former Met Police detective Peter Bleksley said Foxtrot are able to recruit unsupervised “lone wolf” teens who “fall down dangerous online rabbit holes”.

He told The Sun: “Children can become very easy prey for these predators scouring the internet looking for people whose lives are unfulfilled.



“These children are often dim-witted, disillusioned, and consequently dangerous.

“They are so stupid that they get lured in by the promise of money which in all likelihood they’ll never receive, because they’ll get caught.

“It’s a heady mix of fleeting fame, money, notoriety, and being part of an organisation which makes them feel like they belong in this world – which they clearly don’t have from their families and friends.

“Had the Norweigans not acted as well as they did (in catching Generalen), Natland would have committed murder on UK soil, and we still don’t know who his target is, so it’s deeply concerning.”

Europol, the EU crime agency tasked with stopping Foxtrot, announced in January they’d arrested a 21-year-old Swede thought to be one of the groups main recruiters.



But Foxtrot’s leader Majid remains a fugitive in Iran – meaning another plot on UK soil is still possible.

Salihu added: “It could happen again (in the UK) – these children are also taking jobs from other gangs and Foxtrot are collaborating with other organisations. They want to send fear to their enemies, wherever they are, so they know they can reach them.

“As long as they have criminal networks with global reach, they can always use them on companies, embassies or their enemies.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Bleksley warned that tracking lone teenage assassins will continue to be a headache for UK police and security forces.

He added: “They’re lone wolfs being recruited by a central network, and it’s so often these lone wolfs which slip through the net, so it’s very difficult for law enforcement.



“Someone like Natland only has to be lucky once. It’s going to hoover up a lot of resources from crime agencies and security services in looking for them.”

News.title: Rolex rippers who robbed fashion designer to A-list stars of his £170k Richard Mille watch in central London are jailed
News.content:
Next

ROLEX rippers who robbed a fashion designer of his £170k Richard Mille watch outside a Mayfair restaurant are jailed.

Catalin Botezatu fought back when he was attacked by Ali Eldahouzze, 22, and Abdel El Habchi, 30.



A third assailant, Younes Djoudi, 34, then cut the diamond and crystal Richard Mille timepiece from his wrist.

Botezatu – who worked for Versace – said he was afraid for his life when the thieves struck.



He was smoking outside the restaurant with his friend on January 28 when he was attacked.

Botezatu had recently had a major cancer surgery on his heart where stents had to be put into his arteries.

He was on a visit to London when he was robbed and said he never wants to come back.

Speaking in court prosecutor Arizuna Asante said: “At the time of the robbery he felt alarmed and stressed.



“Even the softest of punches could have put his life in danger…This was a terrifying ordeal for him.”

Eldahouzze and El Habchi, both aided by Arabic interpreters, denied robbery but were convicted by the jury while Djoudi earlier admitted the charge.

Passing sentence, Judge Dafna Spiro said: “You each fall to be sentenced for a single offence of robbery of a high-value watch committed on 28 January 2026 in Berkeley Square, Mayfair. The victim was a prominent fashion designer, Catalin Botezatu.

“This was a serious offence. It was planned and premeditated. The involvement of all three defendants continued after the robbery.

“They reunited a couple of hours later in Slough, then travelled together to a block of flats in North London where they remained for some hours.



“The victim was approached and overpowered by all three defendants. He was forced into railings, restrained and deprived of his watch by the use of violence. A sharp implement was used during the robbery, causing injury to him.

“The victim was fearful for his life, he had cancer surgery and stents put in his heart, he was terrified that he would be caused serious harm.

“It is a constant shame and blight on our city that robberies like these occur and it’s unsurprising that Mr Botezatu has been deterred from returning as a result.



“I find that Djoudi played a leading role in the commission of the offence. He brought the others to the area, was the first to target the victim and was the individual who removed the watch from the victim’s wrist.”

“For each of you, only an immediate custodial sentence can properly reflect the seriousness of this offending.”

Djoudi was jailed for five years and nine months, El Habchi got five years and six months and Ali Eldahouzze was given three years and six months.

The prosecutor said: “Djoudi has an active deportation order and has no right to remain in the UK.

“A foreign national is liable to deportation if a sentence of more than 12 months custody is imposed.”



El Habchi has indefinite leave to remain and is married to a British woman, and Eldahouzze has leave to remain until 2028 and arrived in the UK as an unaccompanied asylum seeking child.

Botezatu’s limited edition diamond-encrusted watch was worth £170,000 more than a decade ago and the timepiece could now be worth considerably more.

Prosecutor Asante said the watch has never been recovered.

The timepiece reportedly had a high sentimental value as Botezatu was given it by a friend who has since died.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Botezatu studied under Gianni Versace before launching his own fashion label Delphi back in Bucharest, and has featured at Paris, New York and Milan fashion week.



He also hosted the Romanian version of Next Top Model from 2011 to 2012.

News.title: Twisted couple who ‘beat daughter, 9, to death’ said she was hit by a car – as they are probed for girl’s sexual abuse
News.content:
EVIL PARENTS Twisted couple who ‘beat daughter, 9, to death’ said she was hit by a car – as they are probed for girl’s sexual abuse







Next

A TWISTED couple accused of beating their nine-year-old daughter to death claimed she was hit by a car as cops probe sexual abuse allegations.

Mum India Miller, 27, and stepdad Sean Scott, 45, are accused of murdering little Maya Thomas, whose battered body was found covered in bruises and horrific injuries.



Investigators are now probing claims the youngster was also sexually abused.

Maya’s devastated grandmother claims the couple had even pulled her out of school to hide the telltale signs of abuse.



The horror unfolded in Paulsboro, New Jersey, when the pair called 911 at around 1.10am on October 13, claiming Maya had been struck by a passing car.

Scott initially told cops the youngster had been walking the family dog when she was apparently mown down by a vehicle.

Miller claimed she heard a screeching noise outside before her daughter was discovered near a shed on their property.

But the couple’s chilling account quickly began to unravel when officers arrived to find Maya unresponsive inside the family home.

Her face was badly injured, while extensive bruising covered her tiny body.

Medics rushed the critically injured youngster to Cooper Hospital, where she tragically died at around 6.45pm.



Investigators swiftly cast doubt on the couple’s hit-and-run story after determining her horrific injuries were inconsistent with being struck by a vehicle.

Surveillance footage from nearby public buildings also failed to show any cars travelling through the area at the time of the supposed collision.

And the couple’s account suffered another devastating blow when Maya’s four-year-old sibling was questioned by detectives.



According to court documents, the youngster told cops Scott had struck Maya in her eyes and face.

The child also claimed the nine-year-old had been hit by a Paulsboro police car.

As detectives combed through the family’s home, they made a series of grim discoveries.

Wet and bloodied children’s clothing was allegedly found inside a bathtub in an upstairs bathroom.

Investigators also discovered suspected blood on the surrounding tiles, a Swiffer WetJet mop and other cleaning supplies.



The disturbing evidence formed part of the murder investigation that saw both adults hauled into custody.

New Jersey’s Division of Child Protection and Permanency has since confirmed it is investigating allegations of both physical and sexual abuse.

The agency was alerted to the suspected abuse on Tuesday after the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office contacted the state’s Child Abuse Hotline.

Meanwhile, Maya’s heartbroken grandmother has made a chilling claim about why the little girl was being taught at home.

Lynn Miller said Maya was homeschooled “because they didn’t want anybody to see the bruises”.



The grieving grandmother revealed she had raised Maya in Las Vegas from the age of 18 months until she was seven.

But the youngster later moved to New Jersey to live with her mum and stepdad.

Lynn said her daughter severed contact around two years ago, leaving her unable to speak regularly with her beloved granddaughter.

Remembering the little girl before the tragedy, she said: “She was a happy, carefree girl.”

Miller and Scott have both been charged with murder, endangering the welfare of a child, abuse or neglect, filing a false police report and hindering prosecution.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair remain behind bars at Salem County jail and are due to appear before a judge on Tuesday.

Maya’s four-year-old sibling has meanwhile been placed in the care of child protection authorities as the investigation continues.

News.title: Man, 39, charged with murder after man in his 40s found dead in caravan at UK holiday park
News.content:
CARAVAN 'MURDER' Man, 39, charged with murder after man in his 40s found dead in caravan at UK holiday park







Next

A MAN has been charged with murder after a man was found dead at a caravan park.

The victim, in his 40s, was discovered fatally injured at Valley Farm Holiday Park in Clacton, Essex, on Wednesday night.

Daniel Fox, 39, has now been charged in connection with the alleged murder.

He’s also been charged with three counts of assaulting an emergency worker, two counts of making threats to kill, and one count of burglary.





The suspected killer is due to appear at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court on October 17.

Detective Inspector Tim Coyles, who’s leading the investigation, said: “Specialist officers continue to support the victim’s family.

“I want to thank my team for their work enabling us to get to this stage swiftly.

“I know this is incident has caused a great deal of shock within the community around the holiday park and I want to thank the public for their support and understanding.”



Essex Police have urged anyone with information relating to the incident to contact them immediately.

News.title: Brit tourist, 25, dies after suffering seizure and collapsing in front of parents during family holiday on Greek island
News.content:
TRAGIC END Brit tourist, 25, dies after suffering seizure and collapsing in front of parents during family holiday on Greek island







Next

A BRITISH tourist has tragically died after suffering an epileptic seizure while on holiday with his parents in Greece.

The 25-year-old man, from Manchester, collapsed at his holiday accommodation on the popular island of Kefalonia on Friday.

His horrified parents desperately tried to save him after he suffered a seizure and lost consciousness at around 5pm.

An ambulance was immediately called to the property in Lourda, in the south of the island.





But despite his parents’ frantic efforts to administer first aid, the young man could not be saved.

Emergency crews arrived at around 5.30pm, but the Brit was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

The holidaymaker reportedly had existing health problems, including a genetic condition, and had additional needs.

He had been staying at the tourist accommodation with his parents when the tragedy struck on October 16.



It comes just after another Brit tourist died after collapsing on a Greek beach during a holiday with his wife.

The 67-year-old man reportedly felt unwell during an outing to the beach of Lourdas, in Kefalonia last week.

His wife rushed to help him after he suddenly collapsed before paramedics arrived and took him to the General Hospital of Kefalonia.

But the man was tragically pronounced dead.



The man was suffering serious health problems related to his heart, local reports said.

An autopsy report has been ordered to determine the exact circumstances of the tourists death.

News.title: Three men jailed for over 158 years EACH over murder of tourist brothers and pal on Mexico surf trip
News.content:
Next

THREE men have been sentenced to more than 158 years in prison each for the grim murders of two Australian brothers and their friend.

Jake Robinson, 33, Callum Robinson, 30, were shot dead alongside their American pal Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, in a botched 2024 robbery.



The trio from San Diego, California, had travelled to the Mexican state of Baja California on a surfing trip when tragedy struck.

Three Mexican defendants, Jesus Gerardo Garcia, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus, were found guilty of homicide on Friday.



They were also convicted of aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence during the trial.

Speaking outside court, Jake and Callum’s parents Martin and Debra Robinson paid tribute to their sons and his friend.

Martin said the verdict marked a “significant moment” in a “long and painful journey to seek justice”.

A huge search and rescue operation was launched after the tourists were reported missing in April 2024.



They had been camping in a remote beachside area near the northern city of Ensenada when they disappeared.

Debra alerted authorities after her sons failed to show up to their Airbnb and contact cut off abruptly.

A week later their bodies were found in a 50ft clifftop well at Punta San José in Santo Tomás with gunshot wounds to their heads.

Shell casings were also found at the campsite where the three men were last seen.

And the white pick up truck they were travelling in was found burned, several kilometres away.



The deaths of the trio shocked Mexico and sparked an outpouring of grief and indignation in Australia and the United States.

Baja California is notoriously violent, with high rates of killings and broad-daylight shootouts driven by cartel turf wars.

During a separate trial last year the former girlfriend of the alleged ringleader was found guilty of crimes related to “violent robbery”.



Ary Gisell Silva was sentenced to 20 years in prison following her conviction.

Silva admitted she instigated and participated in the robbery of the tourists’ belongings, which resulted in their murder.

According to the prosecution, the attackers “intentionally surprised the surfers and shot them with firearms”.

The judge ruled the three Mexican defendants acted with premeditation.

Page Rhoad, Jack’s mother, said “there will never be justice for the loss of a child, but these men will never hurt anyone else again”, after the sentencing.



Callum, a talented lacrosse player, had moved from Australia to the United States to pursue his dreams.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His college lacrosse team from Stevenson University paid tribute to their “dear friend and teammate” after his death was announced.

In a statement they said: “From his days leading us to victory on the field to his unwavering commitment to academic excellence, Callum was a true inspiration to us all.”

News.title: Aberfan disaster survivor haunted after being 'buried alive with dead classmate victim on his shoulder'
News.content:
It might have been nearly 60 years ago, but Jeff Edwards can still picture his dead classmate. She was killed when a coal tip collapsed on a Welsh mining village, engulfing a school and houses.

In total, 144 lives were lost in Aberfan, including 116 children, making it one of Britain’s worst industrial disasters. Instead of searching for coal, a community found itself digging for life. Only eight at the time, Jeff was the last child rescued alive.

With the King visiting next week to mark the 60th anniversary, Jeff recalls the moment his village was ripped apart by tragedy. Class 2A of Pantglas Junior School was having its last day before half-term when death arrived on the morning of October 21, 1966.

To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 7 Images Jeff told the Mirror: 'The only reason I survived was that I had a pocket of air around me which enabled me to breathe.' (Image: Philip Coburn)

King and Prince William to make emotional visit to remember Aberfan victims 60 years on READ MORE :

“There was a sort of rumbling noise,” says Jeff, 68, who lives hundreds of yards from where the school once stood. “And that rumbling noise got louder and louder. The ground started to shake, and the teacher said to us, ‘Don’t worry, it’s only thunder’. The next thing I remember was waking up with all this material over me.

"My right leg was under a radiator with hot water coming out on it. On my left shoulder was a dead girl and I couldn’t get away from her because I was stuck, the desk was against my stomach... The only reason I survived was that I had a pocket of air around me which enabled me to breathe. The majority of children who died in the disaster either died of physical trauma as a result of the tip material or the roof collapsing, or they died of asphyxiation, they were buried and smothered.”

Jeff’s striking blond hair was spotted during the rescue and he was saved. A powerful black-and-white image shows him being carried, wrapped in a blanket. We visited the site of the disaster with Jeff, where a memorial garden marks those who lost their lives.

‌



View 7 Images In total, 144 lives were lost in Aberfan, including 116 children, making it one of Britain’s worst industrial disasters (Image: Daily Mirror)

Jeff sustained injuries to his head and stomach, but it was the psychological pain that hurt him most. He explains: “The effect on you of seeing the scenes that you’d seen as a young child, particularly the girl on my shoulder, would give me constant nightmares. Any noise, particularly thunder, would make me extremely frightened. I didn’t want to go to school because I was afraid that the tip would come down again. I used to wet the bed because of the anxiety that I felt and the nervousness that I had.”

Recalling the dead girl on his shoulder, Jeff says: “As time went on, her skin became very puffy. Her eyes started to sink into her head. I used to see that continuously, practically on a daily basis, and have nightmares about that.” Asked if he can still picture her, Jeff replies: “I can see her now.”

View 7 Images Little Jeff, aged eight, being carried on the day of the disaster (Image: Western Mail)

‌



He adds: “Obviously that caused the nightmares, it caused the depression. You just learn to live with that. You develop mechanisms that you can cope with the anxiety and stress that you face as a result of seeing that.” Jeff led Merthyr Tydfil County Council for four years and has been an influential community figure for decades.

He was made an OBE for his services to fellow survivors of disasters and to charity. Earlier this year, it was presented to him by the King, whose mother visited Aberfan after the tragedy. But the late Queen had faced criticism for taking eight days to go to the village, in south Wales. Her reaction to the disaster – featured in an episode of Netflix drama The Crown – was said to be one of the biggest regrets of her reign.

'I was buried alive with my dead friend's head on my shoulder'

Aberfan disaster survivor recalls the moment tragedy struck

Another in Jeff’s class who survived was Gerald Kirwan, a dad-of-two who has five grandchildren. Speaking from his Aberfan home, he says: “My first best friend didn’t come to school so my second-best friend was sitting behind and he asked the teacher, could he come and sit next to me. The next thing I could hear a noise, like a rumbling and it got louder. How I can describe it is like a jet aeroplane.

‌



“A black mass just came, you could see it coming through the windows. I must have got knocked out because I had been shoved from the middle of the class against the back wall. I was buried up to my chest. [A girl] was on top of me. My little friend, his little head was... on my shoulder. I was speaking to him, ‘Are you OK? Are you OK?’

View 7 Images Gerald says: 'I’ve got grandchildren, I’ve got kids. I can’t imagine what happened to me happening to any one of them.' (Image: Philip Coburn)

“There was blood running down from his nose and from the corner of his mouth, a frothy blood... he didn’t talk.” He was dead, Gerald says.

The now defunct state-owned National Coal Board was found responsible for the tragedy. A tribunal concluded: “The Aberfan Disaster is a terrifying tale of bungling ineptitude by many men charged with tasks for which they were totally unfitted, of failure to heed clear warnings, and of total lack of direction from above.”

‌



Gerald, who miraculously escaped serious injury, went on to work a number of jobs including at the colliery. He says: “I’ve got grandchildren, I’ve got kids. I can’t imagine what happened to me happening to any one of them. I’d be shouting from the top of the mountains about it.”

'All my life I've told my story'

Gaynor Madgwick, who spent 12 weeks in hospital, was the girl on top of Gerald. She survived but her brother and sister both died. The 68-year-old retired charity worker, who lives in Merthyr Tydfil, wrote a book about Aberfan. She says: “All my life I’ve told my story.”

View 7 Images Retired charity worker Gaynor wrote a book about Aberfan (Image: Philip Coburn)

Mum-of-three Gaynor has six grandchildren – the youngest is eight, the same age she was on the day of the tragedy. Speaking at the memorial garden, Gaynor explains: “She’s been here. She knows everything about what happened to her grandma.”

‌



'I was laid with deceased bodies until someone thought they saw me move'

Another pupil in the class, David Davies, was mistakenly placed with the dead. He says: “I was buried immediately and, fairly quickly, from something falling from the ceiling I was rendered unconscious. When I was brought out I was laid with the deceased bodies, covered in a blanket until someone thought they saw my foot move. So I was re-examined by a doctor, obviously I was still alive and so I was taken off to hospital.”

View 7 Images David was mistakenly placed with the dead after disaster struck (Image: Philip Coburn)

David suffered “fairly serious injuries, mainly head injuries”, he says. The 68-year-old, who went on to study at Cambridge and work as a lawyer, lives in the village today and chairs the Aberfan Memorial Charity. In 2023, he showed the Prince and Princess of Wales the memorial garden.

Next week, the King will be joined on his visit with the Queen and Prince William. David says: “Obviously it was an awful thing, but I think it’s far more than that.

‌



View 7 Images David with the Prince and Princess of Wales in 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

It’s really about the resilience, the fortitude and the community coming together as it did in the years after 1966. It’s not untypical of Welsh valleys communities, even today. If there’s a need to come together collectively to do something positive, that’s what we do. It’s in our blood, really.”

For Jeff, it is vital to continue telling the story of Aberfan. He says: “It’s important that we keep the memory alive because of the tragedy that happened, the loss that it made. That sacrifice that was made should not be in vain, it should be there to help others.”

News.title: Woman, 22, died of head injury after skydiving accident - inquest hears
News.content:
Woman, 22, died of head injury after skydiving accident - inquest hears

The experienced skydiver was found in a field and pronounced dead

View 2 Images Madeleine Trask

A 22-year-old woman died from a head injury after a skydiving accident, an inquest has heard. Madeleine Trask died after the incident at Langar Airfield on July 5, which saw police, firefighters and paramedics called to the scene.

‌



The experienced skydiver was found in a nearby field and pronounced dead. An inquest into her death opened at Nottingham Coroner’s Court, hearing that a provisional cause of death has been given as a head injury.

The hearing has now been adjourned, with a date for the full inquest yet to be set. Following Madeleine’s death, a statement released by Skydive Langar said: “We are deeply saddened to confirm that a fatal incident occurred at our centre today involving an experienced skydiver.

View 2 Images The incident happened during a skydive

“The entire team at Skydive Langar is devastated by this tragic loss. Our immediate thoughts, deepest condolences, and full support are with the skydivers family, friends, and everyone within our close knit community who has been affected at this incredibly difficult time.

British Skydiving - the national governing body for the activity in Great Britain and Northern Ireland - subsequently confirmed that a board of inquiry would be convened to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death.

The body said: “We recognise that incidents such as this can have a profound impact on those involved, those who witnessed the event, and the wider skydiving community.”

According to Madeleine’s LinkedIn profile, she started work in the café at Skydive Langar in May 2023 before working as a parachute packer from summer 2025 onwards.

News.title: 'I pretended to be related to Fred and Rose West to deter my school bullies'
News.content:
'I pretended to be related to Fred and Rose West to deter my school bullies'

Charlotte West used to be teased on the playground for sharing the same surname as serial killers Fred and Rose West but one day she used it to her advantage

View 4 Images Fred and Rose West (Image: PA)

Notorious serial killer Rose West is reportedly “on her last legs” inside high-security prison HMP New Hall in West Yorkshire.

‌



‌



The increasingly frail 72-year-old has spent 31 years behind bars after being caged in 1995 for helping husband Fred commit at least nine murders at their home in Gloucester between 1967 and 1987. A source told The Sun the killer was in a “really bad way” and can “barely move”.

‌



They added: “The fact she has this PEEP in place shows what a poor state her health is in. Having a PEEP is extremely rare and officers only use them for those in the most danger if there is an emergency.”

‌



A PEEP relates to plans for prison staff who supervise inmates with health issues or disabilities that could impact their ability to evacuate in case of an emergency like a fire. The source continued: “And people have been talking about how West is on her last legs and does not have long left because of her health. She cannot leave her wing and is also resigned to dying in jail.”

Given the heinous crimes of Rose and her husband Fred, it’s no surprise that many would not want to be associated with them, but this was not always the case for Charlotte West, who used to be a playground target because of her infamous surname.

View 4 Images Charlotte West was targeted in school because of her infamous surname (Image: Charlotte West)

‌



School pals often teased her and asked how many bodies were in her garden and by her own admission, she also looked like Wednesday Addams, something which she was already picked on for before the House of Horrors hit the news.

But after months of relentless mocking, Charlotte stunned her primary school classmates when she pretended Fred West was her uncle. All of a sudden, the bullying stopped and she started to walk to class with a swagger. But in January 1995, Charlotte's dark joke escalated when Fred took his own life before he could face trial for killing 12 people.

View 4 Images Charlotte was called Wednesday Addams in school (Image: Charlotte West)

‌



Speaking to this reporter back in 2022, Charlotte told the Daily Star: “Kids used to say, ‘Ugh, you are related to Fred West’ and they would say, ‘Oh I wouldn’t go to your house for a barbecue’. They also asked how many bodies were in my back garden and they called me Fred when we played chase or sometimes Heather [the couple's first victim]. It didn’t bother me but after a while I got annoyed because it was constant.”

Charlotte, who was only seven at the time, was assured by her family that she was not related to the evil couple. But one day in class she decided to tell a lie to get the other kids to back off.

She remembered: “I was sitting in class and this boy came along and she said, ‘Oh Fred, can I borrow a rubber?’ He then asked if I really was related to Fred and I turned around and said, ‘Yes, he’s my uncle’. I said it without smiling and looked him dead in the eye and he took a step back and everyone fell silent. They didn’t mention Fred again until he died.”

‌



View 4 Images Serial killer Fred West was found hanged in his cell on January 1, 1995 (Image: PA)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google, make us your preferred source. Free and easy to do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

And from that memorable moment, everything changed. Charlotte, now a mum who works in a hardware store, said: “I’m glad I said it because it put a stop to it. It made me feel… not powerful but I kind of became a little bit smug and I came in with a bit of a gangster’s walk and with a bit of an attitude.”

Article continues below

But Charlotte panicked when Fred West then took his own life from his cell at HMP Birmingham. She recalled: “I heard the news over the Christmas holidays and I remember thinking, ‘Oh my god’ because I knew it was going to be mentioned in school. I got to school and people were like, ‘I’m so sorry about your uncle’ and I felt like I had to keep it up. I was like, ‘Thanks so much, difficult time’ and I felt really awkward having to pretend to mourn a serial killer.”

Charlotte eventually moved out of Somerset to settle in Ireland with her family. And although people don’t bring up her surname as much, it remains a topic of conversation. She laughed: “I will still get some who give a ‘Ooooh’ when I say my full name and I think ‘here we go again’. I’ve had this for 30 years.”

News.title: Oregon female teacher fought school shooter and tried to grab his gun after four killed
News.content:
Oregon female teacher fought school shooter and tried to grab his gun after four killed

A 16-year-old armed with a shotgun opened fire on a special education class at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, killing three pupils and a teacher before another teacher and a parent stopped him

View 2 Images Community members at a makeshift memorial in front of Silver Rail Elementary School on Friday (Image: Getty Images)

A school teacher grappled on the floor with a shotgun-wielding teen who had opened fire on a special educational needs class.

‌



‌



The teen fired as many as 15 rounds in the class at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, in a savage attack that killed three children, aged five to 11, and a teacher. The 16-year-old suspected attacker used to be a student at the school, police said.

‌



His rampage came to an end when the brave teacher threw her mobile phone before tackling the teen to the ground in an attempt to disarm him, it has now emerged.

‌



As the two struggled on the floor of the classroom, a bystander armed with a pistol ran in and shot the attacker. The bystander, a father who had two girls at the school, had been driving past when he saw the suspect firing in the school's car park and then shooting through a window to enter the building.

View 2 Images People grieve at the site of a makeshift memorial (Image: Getty Images)

After the attacker was stopped, police found about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition on him.

‌



Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said: "To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude.”

Two of the four victims were identified by cops at a news conference on Friday as five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

Meghan’s family said she was "compassionate and had a huge heart" adding that her goal had been to be a teacher in the district where she’d grown up. "She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," they said.

‌



The grandfather of five-year-old Rhoam Summer, Bryan Jolly, said the family were in a state of shock following his death.

His grandson was " very bright and very mischievous and very fun-loving, and totally without fear,” he told the New York Times, adding: "The whole thing is senseless, and a shock."

An eight-year-old and 11-year-old were also killed in the attack but they have not been named publicly, police said. A 54-year-old teacher and a seven-year-old student are both in hospital with injuries following the shooting. The child’s condition is described as serious but stable.

‌



Police Chief Krantz praised the teacher and parent who stopped the shooter, saying her brave actions grappling with the teen had "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed". Both were unhurt.

The suspect was named by police as 16-year-old Griffin J John II, who had been a special educational needs student at the school. Investigators are searching his home as officers try to find out how he got hold of the gun.

The hero dad who shot him was identified by his family as 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco, a local carpenter. His brother told NBC news how the dad had witnessed the gunman open fire on a vehicle outside the school and then shoot through a window to gain entry.

‌



Mr Giamanco carried a legally concealed .40 calibre firearm in his vehicle and he grabbed his weapon and "and decided to go in after" the suspect, his brother said.

Mr Giamanco’s mother, Kenda Freeman, who lives in California, told CBS news of a “traumatised” phone call her son made to her moments after the incident. "He said 'a man went into my daughter's school'," she said, "And, um, shot kids. And he said, 'and I looked at him point blank, and I shot and killed him, mum'."

"I told him he saved a lot of lives,” she added, “and he said, 'mum, I couldn't save them all'."

Article continues below

US President Donald Trump called Giamanco a "great hero" saying without his actions the shooting could have been "much worse".

"It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said.

Oregon Governor Tina Kotek also praised the heroic dad for stopping further loss of life but added his actions “carry a heavy emotional burden and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well".

News.title: Putin defies Trump as Russia launches massive attack on Ukraine power plants
News.content:
Putin defies Trump as Russia launches massive attack on Ukraine power plants

Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has launched one of its largest attacks on the Ukraine's energy sector since the war began

View 2 Images Putin's forces have attacked Ukrainian power plants (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Russia has launched a massive attack on Ukrainian power plants in yet more evidence that the White House's efforts to negotiate an energy ceasefire between the two nations has failed.

‌



‌



Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said "more than 15 critical power generation and transmission facilities in various regions of Ukraine were targeted" using around 320 drones and missiles.

‌



He said: "Although our troops manage to shoot down a significant portion of them, the sheer scale and relentless nature of the Russian strikes—particularly those targeting the energy sector—unfortunately have many negative consequences."

‌



The attacks, between 7pm yesterday (Friday) and 7am today, come after Trump claimed last weekend that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire". Multiple attacks on energy facilities have followed, with Ukraine launching a major attack on a Russian refinery in Ryazan, south east of Moscow, on Thursday.

View 2 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says his country's energy sector has been targeted again (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Major Pope Leo health update as Vatican issues statement after cancer surgery READ MORE :

Trump has demanded that Zelensky stop attacking Russian oil refineries, claiming it is the cause of a global rise in the price of diesel fuel and calling the Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries a "disgrace".

‌



The latest Russian attack comes after Trump and Zelensky rowed over the US President's controversial decision to waive sanctions and import millions of tonnes of Russian diesel to the US in a £3.3billion deal.

Zelensky fiercely condemned the arrangement, branding it a "weak decision" and a "gift to Vladimir Putin". On Thursday, Trump told US outlet Newsmax he was "not a big fan of Zelensky" and that he was "not a good guy for us to deal with".

"He doesn't want to settle," Trump said. "He says he wants to settle, but he doesn't."

‌



"As you know, Putin hates Zelensky, and Zelensky hates Putin," he added. "And when you have that kind of hatred, it's very hard to get something settled."

Mr Zelensky said the situation, following the latest Russian attacks, was most difficult in Lutsk, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Shepetivka, Slavuta, and Netishyn.

He said: "Restoration work is ongoing, and all necessary services and all available resources from Ukrainian energy companies are involved in the effort. Thank you to everyone who is working practically around the clock to restore power."

Article continues below

The Ukrainian president added: "It's important that everyone in America also sees what's really going on. At a time when the Russians launched such a massive attack on our energy sector, a decision was unfortunately made in the United States to completely ignore the Lindsey Graham Act, which was intended to exert truly effective pressure on Russia to end this war."

The Lindsey Graham Act is the law through which the US imposes sanctions of foreign countries or people.

News.title: UK Beast from the East snow update as weather experts warn El Nino is 'strengthening'
News.content:
UK Beast from the East snow update as weather experts warn El Nino is 'strengthening'

El Niño is 'strengthening rapidly' according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), increasing the chances of the UK being hit by a Beast from the East-type event

View 3 Images The Beast from the East caused chaos in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

El Niño is "strengthening rapidly" just weeks before its anticipated peak in December, according to experts - as the chances of a weather event previously linked to the notorious Beast from the East increase.

‌



‌



El Niño is a climate phenomenon that occurs every two to seven years when temperatures in the tropical eastern Pacific climb 0.5C above average, influencing weather patterns across the globe.

‌



It can heighten the likelihood of cold snaps in late winter in north-west Europe, including the UK. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said in its most recent update that sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific are expected to surge to "record levels" in October, November and December, "reflecting the strengthening of the El Niño event".

‌



Following its peak, El Niño "tends to promote the breakdown of the polar vortex, especially in late winter", according to the US government's NOAA Chemical Sciences Laboratory.

View 3 Images The UK could be hit by a deep freeze (Image: PA)

The weakening of the polar vortex - a band of strong westerly winds surrounding a pool of cold air high in the stratosphere - "may raise the chance of Sudden Stratospheric Warming events, which can increase the potential for cold weather", the Met Office warn

‌



The national weather service previously said that several extreme cold and winter snow events have been linked to the effects of sudden stratospheric warmings, including those in 2009-10 and 2013, as well as the notorious "Beast from the East" in 2018.

The so-called "Big Freeze of 2010", which saw the winter of 2009-10 become the coldest in three decades at the time, also coincided with an El Niño event.

View 3 Images (Image: Met Office)

‌



WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said: "El Niño is firmly established and strengthening rapidly. WMO forecasts indicate a near-100 per cent likelihood that it will persist through February 2027, potentially being one of the strongest since at least 1950."

She explained that the near-certainty figure reflects a consensus amongst 13 national and international centres - from Washington to Tokyo to London to Pune - built on real-time exchange of ocean buoy, satellite and radiosonde data. For October, November and December, the seasonal average sea-surface temperature anomaly is predicted to reach approximately +3.7C, hitting its peak around December.

This would represent the highest figure ever recorded, eclipsing the previous record of +2.6C, which was set between November 2015 and January 2016.

Article continues below

Strong El Niño events are typically associated with a rise in global average temperatures, as additional heat released from the ocean into the atmosphere spreads around the globe, further warming other ocean basins, the Met Office explains. Exceptionally strong El Niño events can therefore play a role in record-breaking global temperatures in the year after they reach their peak.

The current event is unfolding against a backdrop of long-term human-induced climate change, which means its effects are layered on top of an already warming climate, according to the Met Office.

News.title: Katie Zacharia's wildest moments before being fired as Trump's press secretary after just five days
News.content:
Katie Zacharia's wildest moments before being fired as Trump's press secretary after just five days

Zacharia has gone down in history as the shortest-lived press secretary following an especially tumultuous week for the Trump appointee and less than 10 days into the job

View 5 Images Katie Zacharia left her role after just four days (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Katie Zacharia this week broke the record as shortest-lived Donald Trump pick, with the White House press secretary crashing out of her job after fewer than 200 hours - but she still left a packed highlight reel.

‌



‌



The former conservative media contributor and Senior Communications Advisor to Truth Social, Trump's social media company, was inducted into her role on October 12 to replace Trump administration high-flyer Karoline Leavitt, and delivered her first press conference the day after. Just four days later, however, a week after she was confirmed as Ms Leavitt's replacement, she was out of the job.

‌



Her brief rise and fall came after a series of blunders that brought massive scrutiny on her personal and professional life - and ultimately the US president.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Donald Trump halts massive sanctions on Russian goods just days before they take effect READ MORE :

View 5 Images Zacharia confused the president and her husband in her first press conference (Image: Getty Images)

The first conference

Zacharia's first conference came a couple of days into her brief tenure, an unusual move for a brand-new press secretary. Her predecessor, Ms Leavitt, was selected on November 15, 2024, and didn't appear before the White House press pack for several more months until January 28, 2025, eight days after Trump was inaugurated.

‌



That short time showed during her first conference, which the White House billed as a "powerful inaugural briefing", when she made a series of blunders and exited after only 14 minutes. She was notably stilted during the appearance, making a series of unnatural pauses and reading aloud from a binder with monotone delivery.

At one point while speaking about her family, she became the first press secretary to confuse the president for her husband. She said: “The idea of not spending evenings with my kids is completely unacceptable. So my president — excuse me, my husband, that’s a good one — my husband is out here for the week because we have two birthdays in our family and we are very, very protective of celebrating birthdays as a family.”

View 5 Images Zacharia faced several questions about her career following her first conference (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Zacharia then took questions, but spent just eight minutes doing so and failed to answer a key question from Fox News about whether the US was still intelligence sharing with Ukraine. She abruptly exited after saying the president was heading off on Marine One, concluding a very short first session. Press secretaries tend to spend time jostling with members of the press pack, and average briefings would usually last around 45 minutes.

The questions about her career

The immediate aftermath of her first appearance before the press only produced more questions, with Zacharia quizzed by reporters over her work history. Speaking outside the White House while standing nearby the president, Trump was asked by a reporter where she qualified.

They asked: "Where did she pass the bar exam? Which state?" Trump then asked the question himself before Zacharia responded: "When I moved to China."

‌



The answer only raised more questions. Zacharia graduated with a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, meaning she is capable ot practising law, and went on to work in the profession overseas, she said.

But there was some debate as to whether she worked as a lawyer or attorney, with the latter of the two needing to pass the Bar exam before they can offer legal advice or counsel. It has since been reported that she didn't pass the Bar exam, which provides the necessary accreditation to practice law in the US.

View 5 Images Zacharia was quizzed about her law career while standing right next to Trump (Image: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

‌



The Wall Street Journal reported that she sat for the exam in California, but didn't pass, and the New York Times was unable to find any licences to her name anywhere she had lived in the US.

The Hannity interview

Very few things are likely to get key figures in Donald Trump's good graces than an interview with his favourite media personality, Sean Hannity, who is among the president's most vocal supporters. Hannity, a Fox News host, is famous for giving Trump administration members glowing receptions when they appear on his show.

But he didn't follow his usual trend with Zacharia, who received a comparative cold shoulder from the media giant the day before she was fired. She was repeatedly challenged by Hannity, who brazenly called her press briefing "widely panned".

‌



Zacharia tried to defend herself, saying she had “very little prep time” since she was offered the job. She said: “What I feel is I really stepped up and to the plate to do the press conference, Sean, with very little prep time.

View 5 Images Zacharia was ultimately pushed out following a less than glowing interview with Sean Hannity (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Given the fact that I've been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day."

Hannity then thumped back with a grilling of her legal career, saying: "Why not just say, ‘I went to Pepperdine Law School and then took a different career path’? Why get into this long drawn-out thing about the difference between a lawyer and an attorney?"

Trump's final push

News broke that Zacharia left her role on Friday, moments after Trump revealed he had offered her advice about the stresses of the job. He told reporters that she was treated "very badly, very unfairly" following her shaky debut, adding he wanted to leave the decision about her remaining press secretary with her.

Article continues below

He said: "I said to Katie just two minutes ago, I said, Katie, you know, you don't have to do this ... the news has been so nasty to her. I've never seen anything like it. And I said, I said to her honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider. You think about it, but I wouldn't reconsider. She's got a beautiful husband and family ... maybe it's not for her."

She vacated the role the same day, lasting even less time than Anthony Scaramucci, who served in the role for 11 days and left with his name as shorthand for a unit of measurement. Mr Scaramucci himself took to X to comment on her departure, saying: "Records are made to be broken. But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain."

News.title: Strictly's Amy Dowden gives unexpected response to Brendan Cole's brutal criticism of her
News.content:
Strictly's Amy Dowden gives unexpected response to Brendan Cole's brutal criticism of her

EXCLUSIVE: After Former Strictly star Brendan Cole said Amy Dowden was 'not up to the challenge' of being a show pro, she has hit back with grace

View 4 Images Amy Dowden has responded to Brendan Cole's criticism about her (Image: BBC)

Strictly pro Amy Dowden has responded gracefully to Brendan Cole after his disparaging comments about her recent performance on Strictly Come Dancing. Last week, Brendan, who left the show in 2017, said, “To be a pro on Strictly is a big job and one has to be up to the challenge. Amy has not been up to the challenge, in my opinion.” His shock criticism continued with, “I don’t think Amy’s been doing a very good job for the last few years and she’s been out first for the last few years. One can do the maths on that.”

‌



‌



View 4 Images Amy has responded to Brendan's criticism about her

‌



View 4 Images Amy says it is important to be kind

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google, make us your preferred source. Free and easy to do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Brendan also claimed he could see Amy, 36, “counting in” her partners, a sign to him the “job has not been done”.

‌



Amy, who announced she was cancer-free in February 2024, after being diagnosed with stage-three breast cancer the previous year, told the Mirror exactly what she thinks of his remarks. She says, “I’ll be honest, what do you expect from him? It’s fine. I’ve never been brought up to be personal, and in this day and age especially I think it’s so important to be kind, and to think about the next generation. “I always try to use my platform in the right way. I work with various charities. But also I want to be the right kind of role model. I run a dance academy and all my little boys and girls really look up to me. That’s important.” After Brendan’s comments, Amy posted a video on her socials that was praised as “perfect” by fans. Miming the opening line from Mariah Carey’s track Obsessed, Amy can be seen blowing a kiss at the camera and saying, “Why are you so obsessed with me?” “If you know, you know,” her cryptic caption read, along with the hashtag, “In a world where you can be anything, be kind.” Amy’s fellow Strictly pros Aljaž Škorjanec, Dianne Buswell and Kevin Clifton showed their support, while Carlos Gu replied, “Iconic as always”. Amy, who was glowing as she chatted to us at the Women of the Year Awards in London, clearly hasn’t let it get to her. “I’m feeling really happy and healthy,” she beams. “I’m feeling fitter and stronger than I’ve ever been. It’s so special to be here, celebrating such brave, inspirational women.” Amy and her celebrity partner, hairdresser Chris Appleton, were the first to be eliminated in this series. Admitting she’s gutted, she told us, “I was having the best time with Chris. We’re still the best of friends. We were FaceTiming yesterday.”

View 4 Images Amy and her celebrity partner, hairdresser Chris Appleton, were the first to be eliminated in this series

She said the lasting bonds formed are a huge consolation. “Brian Conley MC’d my wedding, Tom Fletcher sang at it. JJ Chalmers wore the kilt he wore for our Viennese waltz on my big day. I spoke to Karim Zeroual yesterday, who I made the final with in 2019. “You share a unique experience together. When you’re in that training room, it’s intense, but it’s amazing. You form friendships for life.”
