Sports.title: Solly March set for surprise EFL transfer two months after Premier League plea
Sports.content:
Solly March set for surprise EFL transfer two months after Premier League plea

Solly March is reportedly set to sign for Charlton Athletic following his summer exit from Brighton.

The winger made 300 appearances and scored 26 goals across a 13-year spell at the Seagulls.

2 March is heading back to the Championship with Charlton months after ending his 13-year stint with Brighton Credit: Getty

March was part of the side that finished as runners-up in the 2016/17 Championship to earn promotion to the Premier League.

Knee injuries blighted the latter years of his time on the south coast, and he has remained a free agent since the window shut.

However, as per various reports, the 32-year-old is heading back to the Championship by signing for Charlton.

The Addicks are 13th in the standings and managed by the animated Nathan Jones, who worked with the player at Brighton.

Jones was assistant to Oscar Garcia and oversaw March's senior debut for the club.

When Sami Hyypia resigned as manager in December 2014, the now-Charlton boss played March on two occasions as Brighton caretaker.

What did March say on his future after Brighton exit?

Throughout his spell at Brighton, March played on both wings and in midfield, and even had a brief spell at left-back.

His versatility played a key role in the club becoming an established Premier League side that now competes in Europe.

However, whilst he has plenty of Championship experience thanks to his 75 appearances in the division, he was keen to stay at the top.

2 March told talkSPORT towards the end of the summer window that he is still capable of playing in the Premier League Credit: Getty

"For me personally, I still want to play in the Premier League," he told talkSPORT in August, whilst also dismissing a move abroad.

"I definitely think I can do that. Maybe I've got to be patient, I don't know. But it's difficult, you get itchy feet, you're at home alone and training alone."

March added: "I can play many positions.

"I think I've got quality that maybe a lot of Premier League teams don't have, and I think the experience helps.

"When you've played 300 games, you know what it's like, and you can help the younger players and advise them.

"I still think I've got the quality... I'm feeling good, the best I have in two years. Just waiting for the right chance, and I think patience is the key."

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola makes eye-opening admission over Liverpool tactics four games into Premier League career
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola has admitted that it is less 'tactical' in the Premier League at Liverpool than at his former club Paris Saint-Germain.

The Frenchman is settling into life at Anfield after a huge £123million transfer from PSG to the Reds on deadline day.



3 Barcola sparked into life in sublime style in midweek Credit: Getty

He is yet to do much in the Premier League with no goals or assists, but the winger is off the mark for the Reds in the Champions League.

Barcola scored a hat-trick for Liverpool in their 6-3 win over LASK to become the first Frenchman in the club's history to do so.

In an interview in French, he discussed life on Merseyside, where he revealed that Andoni Iraola's style is a bit less tactical than Luis Enrique.



Barcola on life in the Premier League

"It's going well," Barcola told Téléfoot. "I was able to meet my teammates; there is a very good coach who has good ideas.

"I'm trying to adapt because it's really very different from PSG."

Asked specifically about the Premier League, he added: "It's different; I find it less tactical, although we had a very, very tactical coach [at PSG].



"But overall, I think it's less tactical; there are less changes on the pitch.

"Whereas with the previous coach, I would have to come inside, or sometimes move out to the flank and then someone else would take my spot. It’s very different now..."



You only have to watch PSG's game against Manchester City in the Champions League to see what Barcola means, and it is in no way intended as a dig at Iraola.

3 Barcola can only gain confidence from that hat-trick scored in the Champions League Credit: Getty

In that match, all of the PSG team were constantly rotating, popping up all over the pitch, and it was very fluid.

With Liverpool, it is a bit more rigid, with Barcola playing almost exclusively on the left so far - both on the team sheet and in-game.



And Enrique is a two-time Champions League-winning manager, while Iraola has earned his role at Liverpool after doing a brilliant job with Bournemouth.

Last season, he got them into the Europa League with a sixth-placed finish, but it had been a steady building process before that, leading to them earning European football with high intensity and aggressive football.

Quality to shine through

Despite the quiet start to life in the Premier League, Rory Jennings feels there is no way that Barcola turns out to be anything like Florian Wirtz - who has been branded the biggest waste of money ever.

3 Wirtz and Barcola showed flashes of a potential partnership against LASK Credit: AFP



Both cost over £100million, but Wirtz is into his second season at Anfield and is yet to show any of the form he displayed at Bayer Leverkusen.

Speaking on Thank Football It's Friday, he said: "He's scored a hat-trick in the Champions League, and you are new to the club.

"I was talking to somebody recently, on-air, and they mentioned Wirtz and Barcola, but you have to separate those two - they are very different.

"Barcola will succeed. He is far too good to fail. He is a remarkable footballer, and The Kop will be soon serenading him with that Maxi Rodriguez song.



"That is going to be happening week in, week out because he's a class act.

"It is going to work for Barcola - he is mustard. I think he's brilliant, mate, I really do. We saw shades of it at Portman Road."

Sports.title: Former Man United star Ander Herrera reveals he is now 'playing for free' after choosing to donate weekly wage to his boyhood club - having cashed in on £53m at Old Trafford and PSG
Sports.content:
Former Man United star Ander Herrera reveals he is now 'playing for free' after choosing to donate weekly wage to his boyhood club - having cashed in on £53m at Old Trafford and PSG

Ex-Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera has revealed he is playing for free at his boyhood club Real Zaragoza.

The 37-year-old who has two caps for the Spanish national team was, until very recently, living out the final years of his storied career in Argentina with Boca Juniors but has now decided to ply his trade in the Spanish third division with Real Zaragoza, in hopes of bringing the historic club back to the big time.

Herrera is reportedly earning £5,500 per week, a far cry from the £150,000 he earned while playing for European giants Paris Saint-Germain. But in an interview with Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand on the former centre-half's YouTube channel, Rio Ferdinand Presents, the Spaniard revealed that every penny of his wage will be going to the club's foundation.

The six-time Copa del Rey and one-time Europa League cup winner said: 'Now in a difficult moment for the club, I think we all, we the fans, we have the responsibility to help the team and the club. And I feel so proud of my career.

'I feel so proud about what I have achieved in terms of football and also in terms of money. So I don't need it. I wanted to play for free. I wanted to help for free.

'At home, my city, where I grew up, and hopefully, as I told you before, helping the club to come back to professional football.'

The Spaniard revealed the motivation behind his decision to return to Real Zaragoza in an interview on Rio Ferdinand Presents source: RioFerdinandPresents/YouTube

Herrera spent five years with Manchester United winning four major trophies but is now hoping to bring his boyhood club back to the professional game

Real Zaragoza, slipped into the third division of Spanish football, officially a semi-professional division, at the end of last season in one of the most shocking declines a big European club has experienced in recent years.

Herrera also stressed the importance of his decision: 'I think we also have to give something back to football, you know, and I wanted to do this because I am not only a professional football player, I am also a football fan and I love what I do.

'And one day, probably soon, when I am retired, I want to feel proud of what I have done during my career.'

Ferdinand took Herrera's candor as an opportunity to pile more criticism onto Manchester United's rivals, Manchester City, saying: 'In a world where Man City have these charges hanging over their head, it's so good to hear about a gesture like this still in the game of football.'

The pair continued to joke about the potential re-attributing of Premier League winners medals following the bombshell Manchester City verdict.

Ferdinand began by saying: 'I'm waiting for my medal as well, so you can have one and I can have another one as well.' Herrera gave a classy response saying: 'I don't know if we deserve the trophy, but for sure they don't deserve to win it.

'If the Premier League want to keep being respected all around the world they have to do something.'

Herrera could potentially be entitled to a Premier League winners medal as he was a key part of Jose Mourinho's 2017-18 Manchester United side that finished second to City, although they were 19 points off the pace.

The one-time Europa League and FA Cup winner with Manchester United did express some sympathy for the Manchester City players during his interview, saying: 'I don't know if you will agree with me but if I was a Man City player I would be angry with my owners, I would be angry with my board, because they have put all that I have done during these years in doubt.'

Sports.title: Chris Woakes reveals how killjoy Ashes hero Ashley Giles stopped England stars celebrating World Cup triumph - and takes aim at ECB for 'bottling' open top bus parade
Sports.content:
Chris Woakes has accused the ECB of ‘bottling’ the chance to project England’s historic World Cup win with an open top bus parade.

In an extract from his autobiography The Wizard, published by The Guardian, the ex England all-rounder lamented the lack of a celebration commensurate with the magnitude of winning a first 50-over title in 2019.

Arguing that it was on a par with the iconic Ashes triumph of 14 years earlier, he wrote: ‘The 2005 team had been given an open-top bus parade through London and I couldn’t help wonder why delivering the first men’s World Cup in England’s history didn’t merit something similar.

‘The country had been transfixed by that final, with a record 15 million viewers tuning in over the course of the match, after Sky had shared the coverage with Channel 4.

‘Fair play to Sky: they’d paid top dollar for those rights and were perfectly entitled to keep the coverage to themselves, but they recognised the greater good and did the sport a huge service. So why did the ECB bottle it?

‘Football clubs get the open-top bus out for League Cup wins and supporters line the streets to see their heroes. We could have done the same, reaching out to thousands more people than we did. It still makes my blood boil to this day.’

The 37-year-old Woakes, who also featured in England’s Twenty20 World Cup-winning side of 2022, recalled the buzz of being able to celebrate the super over victory over New Zealand post match, with friends and family including wife Amie joining him on the Lord’s outfield.

Chris Woakes has hit out at killjoy chiefs who denied England's World Cup heroes of a party

England conquered the world in 2019 but a strict curfew meant they could not enjoy a proper celebration

Celebrations continued with champagne and other drinks in the dressing room, but a block on taking those celebrations into central London’s early hours rankled some of the senior players, according to Woakes.

‘From there, it was back to the Landmark hotel, where a bit of aggro followed. It was around 10pm but our midnight curfew was still in place, making it a bit pointless to go back out in town unless the restriction was lifted,’ he added.

‘Sadly, Ashley Giles, who’d been our director of cricket since the previous year, was having none of it.

‘It felt like the ECB was too worried about what could go wrong. Some of the lads properly kicked off here, not least since Gilo himself had been part of the 2005 celebrations that had become folklore.

‘So, we settled in back at the hotel bar feeling a bit aggrieved; forced to settle for the same surroundings as the night before when a fresh location was the order of the day.

‘A bit like the lack of a parade, it seemed needlessly cautious. We had won a World Cup, for heaven’s sake – if you can’t milk it then, when can you?’

Sports.title: Poppy protest footballer James McClean claims former club 'hung me out to dry' over political stance - and opens up on death threat that left him needing police protection
Sports.content:
Poppy protest footballer James McClean says his former club Sunderland 'hung him out to dry' over his stance.

And he has opened up on the death threat which saw his house guarded by police after he first went against the grain in 2012.

McClean, 37, is remembered in English football for his refusal to wear the poppy because he feels it shows disrespect to people who died during the Troubles in his home nation of Northern Ireland. He also played in the Premier League for five seasons with the Black Cats and West Brom.

His hometown, Londonderry, known to Republicans as Derry, was the scene for the infamous 1972 Bloody Sunday massacre, in which British soldiers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a protest march, with 14 killed.

'Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen,' he told The Guardian.

'It was a very difficult year and I felt a lot of that could have been handled better by the club. But Sunderland came out with a statement before the game which drew all eyes on me. It was there to protect the club. They basically said this is James’s personal decision but we, as a club, wholeheartedly support the poppy appeal.

James McClean says Sunderland 'hung him out to dry' over his poppy protest stance

The star, who was born in Northern Ireland, has always refused to wear the poppy as he feels it shows disrespect to people who died during the Troubles

'I wanted to make my own statement but I was constantly told by the club that: "No, no, it’ll die over. Just leave it."

'I’d just turned 23 and I thought the club had a duty of care to look after me and that’s what they were doing. I’d won the player of the year the previous season but I felt they hung me out to dry.

'The next game was away to Fulham on a Sunday, on Sky. A threat was made that I would be shot if I came on to the pitch. I remember Erin [his wife] panicking. It sounds extreme and people might say: "Oh, wise up, you’re not going to be shot on TV." But the night before the game I was assigned two police officers to stand outside my door. So the Met police took it seriously and that made it more real.'

McClean has followed his stance ever since, despite the intimidations. In 2024, he even stood separately from the Wrexham and Mansfield players as they observed a minute of silence for Remembrance Day.

He has previously stated that if the poppy was only used to memorialise those who died solely in WW1 and WW2 then he would be happy to oblige with the show of respect.

His decision has previously seen McClean suffer torrents of abuse from angry supporters that view his poppy snub as an insult to the memory of armed forces personnel who have lost their lives in combat.

The Republic of Ireland international is a divisive figure in professional football having previously issued calls for a united Ireland, refused to wear a poppy as is tradition in fixtures throughout November and once posed IRA-style in a balaclava in front of his children for a 'school history lesson'.

In September, he clashed with Birmingham City supporters when being substituted and later called a fan at the match a 'smelly fat gammon' after catching a cup of Bovril that had been thrown at him.

He says he would sometimes go 'looking for conflict' during his career - and even suffered from death threats

He is back at hometown club Derry City but is not playing and says they fed him 'b*******'

He admits to the Guardian that sometimes he riles people up deliberately.

'There were days where I went looking for the conflict,' he says.

McClean has been back in the headlines recently after moving to his hometown club Derry City.

Derry attempted to bin off McClean in August – despite signing him in January on a multi-year deal – reportedly claiming he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

He has branded it 'incomprehensible' and a 'dangerous precedent' for the club to try and terminate his deal due to his physical issues.

And he told the Guardian: 'I was meant to be coming home for the fairytale ending. But you quickly realise the promises are just b*******.

'It’s not good. It’s a player against owner and there’s only one winner. I think that’s it in terms of Derry City. You never think you’ll be betrayed by your own so it’s painful.'

Sports.title: How bankruptcy and a painful divorce inspired England rugby World Cup hero's incredible body building journey with physical transformation leaving fans stunned
Sports.content:
Reaching the top of the mountain is one thing, but working out where to go after conquering the summit is quite another.

For Phil Vickery, the pinnacle came in Sydney in 2003, when England were crowned world champions after vanquishing Australia in one of the most thrilling finals in sporting history.

As the final whistle blew, the tight-head prop - who had been substituted at the end of normal time and forced to watch the rest of the nail-biting final from the sidelines - invaded pitch in celebration as Jonny Wilkinson's last-gasp drop goal sealed England's historic victory. It was a moment that would come to define Vickery's glittering rugby career.

And yet, while the roar of that famous triumph would never fade, life after rugby proved a rather different challenge. Bankruptcy, divorce and a loss of the identity left the former England captain facing a battle more daunting than any opposition forward.

Remarkably, bodybuilding would offer Vickery a new sense of purpose. Now competing on the bodybuilding stage, the former prop has undergone a remarkable physical transformation, looking almost unrecognisable from his rugby-playing days.

'Whatever else is going out in the rest of the world is totally irrelevant when you walk through those gym doors,' he told Daily Mail Sport's Nik Simon in 2024. 'I needed a challenge, something outside my comfort zone, and I thought shall I do a bodybuilding show? I was placed third.

Bodybuilding offered England World Cup winner Phil Vickery a new purpose after retirement

The prop reached the summit of world rugby in 2003 before going on to captain his country

'My genetics are c**p, I'm not made to be a bodybuilder, but I loved the process. The pain and the hurt and the suffering to get on stage.

'When you look someone in the eye who has gone through that you think, 'F***ing respect'. It's similar to when I look at another rugby player, 'You're hurt, come here bud, well done'.'

Bodybuilding was far from Vickery's first attempt to forge a new path after retirement. Shortly after hanging up his boots, the former England prop turned his attention to the kitchen, winning the 2011 series of Celebrity Masterchef. The triumph inspired him to pursue a career in the restaurant trade, launching his venture, No. 3, in Cheltenham.

But the business soon encountered difficulties. The Covid-19 pandemic disrupted its planned opening in 2020, forcing the restaurant to initially operate a collection and takeaway service before eventually opening its doors.

Despite later relocating to new premises, No. 3 ultimately ceased trading in January 2024, with Vickery citing the cost-of-living crisis and soaring energy bills among the factors that had devastated trade.

The closure marked another painful setback for the former rugby star, with the financial fallout forming part of a wider period of upheaval that would culminate in personal bankruptcy the following month.

Vickery applied to make himself bankrupt using debtor's petition in February 2024, owing his liquidated management consultancy Vix Limited £97,806.

Sources told the Daily Mail that he had amassed debts of 'hundreds of thousands of pounds' to a lot of contacts and the HMRC, and the company also owed HMRC £71,000 in VAT and PAYE and National Insurance payments.

Alongside the financial turmoil, Vickery was also navigating the breakdown of his marriage, leaving him grappling with both professional and personal challenges simultaneously.

'It's been f***ing difficult,' Vickery candidly told The Good, The Bad and The Rugby podcast in December 2024 . 'The hardest bit is obviously the family side of things.

'I think, like all these things, you make decisions and things happen. Then it's about dealing with the repercussions - and often that's sad, it's difficult, it's hard.

The former rugby star showed off his physique after taking part in his latest competition in Hull

Vickery said his newfound passion for bodybuilding followed his divorce from his wife

'There aren't any winners in it for anybody. Obviously family, my children, and all your associates - your conditional friends and your non-conditional friends - you find out who those are.

'It's been an interesting exercise. It hurts, it's horrible. Honour, integrity - all those things - but it's happened.

'It's very rare that it's business and personal all at the same time. But for me, perhaps they are a bit more linked. It's been hard.'

Vickery's decision to embrace bodybuilding was not an overnight fix, nor did it erase the difficulties he had faced, but it gave him something tangible to work towards at a time when he desperately needed a fresh direction.

Warned of the dangers of alcohol during difficult times, he was determined not to reach for the bottle during what was undoubtedly the toughest period of his life to date.

During his Daily Mail Sport interview in 2024, he explained how bodybuilding became a far healthier alternative: 'Going through divorce, somebody said, "Don't let drink become your friend" and that really spooked me.

'I could quite easily see how I could fall into that, so I consciously stayed away from it. Bodybuilding was a good excuse, that final prep, because you're super clean.

'Covid, the restaurant, bankruptcy, divorce… is it the lowest point of your life? Of course it is. It's your own integrity. It's Phil Vickery; honesty, integrity, passion, pride… but you've failed. You can keep playing a game, telling yourself you'll make it work. In the end, it caught up with me.

'You start to ask yourself the question: "What is the purpose of me being here? Is it easier if I'm not here?"

'There's been scenarios which I've gone through in my head but the more I think about that, regardless of what others think of me, I've got two beautiful kids, an amazing brother and sister, my mum, my aunty, my uncle, my cousins. Selfish isn't the right word but you think, "Come on".'

The former England captain also revealed how deeply he struggled to come to terms with life after rugby, admitting he could not bring himself to attend the 10-year reunion of England's 2003 World Cup-winning squad.

His struggles were also reflected in his physical condition. Following three neck operations, Vickery found it difficult to maintain the training regime that had defined his playing career, while the absence of a clear competitive goal saw his weight steadily increase.

'I really struggled with the gym after rugby because I had always trained with a purpose. Suddenly you get a little bit bigger and a little bit rounder,' he added.

'Another year, another half a stone. Before I knew it, I was 24 stone. A big whopper. You're thinking, "F***ing hell, my knees hurt, my ankles hurt, my shoulders hurt. F***ing hell, Phil, come on".

By 2024, however, Vickery had shed six stone, bringing his weight down to 18 stone. More importantly, he had come to recognise exercise as something that could benefit him beyond the demands of elite competition.

'It took me a long time to understand that I need to go to the gym for my own wellbeing, be it physical health or mental health,' he added.

At his lowest ebb, it offered Vickery (pictured in 2024) a dose of endorphins and escapism

In August, Vickery also revealed he has issues with his memory after being diagnosed with 'probable' chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a brain disease that is usually caused by repeated head impacts.

'The sport’s f***ing amazing,' he told The Observer: 'Rugby’s an amazing sport. You know, the sad reality is I sit here today: would I do it all again? Oh my God, I would. I’m f***ing mental, but I would because it’s amazing.

'I also sit here knowing there are lots of people out there, I believe, who are suffering because of the sport. And it’s not about blaming the sport and about getting all nasty and horrible.

'Let’s just f***ing help people. There are people suffering, so let’s help them.'

Now, at 50, Vickery is thriving in his unlikely second career as a bodybuilder. On Tuesday, he stunned fans by sharing a glimpse of his remarkable physique on social media, posing with a bronzed, chiselled frame following his latest competition in Hull.

On Instagram, Vickery said: 'Your physique is the reflection of your work. It’s not about anyone else for me it’s just you being the best version of you and being better than last time.'

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand embroiled in fat-shaming row after telling Man United influencer to 'pick up your t**s' following Instagram dig
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand embroiled in fat-shaming row after telling Man United influencer to 'pick up your t**s' following Instagram dig

Rio Ferdinand has been branded a 'disgrace' after becoming embroiled in a fat-shaming row with a Manchester United content creator.

The Old Trafford legend told a male influencer, Saeed TV, to 'pick up your t**s' after the fan called on him to criticise the club's ownership.

And the dig has become something of a PR disaster for the 47-year-old, who is now taking a lashing from fans in his own Instagram comments section - though some have sided with him.

Ferdinand had posted a picture of himself with Michael Carrick and quoted the manager, who said: 'It is not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player and anyone else who works at the club.'

It is unclear why he shared this, but it could be a reference to the comments of Lisandro Martinez, who this week hit out at the club's top brass and suggested their squad was too weak in an explosive interview.

But Saeed TV was frustrated at Ferdinand's recent silence towards Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers, commenting: 'Stop yapping and call out the owners!'

Rio Ferdinand is under fire after seemingly fat-shaming a content creator who criticised him

An influencer called Saeed TV had criticised Ferdinand for not being more vocal about the club's ownership

Ferdinand suggested that Saeed was 'out of breath typing' and has sparked a huge reaction

In fairness to Ferdinand, while not as outspoken as the likes of Gary Neville, he has previously criticised the club's ownership on select occasions.

And he hit back: 'Stop yapping and pick up ya t**s, ya out a breath typing!'

Saeed has since shared a response video, saying in one section: 'You are a grown man and this is the response you put on social media.

'You have got kids watching you. You are a role model to so many around the world, and yet this is how you conduct yourself around the world. It's absolutely embarrassing.

'You've got people around you who respect you. What is there to respect when you're speaking like this on social media?

'It doesn't affect me because I've been through a lot on social media and above all, I've been racially abused, so I've got thick skin.

'For me to hold you accountable and for you to resort to that... it tells everything about you.'

He argued that Ferdinand is keeping quiet about United's leadership to retain his access to the club.

The former England defender's jibe has not gone down well on social media, with some followers condemning him.

'Rio Ferdinand is an absolute disgrace. Imagine being SO blind that you have to resort to this type of nonsense,' wrote one fan on X.

'That’s wild man, very very low personal blow from Rio. Uncalled for,' another said.

One said: 'That's poor from Rio.'

However, others felt that Saeed had been unnecessarily provocative after Ferdinand had merely shared a positive post.

'He has told a club legend to stop yapping. Rio is not his friend nor his guy. Respect is given before it is requested,' one said.

'Can’t stand Rio, but if you’re gonna say “stop yapping” to a grown man, he's well within his rights to insult him,' another said.

'He was disrespectful first so got disrespect back,' one commented.

'So Saeed is allowed to go at Rio all the time and he can’t hit back, understood,' another said.

Sports.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle
Sports.content:
Tributes have been paid to ‘funny’, ‘charismatic’ and ‘brilliant team-mate’ Hyron Andrews after the former Sale Sharks lock died of a suspected heart attack in news that has shocked the rugby world.

On Friday morning, French media reported a playing member of the Lions – one of South Africa’s four big domestic teams – had been found unresponsive in a shower at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso Hotel just outside of La Rochelle – the venue where the side is preparing for European Champions Cup game on Saturday which will go ahead as planned.

Just a few hours later, the Lions confirmed the passing of Andrews, 31. Emergency services arrived but were unable to save him and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Andrews only returned to his native South Africa to join the Lions this summer after departing English club side Sale for whom he made 45 appearances. Of those, 19 came for the Sharks last season. Andrews' former club boss, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, said: 'Hyron was just a brilliant guy and team-mate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with.

'He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maiglin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.

'Most importantly, he was a loving husband and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him. It’s just absolutely devastating for everyone.'

Lions player Hyron Andrews, 31, has died of an apparent heart attack in La Rochelle, a day before the two sides were due to meet in the European Champions Cup

Hyron and his wife Maiglin along with one of their sons are pictured here

Confirming Andrews’ passing, the Lions said in a statement: ‘The Lions Rugby Company is deeply saddened by the passing of player Hyron Andrews while on tour with the 10bet Lions ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and Vodacom United Rugby Championship fixtures.

'This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community. The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family and his loss will be felt profoundly by his team-mates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him. Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron’s wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn.’ The Lions have confirmed that their scheduled clash with La Rochelle will go ahead with the team’s players keen to pay tribute to Andrews on the field.

Reports in the French media said a psychological support unit had been set up for the Lions franchise's players and staff, as well as the hotel personnel.

Rudolf Straeuli, Lions chief executive, said: ‘We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season.

'On behalf of our chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to Maiglin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect.’

The Lions added: ‘The Lions Rugby Company will communicate further details regarding an appropriate tribute in due course. In honour of Hyron, the 10bet Lions will fulfil their opening match of the Investec Champions Cup against La Rochelle tomorrow evening South African time. May Hyron rest in peace.’

Andrews' former employers Sale said: 'Everyone at Sale Sharks is devastated to learn of the death of our former player Hyron Andrews. Hyron was a much-loved member of the squad during his time with us and everyone at the club is united in sending their love, thoughts and heartfelt condolences to his wife Maiglin, their beautiful boys and the rest of his family and friends and everyone at Lions Rugby.'

PREM Rugby also said in a statement: 'Everyone at PREM Rugby and our clubs is deeply saddened by the passing of Hyron Andrews and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to his family and friends.

'Our thoughts are also with Hyron’s team-mates past and present, everyone at the Lions and Sale Sharks, and the wider South African rugby community at this very difficult time.'

Hyron Andrews career Andrews spent the majority of his career playing in his native South Africa with the lock having joined the academy of Durban-based the Sharks in 2014. He made his debut for the Sharks in 2016 and made 83 appearances for the team, scoring three tries. Andrews was part of the Sharks side that reached the quarter-finals of the Champions Cup in 2023. The 6’8 lock joined Sale Sharks on an initial short-term deal in the 2023-24 season. He ultimately stayed at the PREM Rugby side for a further two seasons, playing 45 times in total. Andrews left at the end of last season to return to South Africa with the Lions. Internationally, Andrews represented South Africa at the 2015 World Rugby Under 20 Championship in 2015. The junior Springboks were beaten in the semi-finals by England, but won the third place match against France.

Andrews was a former South Africa Under-20 international.

Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union, said: 'This is terrible and distressing news. Our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community.

'There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maiglin and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

'Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

'His untimely passing is a devastating loss and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

'The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maiglin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.'

In a bizarre coincidence, Andrews’ tragic passing occurred on the 10-year anniversary of the death of Munster legend Anthony Foley. A former Munster coach and captain, Foley died in his sleep on October 16, 2016, at the age of 42 in Paris on the eve of a European tie against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.

Ronan O’Gara, the current La Rochelle head coach, was an ex-Munster team-mate of Foley’s. Reports have suggested O’Gara headed to the team hotel of the Lions to offer the team’s grieving players and support staff emotional support. La Rochelle said they had learned of Andrews’ death with ‘immense sadness.’ They added: ‘The club extends its deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates, staff and the entire Lions family.

South African star Andrews played for Sale in England before leaving at the end of last season

‘To honour the memory of their team-mate and out of respect for La Rochelle and its fans, the Lions players and staff have decided, despite the circumstances, to play the match.

‘A minute's silence will be observed before kick-off. La Rochelle invites its supporters to join in this moment of reflection with the utmost respect.

‘La Rochelle remains by the side of the Lions in this ordeal.’

European Rugby organisers said: ‘It is with deep sadness that EPCR has learned of the tragic passing of 10bet Lions player Hyron Andrews while on tour ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and URC fixtures.’

The organisation’s chairman, Dominic McKay, said: ‘The thoughts of everyone at EPCR and the wider international rugby community are with Hyron’s wife Maiglin, his young sons, wider family, friends, team-mates, the 10bet Lions and all those who knew and loved him at this incredibly difficult time.’ In memory of Andrews, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

Those tributes began when Gloucester hosted French giants and current European champions Bordeaux on Friday night.

Sports.title: The fact Man United cannot drop Lisandro Martinez after his outburst just goes to show he was spot on about Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
The fact Man United cannot drop Lisandro Martinez after his outburst just goes to show he was spot on about Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

Lisandro Martinez will be in the Manchester United squad when they face Leeds on Sunday. And of course he will, because he was right about that shambling wreck of a club.

If he was wrong, and United were indeed a functional, intelligent organisation, he wouldn’t be anywhere near the bus for Elland Road. Not after what he said the other night.

A proper recruitment system would have meant there was enough defensive cover to drop a dissenting voice in questionable form. But United don’t have that. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors messed up another transfer window, so kicking Martinez into the long grass wasn’t an option.

In other words, if Jason Wilcox was better at his job then Martinez would have lost his and here’s a little list to support the point: Cristiano Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho, Marcus Rashford.

In the past few years, all of them have spoken out about those above them at United. And with the exception of Rashford, their feet didn’t touch the ground. Straight red. Rashford got put in the freezer for 18 months.

Martinez’s comments were slightly different, of course. He didn’t go after his manager, like Ronaldo and Sancho, and he didn’t turn up late and then flash some leg to potential suitors, like Rashford.

But he did sing a similar song by tearing strips off the regime in public. That used to be a hard no-no at Old Trafford, irrespective of how much truth was in the pudding.

We know that everything Martinez said about Wilcox and the club’s lack of ambition was accurate. We also know that his performance at the microphone was better than anything he has shown on the pitch in quite some time. No one could score points off him for accuracy, only his wisdom in stating the obvious and his reliability as a witness.

Michael Carrick says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's comments after the defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night

Sir Jim Ratcliffe brought in Jason Wilcox from Southampton in 2024

Michael Carrick’s position in all of this is quite interesting. Unlike Wilcox, he has to answer questions about rogue speakers, limited options and poor results and the links between them.

When the Martinez situation was put to him on Friday, he dealt with it the way he used to play, by taking the least fussy option – he managed upwards by not slapping his bosses and he limited his criticisms of Martinez to saying he made a ‘mistake’. Pinned into a tight space, he found a sensible pass.

Carrick couldn’t have done much better in that no-win scenario. But on some level, and in thoughts best kept to himself, he might even wish to thank Martinez. Because who else in-house has pinned United’s difficulties to the lapels of those who are largely responsible for this mess?

It won’t count for much in the long run, as it’s always the manager who carries the can. And some of the flak he has drawn in recent weeks is justified, of course. Same goes for the players.

But it is inconceivable to think Carrick, a smart man, would have supported the thinking behind a summer window in which United prepared for a return to a European workload by signing three midfielders and a back-up goalkeeper.

A window that offered no cover for a left-back in Luke Shaw, who has managed 25-plus Premier League games in four of his 12 seasons at United. A window that left Martinez and Harry Maguire as the first-choice centre-back pairing. A window that marked two years since they last signed a senior defender, the entirety of which has been spent under the watch of Wilcox, the director of directionless football.

Those are the decisions that shape seasons and what we are seeing from United is no surprise. We all called it a mile off. And we can all see Carrick’s points of exposure when Leeds are in the opposite corner.

Wilcox brought in Carlos Baleba from Brighton to complete United's transfer business this summer - he was the third midfielder they signed, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans

In many ways, they are the last thing he needs right now. They are a club that, for a number of reasons, highlight his shortcomings and those of United’s executive tier.

I was at their game against Arsenal and left with three main thoughts – Leeds dominated the champions for an hour, they are brilliantly organised by Daniel Farke and they know the value of a good defender.

Leeds didn’t have a spectacular window, but it was key to the building of a backline that is jointly the best in the Premier League so far. Nico Elvedi has been a good signing and Tarik Muharemovic an exceptional one; between them, they cost roughly the same as Youri Tielemans, with the difference being that Farke had a clear idea of how to use them.

It’s possible that Carrick will crack that code on Sunday – his team are good for attacking moments, if nothing else.

But it is also possible that Elland Road will prove the worst possible place for him to be, because so many of the areas where his side have under-performed are those where Farke has excelled.

A solid, physical midfield, a reliable defence, and a collective that operates with a detailed, well-understood plan has been shown so far this season by only one of the two clubs in the fixtures.

For Carrick, there is some blame to be swallowed there. But only some. The vast majority goes to higher planes, where the responsibility truly lies for United’s problems.

I would doubt Lisandro Martinez’s judgement in designating himself as the man to point it out. But he wasn’t wrong.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
Sports.content:
Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has claimed Manchester City must be deduced "multiple double figures of points" after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Maguire said: "The redacted report sets out year by year how much the sham contracts contributed to the artificial commercial revenue. Over the rolling three-year period, in some years we could be talking about a £350million difference. That would shatter all records for PSR compliance.

"Everton and Nottingham Forest's deductions covered a single breach in a single year, an overspend of no more than £20million. So is there a ceiling on what can be deducted? And the sanctions hearing could already have taken place. Because City are appealing and everyone has NDAs, we might not know the sanction until the appeal result. But it has to be multiple double figures of points, before you start the calculations.

"I worked out that if you add up nine years of Champions League non-participation for individual clubs at an average of £50million a time, around £20million for the Europa League, plus potential claims from players who missed bonuses, the Premier League's legal fees and a fine, we're talking in excess of a billion pounds regardless of the points deduction.

When asked about the possibility of City being kicked out of the Premier League, Maguire responded: "I think it would be a very unusual vote. We did see Bury get expelled from League Two some time ago but I think that the other clubs would have to bear in mind that Manchester City would probably take legal redress and that could prove to be very expensive if they are expelled without the verdict being held and without the appeal. So it's a risky path to tread, but the strength of feeling does vary from club to club.

"Certainly some of the other elite clubs are very unhappy with the delay in the situation because they feel it has an impact upon their ability to qualify for the Champions League. I think some of the more mid-tier clubs who don't see Manchester City as a threat, their main concern is, is this going to further increase the already sky-high legal costs that have been incurred by the Premier League and they don't want any part of it.

"So, they want a quick resolution and then they can get on with the rest of their season and focus on their own clubs."

Sports.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison
Sports.content:
Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison

La Liga president Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid's media output to 'Nazi propaganda' in an extraordinary claim and Los Blancos have furiously hit back

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex)

Real Madrid have demanded the resignation of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he extraordinarily compared the club's media strategy to 'Nazi propaganda'.

‌



‌



Tebas accused selected journalists of promoting the views of senior Real officials, stating they were acting as the club's 'official mouthpiece' portraying Los Blancos as victims of refereeing decisions.

‌



"Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing," Tebas wrote on social media.

‌



"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.

"The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase. Real Madrid TV is a central piece of that machinery. Where is the full match analysis for each round of games?

"Where are the possible errors that harm other clubs or those that favor Real Madrid? If they applied the same magnifying glass to every match, the result might ruin their script. But the script demands that Real Madrid always appear as the victim."

‌



Real responded in a lengthy statement on their website, branding the comparison 'morally repugnant'.

"The repeated conduct of Javier Tebas shows a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," they wrote.

"Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone who occupies two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football should resort to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

‌



View 2 Images Real have hit back furiously (Image: Getty Images)

"His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and regeneration constitute, in the opinion of our club, a real scourge for Spanish football.

"Consequently, Real Madrid CF demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation."

‌



Tebas insists he is unconcerned by Real's latest demand, accusing the club and 'their lapdogs' of trying to destroy La Liga.

He wrote: "I've lost count of the times that, in thirteen years, Real Madrid's leaders have demanded my resignation or tried to disqualify me: complaints to the CSD, directly or through third parties, criminal lawsuits… Today's is just another one.

"What still hasn't arrived are the responses. They confuse neutrality with independence. My position demands independence, not passivity in the face of injustice or silence in the face of the continuous, disproportionate, and insulting attacks from Real Madrid TV and its lapdogs on our competition.

Article continues below

"The La Liga president must defend it. Including against Real Madrid's leaders. My conclusion: they seek to DESTROY the national competition.

"What they haven't achieved so far with the Superliga, they're trying with a distorted narrative from their media and their lapdogs. They call it regeneration while attacking the prestige of the competition they participate in."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua has role to play in Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has role to play in Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch

Fabio Wardley takes on Daniel Dubois again tonight having had Anthony Joshua back in the gym ahead of the heavyweight rematch

View Image Fabio Wardley with Anthony Joshua

Anthony Joshua has handed Fabio Wardley a late boost in his attempt to regain his heavyweight title.

‌



‌



Wardley will challenge Daniel Dubois in London tonight, five months after losing his crown to his fellow Brit. Joshua himself is preparing to take on bitter rival Tyson Fury in December and has opted to re-unite with Wardley's trainer Ben Davison. And the Ipswich man said: "He’s been back in the gym for a good while and it’s been good to see him.

‌



"He has a different energy; a different aura around him once he appears, and that gives the gym a little buzz and a different feel to it. He’s been straight back in the mix and he’s shoulder to shoulder with the boys like you’d expect." Davison was heavily criticised for not throwing in the towel during Wardley's bruising defeat by Dubois in May.

‌

But his charge insists Joshua's decision to return vindicates his own faith in his coach. "The whole conversation around Ben has always been incredibly frustrating," he added. "It’s so strange, because the levels at which people say he’s not done the right job have been at the absolute pinnacle of the sport.

Article continues below

"They’ve been with me, fighting for a world heavyweight title; they’ve been with Moses Itauma, fighting for a world heavyweight title; with AJ, fighting for a world heavyweight title. It’s going to be tough at the top; you might lose, you might win. That’s enough evidence to show that someone like Ben deserves to have someone like AJ.

"As a fighter, you know what works and what doesn’t work for you, especially Joshua – someone who’s bounced around quite a bit between trainers – so the proof’s in the pudding, really. He’s been bouncing around from trainer to trainer to trainer to trainer, and then has left one, went somewhere else, and gone ‘Actually I know where I felt best in myself and where I got the most out of it’. He has left and thought ‘The grass isn’t actually greener’ and come back."

Fabio Wardley and Daniel Dubois look set to deliver another heavyweight barnstomer again tonight.

‌



‌



The British rivals clashed back in May when Wardley dropped Dubois twice in the opening three rounds only to fail to capitalise. He was then badly beaten for eight rounds before the fight was finally stopped in the penultimate session. The pair will renew their rivalry tonight following a packed undercard featuring some of the hottest talent in the country.

‌



There is also a British title fight and the appearance of a double Olympic champion looking to make his own mark in the heavyweight division. Sports.title: Six incredible moments to look forward to in new Man Utd doc after Lisandro Martinez rant
Sports.content:
Amazon Prime's upcoming All Or Nothing docuseries covering Manchester United's 2026/27 season already looks set to become a classic. But not for the reasons Michael Carrick will have wanted as he endures a nightmarish campaign thus far.

Lisandro Martinez shone a spotlight on the club's hierarchy when complaining about a lack of proper investment in the squad. The Argentinian made his explosive comments after Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid and has since been punished for the outburst.

It's but the latest in a steady sequence of disappointing moments at Old Trafford already this season. And the Amazon film crew may end up having its hands full attempting to fit in every pitfall unless United's campaign begins to turn around.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Martinez's rant after Atleti loss

Following United's worst start to a Premier League season in 40 years and losing to Atletico, enough was enough for Martinez. And he just so happened to be speaking to Amazon at the time when he unleashed on his own club.

"Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment," he said in response to the result. "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.

Lisandro Martinez wants to LEAVE Man Utd as reason for bombshell rant becomes clear READ MORE :

The one Man Utd player at centre of Lisandro Martinez row 'revealed' as real reason for outburst emerges READ MORE :

"Today, Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today. I expect more [investment]. 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

The comments caused a cacophony of criticism online, with the likes of Roy Keane and Jamie Carragher calling out the World Cup winner. Martinez has since conceded he spoke out of frustration and was reportedly fined for his remarks.

‌



It's the exact brand of in-fighting that tends to sell so well with viewers when it comes to a series like All Or Nothing. And Amazon had pride of place to catch the meltdown, which summarises this chaotic first portion of the campaign nicely.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Opening-day loss to Hull

In terms of worst-possible starts to a Premier League season, losing your first match to promoted opposition is up there with as bad as it gets. Even after learning Championship play-off winners Hull City have a bit more about them than was perhaps anticipated.

A 2-0 defeat to the Tigers sent alarm bells ringing straight away that Carrick may not be all he was cracked up to be. The club legend earned the permanent head coach job after a hugely positive spell as interim boss, but this was the first sign of chinks in United's armour.

‌



After so much summer build-up about this being a new United, the season started with simply more of the same. Carrick's United responded the following week with a 5-2 thumping of Ipswich, but that opening weekend disappointment is sure to feature prominently.

Transfer window struggles

View 3 Images United strengthened their midfield heavily over the summer but have been left short in multiple other areas (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Coming into the transfer window, there was a sentiment United had numerous flaws in need of addressing despite last term's strong finish. And yet the only notable signings ended up being exclusively in midfield.

That's not to suggest the club's engine room didn't need a little refurbishment itself. Just perhaps not at the expense of literally ever other position in the starting squad.

‌



United's midfield now stands stacked after around £160million was shelled out to sign Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. However, the failure to sign a new left-back as competition for the ageing Luke Shaw may end up looking like a criminal oversight, while Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury has again left them light up top.

Derby defeat

Fast-forward to mid-September when United took on nemeses Manchester City for their first derby of the season. This was before City were found guilty of 114 charges of Premier League financial breaches.

It was Enzo Maresca's men who got the better of Carrick & Co at Old Trafford. That's despite the fact they played three quarters of the game with only 10 men after Phil Foden's red card.

Erling Haaland's decider, which was surrounded by a significant VAR debate, will undoubtedly form a pivotal moment illustrating how United's morale was set back yet again this season. The result of any Manchester derby is a crucial juncture in any campaign, but this felt more meaningful than most.

‌



JJ Gabriel sideshow

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel's efforts to leave United in this first half of the season look certain to form a storyline (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

A constant thorn in United's side as they've attempted to sow something resembling success is the spectre of JJ Gabriel's future. Once the darling of United's academy and tipped as 'the next big thing' to emerge from the club, he's doing all he can to get clear.

It's unknown what kind of footage Amazon will have to provide insight on this particular matter. Gabriel and his team have operated largely in the shadows as he's sought to make a first-team breakthrough, making demands amid his threats to leave.

The storyline of a promising United youth effectively holding the club to ransom couldn't contrast any more with the days when Sir Alex Ferguson was in charge. Expect to see the plot covered in more detail, hopefully with some unseen info from inside both camps.

‌



Tanking vs Tottenham

The latest major disappointment in United's season and the result that cemented the club's worst league start in 40 years. The Red Devils were on the verge of beating 10-man Spurs before Dominic Solanke rose in the dying minutes to draw 1-1 at Old Trafford.

Tottenham were among the clubs bringing up the rear in the Premier League at the time and looked like easy pickings. Not for a United side struggling massively to string Premier League wins together at present.
