Literature faces a similar choice. We can develop sensible rules that protect authorship, reward originality and guard against deception, or we can elevate detection software into an unquestionable authority and allow suspicion to replace judgment.

The purpose of literary gatekeeping should be to protect the integrity of literature, not to preserve particular methods of producing it. Our task is not to keep machines out of the writer’s room. It is to ensure that the human mind remains in charge of what comes out of it.

Osmund Agbo is a medical doctor, author, and the 2026 recipient of the Thabo Mbeki Prize for Scholarship and Public Service

World.title: Ake to Stockholm: Exhibition celebrates 40 years of Soyinka’s Nobel Prize
World.content:
Curator of Timeless Memories: Elastic Effects of Wole Soyinka, Oludamola Adebowale, has unveiled plans for the project’s eighth edition, which will commemorate the 40th anniversary of the Nobel laureate’s Nobel Prize in Literature.

Themed Ake to Stockholm, the 2026 edition will feature an archival exhibition, a documentary film, an illustrated comic book and artistic presentations exploring Soyinka’s literary journey and the significance of his historic achievement.

The programme will form part of the 27th Lagos Book and Art Festival (LABAF), in partnership with the Committee for Relevant Art (CORA). The flagship exhibition is scheduled to run from 16 to 29 November at Kongi’s Harvest Gallery, Freedom Park, Lagos.

Speaking at a press conference to unveil the programme, Mr Adebowale said the initiative goes beyond celebrating Soyinka’s Nobel Prize to examining the experiences, intellectual influences and struggles that shaped his journey to international recognition.

In 1986, Soyinka became the first African writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, marking a historic moment for African literature on the global stage.

According to the curator, the theme traces the journey from Ake, Abeokuta, where Soyinka spent his formative years, to Stockholm, Sweden, where he received the prestigious award.

He said the project seeks to preserve the historical materials and ideas that illuminate Soyinka’s life and work while making them accessible to audiences across generations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Launched in 2019, Timeless Memories: Elastic Effects of Wole Soyinka is an annual curatorial initiative that explores the writer’s life, literary contributions and intellectual legacy through archival research, exhibitions and public engagement.

Exhibition, showcasing archival materials

The exhibition at Freedom Park will feature archival photographs, historical documents, and visual narratives that document Soyinka’s literary journey and the circumstances surrounding his Nobel recognition.

The organisers said the exhibition would encourage visitors to reflect on the relationship between literature, history and cultural memory, as well as the continuing relevance of Soyinka’s ideas on freedom, justice, political responsibility and human dignity.

A short documentary film will also explore the Nobel milestone through archival materials and recorded testimony.

The programme will include an illustrated comic book aimed at younger audiences, presenting Soyinka’s life and literary journey in a format designed to encourage greater engagement with Nigeria’s literary heritage.

Mr Adebowale said the different storytelling formats were intended to make history accessible to new generations while preserving it.

Examining Soyinka’s literary archives

Another major component of the programme is an international panel discussion titled From Nobel to Posterity: Archiving Wole Soyinka’s Literary Legacy.

Hosted by the Section on Literary Archives of the International Council on Archives, the discussion will bring together archivists and scholars to examine how to preserve, document, and make laureate Soyinka’s literary records accessible for future research.

The session will also consider how literary archives shape how future generations understand writers and their contributions to world literature.

The contemporary art programme will feature The Rebel Series (WS in 1986) at Adegbola Gallery. The exhibition, featuring artist Adewale Kolawole John and curated by Adebowale, will offer an artistic interpretation of Soyinka and the period surrounding his Nobel Prize.

Speaking ahead of the programme, Mr Adebowale said the project was intended to preserve the stories and ideas that help explain Soyinka’s place in history.

He added that the collaboration with LABAF and CORA would provide a platform for extending conversations about the writer’s legacy to a wider audience.

The eighth edition comes as Nigeria’s literary community marks four decades since Mr Soyinka’s Nobel Prize, renewing attention to the historical experiences and creative achievements that have shaped African literature.

World.title: No return to fuel subsidy, multiple exchange rates, Oyedele insists
World.content:
Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on Saturday said there will be no reversal of the government’s policies on fuel subsidy removal and foreign exchange market liberalisation.

Mr Oyedele spoke in response to concerns raised in the wake of the debates over subsidy policies ahead of the 2027 elections.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the minister spoke on the sidelines of the World Bank/IMF meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

Nigeria has introduced a series of reforms the government said were focused on fixing the structure of the economy, although the impact has been enormous for many Nigerians grappling with the cost-of-living crisis.

The government introduced reforms in the foreign exchange market, abolished what it termed a wasteful, corruption-ridden subsidy regime amid fiscal pressures, and institutionalised tax reforms.

While the Nigerian government, led by President Bola Tinubu, has defended its economic policy of subsidy removal as critical to the nation’s fiscal survival, opposition politicians—such as Atiku Abubakar of the ADC and Peter Obi of the NDC—have canvassed for and promised a return to different subsidy arrangements if elected into power.

Although the reforms have been hailed as positive for the nation’s fiscal health by global development and financial institutions, many Nigerians have expressed frustrations over their impact on the domestic front amid skyrocketed energy prices, high cost of living and sundry inflationary pressures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oyedele said on Saturday that there will be no return to subsidy regimes, adding that the 30-day retail margin discount isn’t a subsidy arrangement.

“And let me be clear as well, this was a recurring question almost through all our engagements, but also with the rating agencies, with the investors, and the multilateral institutions. Every time they ask, are you reversing your plans? Are you bringing back subsidies? Let me be clear, there will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the government recently announced an intervention by the state-owned oil company, NNPC, that it would sell petrol at the cost price for about 30 days; a move many described as some form of subsidy. The government, however, insists the intervention is not a subsidy.

“The recent 30-day retail margin discount… is a time-bound commercial decision by the NNPC to reduce margins and support Nigerians. It is not a subsidy paid from public funds,” Mr Oyedele said.

World.title: Enugu approves N32 billion to clear gratuity arrears
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has approved the payment of about N32 billion in outstanding legacy gratuities owed to retirees with the first tranche of N10 billion scheduled for release from next week.

The Secretary to the Enugu State Government (SSG), Chidiebere Onyia, disclosed this on Friday while briefing reporters at the Government House, Enugu, after the State Executive Council meeting.

At the briefing were the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Malachy Agbo; Commissioner for Lands and Urban Development, Chimaobi Okorie; and Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Benedett Okoli, a professor.

Mr Onyia, a professor, said the payment was part of the commitment of the Governor Peter Mbah administration to clear the inherited gratuity liabilities before the end of his first tenure.

He explained that the outstanding gratuities were liabilities inherited by the present administration.

The SSG pointed out that the state government had made provisions for the settlement of the gratuities in the 2026 budget, which had been approved by the Enugu State House of Assembly.

“This amount of money was put in the 2026 budget and approved by the Enugu State House of Assembly. So, it is in appropriation law,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The official emphasised that the decision was not a hastily conceived measure but part of a planned process to address the state’s outstanding obligations to retired workers.

According to him, the government suspended the existing gratuity verification process in December 2025 and established a verification committee to review records dating back to 2000.

He said the exercise was designed to establish the actual liabilities by examining retirees’ records and supporting documents, adding that the amount approved by the Executive Council was based on the outcome of the verification.

Mr Onyia said the first N10 billion tranche would be released to commence payments, after which subsequent tranches would follow until the entire verified liability of approximately N32 billion was cleared.

The SSG added that the administration was also addressing gratuity obligations at the local government level, where the outstanding exposure was estimated at more than N10 billion.

He said Governor Mbah had approved a meeting of the Economic Council to review the local government liabilities to enable local government retirees to start receiving their gratuities soon, alongside their counterparts at the state level.

He clarified that the current exercise focused on legacy gratuities, noting that the government had already commenced the payment of outstanding pension obligations following the verification of eligible beneficiaries.

“The gratuity owed to every retiree across the board from 2000 will be paid,” he said.

The official also stated that the verification committee, which he chaired, had reviewed the records of 66,783 persons across the workforce and pension-gratuity categories.

He explained that the verification exercise was necessary to guard against fraudulent claims and ensure that payments were made to legitimate beneficiaries.

READ ALSO: Enugu govt condemns attack on NDC members

He clarified that retirees, who had concerns with the outcome of the verifications were free to submit their complaints to the verification committee for further review.

Mr Onyia said that clearing the inherited gratuity liabilities was an important step towards ensuring that the state did not continue to accumulate unpaid retirement benefits for future administrations.

He reiterated that the Mr Mbah administration was committed to settling the verified legacy obligations while sustaining payments to eligible pensioners and putting in place a more sustainable pension system for the state.

World.title: Top 5 African countries with the most visa-free travel if you own their passport
World.content:
African passports differ significantly in the number of destinations their holders can visit without obtaining a visa before departure, with Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa leading the continent in international travel access.

The Henley Passport Index, which uses data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), ranks passports according to the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa. Its 2026 rankings place Seychelles among Africa’s strongest passports, followed by Mauritius and South Africa.

Based on the 2026 rankings and available passport-mobility data, here are five African countries whose passports offer extensive international travel access.

Seychelles

Seychelles has one of Africa’s most powerful passports, giving its citizens broad access to destinations across the world without securing a visa in advance.

The island nation retained its position as Africa’s leading passport in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, ranking among the top 25 passports globally in the July update. According to the Seychelles News Agency, the passport provided visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 155 destinations at that time.

Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad.

The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries.

Mauritius

Mauritius ranks among Africa’s strongest passports, offering its citizens extensive travel opportunities across several regions.

The country has consistently placed near the top of continental passport rankings, with access to numerous destinations in Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and other parts of the world.

Mauritian citizens benefit from visa-free arrangements and visa-on-arrival facilities in a range of countries, making international travel more convenient for tourism and business.

Its strong passport position also reflects Mauritius’s international engagement and the agreements that facilitate movement between its citizens and other countries.

South Africa

South Africa ranks third among Africa’s strongest passports in the 2026 rankings, providing its citizens with substantial international travel access.

South African passport holders can visit a range of destinations without obtaining a visa beforehand, although entry conditions differ by country.

The passport is particularly useful for regional travel within Africa, while also providing access to destinations in parts of Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean.

Despite its relatively strong position on the continent, South African citizens still require visas for several major destinations, depending on the purpose and length of their visit.

Botswana

Botswana is among the African countries whose passports offer comparatively broad international travel access.

Its passport provides entry to a range of countries without a prior visa, including destinations within Africa and selected countries beyond the continent.

Botswana’s position places it among the leading African passports after Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa in several 2026 passport-mobility comparisons.

For Botswana citizens, these arrangements can reduce the paperwork and planning required for international holidays, visits and some business trips.

Namibia

Namibia rounds out the five African countries with strong passport mobility in several 2026 rankings.

Namibian passport holders enjoy visa-free access to a number of destinations, alongside access to other countries through visa-on-arrival arrangements.

The passport offers opportunities for regional travel in southern Africa and entry to selected destinations elsewhere in the world.

Although Namibia does not provide the same level of access as Seychelles or Mauritius, it remains among the African countries whose citizens enjoy comparatively broad international mobility.

Vanguard News

World.title: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

A former spokesperson to ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande has dismissed claims by Babachir Lawal that former President Muhammadu Buhari considered Osinbajo’s 2023 presidential ambition “highly immoral and distasteful”.

Akande, who served as Osinbajo’s spokesperson from 2015 to 2023, described the allegation as false in a statement on Saturday, saying Buhari had personally offered to support the former vice-president’s ambition on at least four occasions.

Osinbajo contested the All Progressives Congress presidential primary in 2022 but lost to Bola Tinubu, who went on to win the 2023 presidential election.

Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, ADC, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, had alleged in a recent interview that Buhari would have found it difficult to support Osinbajo’s ambition because of his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor.

Reacting, Akande said he had watched the interview in which Lawal made allegations against Osinbajo and chose to respond because he was present when decisions concerning the former vice-president’s office were taken.

He said Buhari had, on at least four separate occasions, personally offered to support Osinbajo, asking him, “If I don’t support you, who will I support?”

“He was consistent. During the APC presidential primaries in 2022, while campaigns were underway, President Buhari openly commended Vice President Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for the dignified, issues-based manner in which he was conducting his campaign across the country. He spoke in a laudatory tone. The entire Council witnessed it.”

“That is not a President who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a President who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” Akande added.

Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022, finishing third with 235 votes, behind now president Bola Tinubu, who won with 1,271 votes, and Rotimi Amaechi, who scored 316.

World.title: Kwara APC: Oba leads peace committee to reconcile aggrieved members
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, OFR, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The group, known as the Kwara APC Peace Committee, held its inaugural meeting at AbdulRaheem’s residence in Ilorin on September 17, according to a statement made available to Vanguard by Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin.

The statement said the committee was committed to resolving disagreements arising from the outcome of the APC primaries and promoting unity among party members.

AbdulRaheem, a former chairman of the Federal Character Commission, chairs the committee.

Other members include Dr Johnson Adewumi, an educationist, entrepreneur and founder of Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former minister and former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to the Kwara State Government and former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo.

The committee also comprises Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and Africa representative on the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and member of the Tinubu-Shettima Presidential Campaign Council, Pastor John Dara; and former Federal Character Commission member, Hon. James Jiya Kolo.

According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections.

The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other candidates of the party in the state.

The statement said the initiative was aimed at securing the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthening cohesion within the APC ahead of the general elections.

World.title: Zelensky says Trump waiving sanctions ‘rewards’ Putin, warns Moscow wants ‘blackout’ in Ukraine
World.content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky (left) attends a meeting with Head of the Security Service of Ukraine, SBU, Oleksandr Poklad in Kyiv, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE / AFP.

Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday that US President Donald Trump’s decision to block Russia sanctions only “rewards” Russia’s Vladimir Putin and warned Moscow was trying to deprive “millions” of Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter.

Amid a clash with the Ukrainian wartime leader, Trump signed an executive order that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues.

The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine — especially its capital, Kyiv – in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions.

Zelensky said the decision came the same day as Russia attacked 15 critical power generation facilities across Ukraine in “one of the largest” attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid.

“It is important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening,” he said on social media.

The Lindsey Graham Act, he said, was “supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end” adding that the act “could have helped enormously — and still can!”.

“A U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin — all of this only encourages him to keep attacking,” he warned.

The Ukrainian leader said Russia wanted to cause a “blackout” in Ukraine ahead of winter: “Russia is trying to leave millions of our people without electricity and heating.”

He called on allies to keep up pressure on Moscow to “stop this.”

Last winter saw hundreds of thousands in Ukraine consistently without heat and electricity in freezing temperatures.

A day after Trump waived the sanctions, causing Europe and Kyiv to worry which side of the war the White House is on, Ukraine said at least two people were killed in Russian air strikes.

Officials said one person was killed in the southern city of Kherson in an attack that also wounded 22 people, including two children, and that another was killed in the northeastern city of Sumy.

– Russia hails Trump move as ‘historic’ –

The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to Trump, but several Russian officials celebrated the move as a win.

“The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, a Putin envoy, said on social media.

Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets”.

Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.

He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of east Ukraine.

US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war.

Zelensky had rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine’s fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump.

– Putin vows more –

Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter.

Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine by force.

“On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings,” Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire.

“Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People’s Republic,” he added, using the Kremlin’s name for the eastern Donetsk region.

European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump.

“This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” said European Council chief Antonio Costa.

“Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.”

World.title: Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV waves from the window of the car as he leaves the Vatican before being admitted to Rome’s Gemelli University Hospital for an operation to remove a lump from his lung, in the Vatican on 13 October 2026. (Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP)

Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital Saturday where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”.

Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour.

“Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican.

The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”.

“He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment,” the Vatican said.

The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square.

But in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms.

The Vatican’s press office said that Leo celebrated mass on Saturday, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital where he has been recovering.

– Up in air –

News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.

But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take.

Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky.

Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

Pope watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors.

Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20.

The pope himself announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed.

World.title: Nigeria commiserates with Saudi Arabia over terrorists’ attacks
World.content:
By Boluwaji Obahopo

‎

‎President Bola Tinubu has conveyed heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Saudi Arabia over the recent numerous attacks on the country by the Houthi militia from Yemen.

‎

‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made this known when he received the Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Nigeria, Yousef bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, in his office during the week.

‎

‎In the letter, President Tinubu strongly condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi militia and commiserated with the Prime Minister, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the government and people of Saudi Arabia on the attacks that have claimed many lives and destroyed physical infrastructure and critical installations in the country.

‎

‎While delivering the letter to the Ambassador, the Minister noted that there was no alternative to peace, urging people in the region to eschew violence.

‎

‎An obviously elated Ambassador Yousef expressed profound appreciation to President Tinubu for his kind words of solidarity, consolation and principled stance of strong condemnation and abhorrence of terrorists and rebel activists against legitimate governments while stressing his unalloyed commitment to regional and international peace and security.

‎

‎The Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communications to the Minister, Mr. Richard Elesho, made this known in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday.

World.title: I’d have left Real Madrid if I were Vinicius, says Mourinho
World.content:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday if he were winger Vinicius Junior he would have left the club this summer.

The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid’s win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss the Clasico clash against Barcelona on October 25.

Vinicius, 26, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018.

“He’s a spectacular kid who it’s easy to have a good relationship with,” Mourinho told reporters.

“He’s a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile…

“If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn’t be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him.”

In the summer Vinicius signed a new contract with Real Madrid until 2032.

Question marks remain over whether Madrid can line up with attacking superstars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham together, without losing balance.

“Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed and he keeps on smiling,” continued Mourinho.

“No one or nobody can… well, influence him negatively yes, because he’s human… but take away his joy of living and working and being with his team-mates, no, no one can do that.”

Mourinho took Vinicius off during the 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to return to the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti.

Mourinho said he was happy that Vinicius’s ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee “would give him one or two more”.

– ‘There are limits’ –

Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday aiming not to fall further behind league leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday.

Hansi Flick’s Barcelona have won every single match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Real Madrid.

Los Blancos and Mourinho have blamed referees for some of their results, including the 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid in September.

On Friday Real Madrid called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with “those propaganda techniques” and not with the ideology of the Nazis.

“I don’t want to talk about this, there are limits and there are limits. You can only excuse it if it’s a clinical case — otherwise there’s no excuse,” said Mourinho.

“I don’t want to go down that road. Madrid and its fans understands what it is up against.

“For the prestige that the league has abroad, for being the current world champions, it’s better if we try to keep this here and not let it get out (to the world).”

World.title: Police rescue one-month-old baby sold for N2m, arrest two suspects
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

The Oyo State Police Command has rescued a one-month-old baby girl allegedly sold for N2 million and arrested two suspects, including the child’s mother and the owner of the health facility where she was delivered.

The incident occurred in Ido Local Government Area of Ibadan, with the police confirming that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other suspects linked to the alleged child trafficking.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, disclosed this on Friday in a statement.

According to the statement, the case was reported on October 15 by Mary Amos, a resident of the Ogunwade area of Ido, who raised concerns over the disappearance of her granddaughter.

The police said the child’s mother, identified as Cecilia, implicated the owner of the health facility, 40-year-old Dr Adeleke Ebenezer, and Hassan Oludunni, whom she alleged lured her into the arrangement and facilitated the sale of the baby to Odunayo Folawewo.

Investigations reportedly revealed that the transaction involved N2 million, out of which Cecilia allegedly received N1 million, while Adeleke and Oludunni received N500,000 each.

The police subsequently rescued the baby girl and arrested Adeleke, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend Folawewo and bring all those allegedly involved in the incident to justice.

The command said it had rescued the baby and reiterated its commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons.

“The Oyo State Police Command reiterates its commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons and urges members of the public to report suspected cases of child trafficking and related offences promptly,” the statement said.

World.title: Abia PDP Gov Candidate Says No Nation Prospers With Hungry Citizens, Unveils Plan to Revive Agriculture
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Abia State for the 2027 election, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has said no country can achieve lasting prosperity when its citizens go to bed hungry.

Anosike stated this on Thursday in Umuahia in a statement to commemorate the 2026 World Food Day, where he paid tribute to farmers in Abia and across the country.

According to him, food is not a luxury but a basic human necessity, and agriculture must be treated not merely as an economic activity but as a strategic instrument for food security, job creation, poverty reduction and wealth generation.

“Food is not a luxury; it is a basic human necessity. No society can achieve lasting prosperity when its people go to bed hungry,” he said.

The PDP candidate, who described himself as a committed welfarist, said government must go beyond rhetoric and provide practical support to farmers through access to affordable inputs, improved seedlings, mechanisation, irrigation, agricultural loans, storage facilities, processing industries and reliable markets.

Unveiling his agenda for the agricultural sector, Anosike said under his welfarist vision, agriculture would become a major driver of economic growth, rural development and youth employment in the state.

He said his administration, if elected, would ensure farmers earn better incomes, traders have access to affordable food supplies and households enjoy food security.

Anosike disclosed that his Operation Feed Abians (OFA) programme, a Back-to-Farm policy is designed to ensure that there is food everywhere and no Abian goes to bed hungry.

He explained that OFA seeks to promote agricultural production, empower farmers, encourage youths to embrace agriculture, strengthen food supply chains and make food more accessible and affordable.

“We will work towards an Abia where farming is profitable, rural communities prosper, agricultural businesses flourish, and no Abian is abandoned to hunger because of poverty,” he added.

The governorship hopeful also saluted farmers, food processors, transporters, traders and all actors in the food value chain for their role in feeding the nation, stressing that a caring government must feed its people and create prosperity from the soil.

World.title: Reps Threaten Arrest Warrant Against Ede Poly Rector, Bursar Over Audit Queries, Contract Irregularities
World.content:
Juliet Akoje in Abuja

The House of Representatives Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has threatened to secure arrest warrants against the Rector of the Federal Polytechnic, Ede, Engr. Sani Man Yahaya, and the institution’s Bursar, Aishat Shade Adebayo, should they fail to appear before the panel on Monday, October 19, 2026, to address outstanding audit queries, alleged procurement irregularities and other concerns relating to financial management.

Chairman of the Committee, Hon. Bamidele Salam, made this known yesterday when the panel adopted the report of its technical committee, which examined submissions by six tertiary institutions in response to audit queries raised by the Office of the Auditor-General for the Federation.

The action followed the Committee’s review of unresolved issues contained in the Federal Polytechnic, Ede’s 2021 Audit Report, findings from its oversight exercise in the South-West geopolitical zone and a petition submitted to the panel.

The lawmakers expressed dissatisfaction with the repeated failure of the Rector and Bursar to honour invitations to appear before the Committee, describing their absence as worrisome given the outstanding audit queries and other matters for which they were expected to provide explanations.

The Committee warned that it would invoke the relevant constitutional and legislative powers of the House of Representatives to secure their arrest and compel their appearance if the Rector, Bursar and other officials concerned failed to attend the scheduled hearing on Monday, October 19, 2026.

It emphasised that the officials must appear before the panel to answer the unresolved audit queries, clarify allegations of financial irregularities and submit relevant documents needed for the ongoing investigations.

The Committee further revealed that an inspection conducted by its team at the institution exposed what it described as poor project execution, with the level of work allegedly carried out on some projects falling short of the amounts already disbursed to contractors.

It also disclosed that several petitions had been received against the institution’s management, raising allegations of different forms of financial misconduct.

According to the Committee, three audit queries relating to the institution’s 2021 financial year remained unresolved.

They concerned an unretired cash advance, the engagement of an external solicitor without approval from the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, and foreign trips undertaken without evidence of authorisation by the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

The panel also faulted the institution for submitting its audited financial statements for the 2022, 2023 and 2024 financial years late, noting that the delay contravened existing regulations and statutory requirements governing financial reporting.

During its South-West oversight exercise, the Committee identified a substantial discrepancy between the institution’s approved overhead budget and its actual expenditure for 2023.

Although N110.2 million was approved for overhead costs for the year, the institution’s audited accounts showed that actual expenditure reached N882.5 million, resulting in excess spending of approximately N772 million.

The Committee also questioned an estimated budgetary slack of N268.5 million in the institution’s personnel expenditure for the same financial year.

Records presented to the panel indicated that the approved personnel budget was N2.862 billion, while actual expenditure stood at N2.593 billion.

The difference raised concerns about whether adequate due diligence was conducted in preparing the institution’s budget estimates.

Another issue identified by the Committee was the absence of documentary evidence showing that the institution had complied with the mandatory remittance of one per cent of personnel emoluments to the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) between 2023 and 2025.

The lawmakers further expressed dissatisfaction with the institution’s failure to provide procurement documents covering capital expenditure and projects funded by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), despite repeated requests by the Committee.

They described the failure to produce the records as an impediment to legislative oversight, stressing that withholding the documents denied the panel access to information necessary to assess procurement activities and enforce accountability in the use of public funds.

During a physical inspection of an ongoing lecture theatre construction project at the institution’s permanent site, members of the Committee reportedly observed construction work they considered substandard.

The inspection team discovered that the concrete flooring leading to the lecture theatre entrance had been poorly executed, with the material reportedly so weak that it could be broken with the hands and feet.

The discovery heightened concerns about the standard of construction and whether the quality of work delivered by the contractor reflected the amount of money already paid for the project.

Following the inspection, the Committee directed the institution to submit the project’s Bill of Quantities, procurement documents and the identity and details of the contractor handling the construction for further scrutiny.

However, the institution failed to provide the requested records.

The panel also raised concerns over N20.5 million reportedly yet to be credited to the Retirement Savings Accounts of some employees of the institution by Stanbic IBTC Pension and Access Pension.

The findings attributed the delay to the institution’s alleged failure to supply the pension fund administrators with accurate employee details, including the Personal Identification Numbers attached to the workers’ Retirement Savings Accounts (RSA PINs).

According to the Committee, the delay could cause the affected employees to lose interest and other investment returns that would have accrued to their retirement savings if the contributions had been credited to their accounts promptly.

Salam reaffirmed the Committee’s determination to promote transparency, accountability and strict compliance with financial regulations in the management of public resources.

He maintained that public institutions must be ready to justify their expenditure, produce requested financial and procurement records, and provide satisfactory explanations for audit queries raised by the relevant authorities.

The Committee further warned that it would not overlook repeated instances of public officials ignoring its invitations, withholding relevant documents or failing to satisfactorily address concerns raised during legislative investigations.

It reiterated that the House of Representatives would deploy its relevant powers, including measures to compel the attendance of the Rector, Bursar and other officials concerned, if they failed to appear before the panel on Monday as directed.

The Committee also stated that the petitions submitted against the institution’s management would be examined alongside the audit findings and other available evidence in line with the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and applicable laws.

World.title: ActionAid: 133m Nigerians Lived in Poverty, Demands Urgent Housing, Social Protection Investment
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

ActionAid Nigeria has called on federal and state governments to urgently increase investment in affordable housing, social protection and economic justice, warning that millions of Nigerians remain trapped in poverty amid food insecurity, inadequate shelter and widening inequality.

The organisation said approximately 133 million Nigerians, representing 63 per cent of the population, were living in multidimensional poverty, according to the National Bureau of Statistics’ 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index.

It added that more recent World Bank estimates indicated that 123 million Nigerians, or 50.8 per cent, lived in extreme monetary poverty in 2025, underscoring the scale of deprivation confronting the country.

ActionAid Nigeria made the call in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja to mark the 2026 International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, observed under the theme, ‘Safe Homes for All,” within the broader 2026–2028 theme, “United for Peace and Human Rights’.

The organisation said the figures reflected different dimensions of poverty but demonstrated the urgent need for effective and inclusive government interventions to improve living conditions.

It also cited a September 2026 assessment by the Food and Agriculture Organisation, which estimated that 36.3 million Nigerians faced crisis-level or worse acute food insecurity during the June to August lean season.

According to the statement, UNICEF reported that about 11 million children under five experienced severe food poverty in 2024, while its 2026 humanitarian assessment estimated that three million children required life-saving treatment for severe wasting.

ActionAid Nigeria said the figures highlighted the combined effects of economic hardship, conflict and inadequate access to nutritious food, particularly among vulnerable households.

The organisation identified housing as another major challenge, citing a 2025 World Bank analytical review which estimated that 87 million Nigerians lived in poor housing conditions, alongside a national housing deficit of approximately 17 million units.

It warned that inadequate shelter further deepened poverty among women, children, persons with disabilities and displaced communities, stressing that access to safe and affordable housing was fundamental to human dignity, security and economic opportunity.

The Country Director of ActionAid Nigeria, Dr. Andrew Mamedu, said poverty was not inevitable but sustained by inequality, exclusion and policy decisions that denied millions of Nigerians access to basic necessities and opportunities.

“Poverty is not inevitable. It is sustained by inequality, exclusion and policy choices that continue to deny millions of Nigerians access to necessities and opportunities,” Mamedu said.

He added that no Nigerian family should have to choose between food, shelter, healthcare and education in a country endowed with abundant human and natural resources.

Mamedu called for public budgets that prioritised citizens’ welfare, social protection systems that reached vulnerable households, and economic policies capable of creating decent jobs and reducing inequality.

He said national progress should be measured not only by economic growth but also by improvements in the living conditions of the most vulnerable citizens.

On social protection, ActionAid Nigeria said the National Social Register remained an important mechanism for identifying poor and vulnerable households but stressed that its effectiveness depended on transparency, reliable data, inclusive access and accountable implementation.

It cautioned that registration did not automatically guarantee access to government assistance, urging authorities to ensure that eligible households could benefit from available interventions through fair and effective delivery systems.

The organisation said it was working with partners through the European Union-funded Support for Strengthening Social Protection in Nigeria (ESSPIN) project to raise awareness of the register, promote community participation and advocate accountable social protection systems in Abia, Benue, Oyo and Sokoto states.

It urged federal and state governments to increase funding for safe, adequate and affordable housing, particularly for low-income households, while expanding access to healthcare, education, clean water and sanitation.

ActionAid Nigeria also called for adequately financed and inclusive social protection programmes, decent employment opportunities and fiscal policies that protected vulnerable households rather than worsening inequality.

It urged the National Social Safety-Nets Coordinating Office, State Operations Coordinating Units and other relevant institutions to strengthen transparency, data integrity and public awareness in managing the National Social Register to ensure fair identification of vulnerable households.

The organisation further called on development partners, civil society groups and the media to promote meaningful participation by people experiencing poverty, particularly women, young people and persons with disabilities, while monitoring government commitments and demanding accountability for poverty reduction.

It maintained that poverty eradication required more than temporary relief measures, insisting that sustained public investment, equitable economic policies, accountable institutions and measurable implementation targets were essential to delivering lasting improvements.

“Poverty cannot be eradicated through declarations alone. It requires political will, deliberate investment in people and a collective commitment to justice, equality and human dignity,” the organisation said.

ActionAid Nigeria is a social justice non-governmental organisation working to eradicate poverty and injustice, with a focus on social justice, gender equality and sustainable development.

World.title: First Lady To Govs: Establish Functional Community Food Banks In All Senatorial Districts
World.content:
.Extends RHI food outreach to Katsina



Deji Elumoye in Abuja



Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has called on all the 36 state governors to establish functional community food banks in their respective three senatorial districts to strengthen food security and tackle malnutrition especially young children below the age of six, pregnant and lactating mothers.

The First Lady made the call yesterday during the presentation of food items to the wife of Katsina State Governor, Hajiya Zulaihat Radda, for onward distribution to vulnerable persons in the state under the Food Outreach Scheme of the Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI).

Mrs. Tinubu represented by wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Nana Shettima announced that Katsina State has become the 30th beneficiary of the scheme following the successful distributions to 29 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Launched in March 2024 under the Social Investment Programme of the Renewed Hope Initiative, the Food Outreach Scheme provides nutritional support to persons with disabilities, widows and other vulnerable groups to ease their hardship and improve family well-being.

The First Lady disclosed that the intervention is sustained through the generosity of two partners who provide two truckloads of food items monthly enabling the Initiative to support two states every month.

As part of efforts to address food insecurity and malnutrition, Mrs Tinubu also announced the successful completion of the nationwide rollout of the National Community Food Bank Programme designed to combat child malnutrition and support pregnant women and lactating mothers.

She urged state governors to adopt the framework and establish functional community food banks across senatorial districts in their various states stressing that federal and zonal interventions alone would not be sufficient to address the scale of the challenge.

According to her, stronger collaboration between federal and state governments would help extend nutritional support to more communities and ensure that vulnerable Nigerians have access to essential food supplies.

On his part, Governor of Katsina State, Mallam Dikko Umaru Radda, described the event as a day of Hope and Renewed commitment to the welfare of the people noting the intervention demonstrates the Federal Government’s resolve to reach vulnerable Nigerians at all levels.

He said the initiative was a practical intervention with tangible impact complementing the efforts of the Katsina State Government to improve the well-being of its citizens.

Radda noted that his government in alignment with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda is working towards building a future where every Nigerian could live with dignity through investments in education, healthcare and agriculture.

He added that the state government has made concerted efforts to improve security across communities by supporting security agencies with the necessary equipment to strengthen their operations.

The governor further stated that the Renewed Hope Agenda is designed to empower Nigerians to achieve their aspirations, urging the people of Katsina State to support the ruling party in the next election to sustain continuity in governance and development.

On her part, wife of the Katsina State Governor, Hajiya Zulaihat Dikko, expressed appreciation to the First Lady for the gesture stating that the Renewed Hope Initiative has continued to play an important role in promoting the welfare of Nigerians particularly women, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through its various social intervention programmes.

Osun, Ogun and Akwa Ibom States are expected to be next beneficiaries of the food distribution scheme.

The food items were formally handed over to the wife of the Katsina State Governor by wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Shettima, for distribution to the intended beneficiaries.

World.title: Abuja Film Industry Stagnates as Funding, Infrastructure Deficits Hamper Growth
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Abuja’s ambition to emerge as a major filmmaking hub is being undermined by inadequate infrastructure, opaque funding arrangements, a shortage of skilled technical personnel and weak distribution networks, Chairman of Fedmas Studios, Sam Idiagbonya, has warned.

Idiagbonya said the Federal Capital Territory possessed the environment and creative talent to build a competitive film industry but lacked the institutional support, technical capacity and commercial structures required to translate its potential into sustainable growth.

He called for improved production facilities, transparent access to government funding, professional training and stronger collaboration among filmmakers, arguing that the industry could not thrive if practitioners were left to navigate its structural challenges individually.

Speaking on the difficulties confronting filmmakers in Abuja, Idiagbonya said the city offered a relatively conducive environment for production but needed greater exposure and platforms through which local talents could showcase their work to wider audiences.

“Abuja offers a good environment for filmmaking, but we need the infrastructure, the training and the freedom to create,” he said.

The filmmaker identified Lagos as Nigeria’s dominant commercial filmmaking centre because of its established distribution networks, marketers and access to industry opportunities, but maintained that Abuja-based practitioners should not limit their ambitions to local audiences.

“My market is the world. Earth is my market,” he said, urging filmmakers to develop stories with universal appeal and explore opportunities beyond their immediate geographical markets.

He argued that the future of Abuja’s film industry would depend partly on the ability of practitioners to produce compelling content and establish distribution channels capable of connecting their work with audiences across Nigeria and internationally.

Beyond infrastructure, Idiagbonya raised concerns about the implementation of government funding initiatives for the creative sector, insisting that announcements of financial support must be accompanied by clear guidelines on access, eligibility and disbursement.

“If you tell creatives that there is a fund, they need to know the mechanism, the criteria, the timeline and who has benefited,” he said.

He explained that filmmaking involved substantial expenditure on equipment, personnel and post-production, adding that uncertainty surrounding funding arrangements could make it difficult for practitioners to plan and execute projects.

According to him, transparent procedures would enable filmmakers to understand available opportunities, prepare viable proposals and determine how financial support could help them improve production quality.

Idiagbonya also identified the shortage of trained technical professionals as a major concern, particularly in cinematography, lighting, sound and production design.

He cautioned against equating the ability to operate a camera with professional competence in cinematography, stressing that filmmaking required specialised technical knowledge, practical experience and continuous training.

He said investment in technical skills was essential to improving the quality of productions and enabling Abuja filmmakers to compete more effectively in an increasingly demanding market.

The Fedmas Studios chairman further called for a change in the industry’s professional culture, urging practitioners to embrace collaboration instead of allowing rivalry, disagreements and disputes over ownership to frustrate creative projects.

“The future of creativity is collaboration. You cannot do this alone,” he said.

He encouraged filmmakers to subject their scripts and ideas to constructive criticism and combine their resources, knowledge and expertise to strengthen productions.

On the commercial side, Idiagbonya identified high production and marketing costs, delayed payments and the distance between some cinema locations and residential communities as factors affecting the profitability of films.

He said the challenges required filmmakers to think beyond conventional cinema releases and develop distribution strategies suited to the changing habits of audiences.

Digital platforms, including YouTube, he noted, offered opportunities to reach international viewers, although success required an understanding of online monetisation and effective marketing.

“Today, you may be on YouTube. Tomorrow, you may be in the cinema. The next day, you may be on Netflix or working with an international platform,” he said.

He urged filmmakers to adopt flexible distribution models that would allow them to exploit different platforms as opportunities emerged, rather than depend exclusively on one channel for commercial returns.

Idiagbonya also called on governments to broaden support for the film industry beyond established creative centres, arguing that talent development and access to opportunities should extend to filmmakers across the country.

He advocated the establishment of a stronger national film festival that would bring Nigerian and international practitioners together for screenings, competitions, training and professional networking.

Such a platform, he said, would give emerging filmmakers greater visibility, encourage the exchange of ideas and create opportunities for partnerships that could improve the industry’s prospects.

He urged aspiring filmmakers to remain committed to developing their craft, building professional relationships and exploring different distribution channels despite the financial and structural obstacles confronting the sector.

For Abuja’s film industry, his argument is that creative talent alone cannot guarantee growth: sustained investment, professional expertise, transparent funding and access to markets are also necessary to turn the capital’s filmmaking potential into a viable industry.

World.title: Glo’s Support Has Transformed Ofala into World Renowned Cultural Festival, Says Igwe Achebe
World.content:
The traditional ruler of Onitsha, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, has commended Globacom for helping transform Ofala into a world-renowned cultural festival.

Speaking at the 2026 edition of the event at Ime Obi, Onitsha, Anambra State, on Friday, the monarch paid special tribute to the technology company for being a principal sponsor of Ofala for the past fifteen years.

“Their partnership has transformed the festival from a palace ritual to a world-renowned cultural festival owes a great deal to purposeful partnership. Since 2011, Globacom has stood with us as our principal

partner – now fifteen consecutive years of unwavering commitment”, Agbogidi said, adding that “ In good times and challenging times, Globacom has helped us preserve the authenticity of Ofala while enhancing its presentation, documentation, broadcast and global reach. They have helped take a living heritage to the global stage”.

He also applauded the vision of the Chairman of Globacom, Dr. Mike Adenuga, Jr., for his commitment to the preservation of Nigeria’s cultural heritage.

“I thank Globacom and its Chairman, Otunba (Dr) Mike Adenuga, Jr., GCON, a true man of culture, for his vision and belief that culture is not a luxury but a foundation for unity”, Achebe stated.

He noted that the theme of this year’s edition, “Igba Mbo, Iga N’Iru” – Strive and Advance – is “a call to industry, to excellence, to self-improvement and to collective progress. It reflects the spirit of our forebears who built a kingdom on the Niger, and it speaks to our youth who must carry that heritage forward with enterprise and purpose”.

In his goodwill message to the Igwe and Onitsha Kingdom, Dr Adenuga said, “our association with the Ofala Festival since 2011 has been much more than a corporate partnership. It has been a relationship which we cherish deeply and regard as a privilege”.

He expressed his gratitude to the Igwe for the opportunity given Globacom to contribute to the preservation, celebration and wider projection of the priceless cultural heritage. “It gives us great satisfaction to join Your Majesty and the people of Onitsha each year in showcasing to Nigeria, Africa and the wider world the beauty, dignity and enduring values represented by Ofala,” Dr. Adenuga concluded.

World.title: Nestle Nigeria Opens Entries for 2026 Media Awards
World.content:
Charles Ajunwa

Nestle Nigeria has opened entries for journalists and media professionals across the country to submit compelling stories for the sixth edition of the Nestle Media Awards, recognising journalism that brings important issues to the forefront, deepens public understanding and highlights solutions to challenges affecting people, communities and businesses.

A statement by the Corporate Affairs Manager, Nestle Nigeria, Toju Egbebi, said since its inception, the Awards have recognised outstanding reporting across areas aligned with Nestle Nigeria’s Creating Shared Value agenda, including nutrition, agriculture, environmental sustainability, youth and women empowerment, and community development.

“In 2025, the introduction of the Business and Economy Reporting category expanded the Platform’s scope to include journalism examining the challenges and opportunities shaping Nigeria’s business environment.

Speaking on the 2026 edition, Victoria Uwadoka, Head of Corporate Communications, Public Affairs and Sustainability at Nestle Nigeria, said: “Excellence in journalism requires more than telling a compelling story. It demands accuracy, depth, balanced perspectives and a commitment to the public interest. These are the qualities we have sought to recognise and encourage through the Nestle Media Awards. As we invite entries for this year’s edition, we remain committed to recognising the rigour, integrity and thoughtful reporting that distinguish exceptional journalism.”

The statement added, “This year, entries are invited across nine categories: Nutrition and Affordable Food Solutions, Environmental Sustainability, Youth Empowerment and Development, Women Empowerment, Community Development, Finance, Agriculture, Business and Economy Reporting, and Photojournalism Award.

“With the exception of Business and Economy Reporting, submissions must focus on Nestle

Nigeria or Nestle’s global activities and demonstrate a clear connection to the relevant award theme.

“The Business and Economy Reporting category welcomes stories examining Nigeria’s wider business environment, including entrepreneurship, economic policy, access to finance, infrastructure, competitiveness and the challenges and opportunities affecting small and

large enterprises. Entries in this category are not required to focus on Nestle, allowing journalists to explore broader issues and solutions that can help create a more enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

“The competition is open to journalists and media professionals working across print, broadcast and digital platforms in Nigeria. Eligible entries must have been published between November 1, 2025, and October 30, 2026.

“Each submission must include a link or copy of the published work, a profile of the entrant or media organisation of at least 100 words, and a 100-word description of the entry. Each published work may be submitted in only one category, while participants may submit one entry per category.

“Entries open on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and must be submitted through the official 2026 Nestle Nigeria Media Awards Entry Form no later than Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

“Submissions will be assessed by an independent panel of experienced media and industry professionals, with consideration given to accuracy and balance, depth, originality, relevance and the quality of storytelling.

“Winners will be announced at the 2026 Nestle Nigeria Media Awards ceremony on Sunday,

December 13, 2026, in Lagos, where outstanding journalists will be recognised for excellence in reporting across the nine award categories.”

World.title: Pistis Foundation Brings UBOMI 2026 to Lagos After Over 10,000 Medical Interventions in Ibadan
World.content:
Pistis Foundation has announced that its flagship UBOMI Medical and Surgical Outreach will hold in Lagos from October 19 to 23, 2026, bringing five days of completely free medical care to underserved communities.

The Lagos edition follows the successful UBOMI outreach in Ibadan, Oyo State, held from September 21 to 25, which recorded 10,292 medical interventions and reached 3,611 beneficiaries in five days. Services included 2,515 laboratory tests and screenings, 2,121 medical consultations, 1,740 pharmacy interventions, 701 eye-care services, 438 dental-care services, 109 theatre surgeries and 100 eye surgeries, alongside health promotion activities and other interventions.

The results in Ibadan demonstrate the scale of healthcare needs in underserved communities and the difference that coordinated, accessible medical services can make. As UBOMI returns to Lagos, Pistis Foundation aims to build on this momentum and reach more individuals and families who face financial barriers to quality healthcare.

Speaking ahead of the Lagos outreach, Leonard F. Thomas, Executive Director of Pistis Foundation, reaffirmed the Foundation’s commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind because they cannot afford the care they need.

“Healthcare should never be a privilege reserved for those who can afford it. No one should have to endure pain, live with a treatable condition or forgo necessary medical attention simply because of financial limitations. Through UBOMI, we are working to close that gap by bringing quality medical and surgical care directly to underserved communities, completely free of charge. Our goal is simple: to ensure that the ability to pay does not determine who gets the opportunity to live a healthier life.”

Commenting on the Foundation’s broader vision and the significance of the outreach, Pastor Gorman Akinlabi, Board Chairman of Pistis Foundation and Senior Lead Pastor of The Elevation Church, said:

“At Pistis Foundation, we believe that meaningful impact is measured not only by the number of lives reached, but by the dignity restored and the lasting difference made in communities. UBOMI reflects our enduring commitment to putting compassion into action and ensuring that access to essential healthcare is not determined by economic circumstances. As we mark eight years of the Foundation’s work, we remain committed to building partnerships and advancing initiatives that bring hope, improve wellbeing and create lasting change. We are grateful to the medical professionals, volunteers, partners and supporters who continue to make this mission possible.”

The Lagos outreach will provide a range of free services, including general medical consultations, specialist care, laboratory investigations, dental care, eye examinations and glasses, surgical procedures, prescribed medications and other essential health services. Surgical beneficiaries will undergo pre-screening to determine eligibility for procedures.

The outreach will take place at Pistis Annex, Eti-Osa, Lagos, from October 19 to 23. Residents of underserved communities are encouraged to attend early, as services will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis. No payment is required.

The 2026 UBOMI campaign also comes at a significant milestone for its founding organisation. As The Elevation Church celebrates 16 years and Pistis Foundation marks eight years of impact, the Foundation’s healthcare interventions have grown to nearly 60,000 medical interventions since UBOMI began. This milestone reflects years of sustained commitment to making essential healthcare more accessible to people who might otherwise be unable to afford it.

Since its inception, UBOMI has mobilised medical professionals, technical partners, volunteers and supporters to deliver a broad range of healthcare services to underserved communities. The programme continues to demonstrate how collaboration and targeted intervention can help address barriers to healthcare access while restoring dignity, hope and well-being.

Pistis Foundation invites community leaders, partners, medical professionals and the public to help spread the word about UBOMI Lagos so that those who need these services most can benefit.

World.title: Beer, rugby and AK-47s: HOW 1981 Seychelles coup unraveled
World.content:
The story of the botched 1981 Seychelles coup under 'Mad Mike' Hoare would be too farcical for even a Sly Stallone action flick. Image: File/Fotor

The story of the failed 1981 Seychelles coup is one the Department of Defence may wish never happened. An example of an isolated government in Apartheid being overconfident, under prepared and paying the price for it. Nevertheless, 45 years on, their hubris is something we can learn from …

It’s 25 November 1981. And a group of about 50 men step off a flight in the Seychelles posing as tourists on a stag trip. They call themselves the Ancient Order of Froth-Blowers. This happens to be a name borrowed from a real 1930s English beer-drinking club. The only difference is beneath false bottoms in their luggage, covered with rugby kit, is a barrage of AK-47s.

1981 SEYCHELLES COUP

The target in this hastily arranged 1981 Seychelles coup is President France-Albert René. He had seized power in 1977 by ousting James Mancham, a pro-Western leader. The aim was to put Mancham back in charge. The mission was being led by Colonel ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare. The Irishman was a legendary Congo mercenary, born in Calcutta, but living in Durban at the time.



The disguises in this 1981 Seychelles coup lasted all of a few minutes when they encountered an inquisitive customs official. A search turned up one of the many hidden rifles and gunfire erupted all across the airport. Cornered, the mercenaries fought their way to the airport control tower and held it hostage for several hours.

With no way out, they spotted their escape: An Air India Boeing 707, Flight 224, which was refueling on its way from Salisbury to Bombay. They commandeered it, with 65 passengers and 14 crew aboard, and ordered it to fly it back to South Africa. It was eventually diverted to Durban, where officials had shut down air traffic control for seven hours, and forced the mercenaries to surrender.

AFTERMATH OF FAILED 1981 SEYCHELLES COUP

Air India 707. Image: File

The Apartheid regime had a big problem, the world was watching and the reaction to the failed 1981 Seychelles coup was fierce. Most of the men were initially released, however, hijacking an airliner is serious and the government needed to deniability. So, ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare and 42 others were eventually charged and convicted of hijacking in a Pietermaritzburg court in 1982.



Hoare’s sentence, reported to be 20 years, was served in just 33 months before a presidential amnesty freed him. Other men received similarly short terms. The UN Security Council condemned the coup attempt in resolutions 496 and 507. René was only emboldened and stayed in power for another two decades.

But what do you think? Had you ever heard of the 1981 Seychelles coup? Do you have any other examples of crazy South African stories many might’ve forgotten? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: DStv to remove popular kids channel this November
World.content:
A popular children's channel will be cut from DStv this November. Image: canva / file

DStv is losing another international TV channel, with preschool channel JimJam set to disappear from the platform in November after more than a decade.

JimJam will be removed from DStv on 11 November 2026, bringing an end to its 13-year run on the pay-TV service.

The channel, provided by AMC Networks International (AMCNI), was added to DStv in November 2013. MultiChoice has confirmed the channel’s departure but has not explained why it is being removed.



JimJam to leave DStv

MultiChoice told TVwithThinus that JimJam is being removed as DStv continues to “review and refine its channel line-up”, but the broadcaster did not provide a specific reason for ending the channel’s distribution.

JimJam is also notably the last remaining AMC Networks International channel on DStv, meaning its departure will bring the relationship between the two companies to an end on the platform.

MultiChoice added that it will continue to invest in preschool entertainment despite JimJam’s departure.

Sthembiso Semenya, a MultiChoice spokesperson, said DStv is investing in preschool children’s programming through PlayRoom, which brings together local and international content for younger viewers.

Depending on their DStv package, families can also access preschool programming through Cartoonito, CBeebies and DreamWorks.

DStv customers can check the platform’s TV Guide for the channels and programmes available on their specific package.



The latest in a string of channel cuts

The channel’s departure comes during a year of significant changes to DStv’s channel line-up.

MultiChoice has already removed a number of channels in 2026, including BET Africa, MTV Base, CBS Justice and CBS Reality in January.

Cinemagic and Magic Showcase were subsequently removed at the end of June, while M-Net Movies 1, kykNET Lekker, Mzansi Bioskop and Mzansi Magic were discontinued in September.

The changes have also affected DStv’s specialist packages.

In October, MultiChoice announced that five channels would be removed from its R280 Add Indian package from 31 October.

These are SET Asia, Zee TV, SET Max, Zee Cinema and WION, leaving the package with just three channels: Star Plus, Star Vijay and Colors TV.

At the time, MultiChoice said it was refining the line-up to better match how customers watch content and was moving towards “fewer, stronger channels” rather than spreading similar content across more channels.

That decision followed DStv’s major package overhaul in September, after Canal+ completed its acquisition of MultiChoice’s parent company in 2025.

World.title: Orlando Pirates sweat over Sebelebele as Chiefs Derby looms
World.content:
Orlando Pirates could receive a timely boost ahead of the Soweto Derby, with Kamogelo Sebelebele potentially returning to action in time for their highly anticipated clash against Kaizer Chiefs at the end of the month.

The 23-year-old right-back suffered an injury setback during the first half of the MTN8 final against Mamelodi Sundowns, forcing him off the pitch as the Buccaneers went on to lose the match.

Sebelebele subsequently missed Pirates’ midweek encounter against TS Galaxy and is also expected to sit out Saturday’s CAF Champions League clash against African Stars.



His absence has left Pirates monitoring his recovery, with the Soweto Derby against their bitter rivals Chiefs looming on the horizon.

The injury could also present an opportunity for new signing Bulelani Sigomoshe to stake his claim for a place in the team as head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou considers his options at right-back.

Speaking about the defender’s condition, Ouaddou confirmed that Sebelebele was still being assessed by the club’s medical department, although he remains hopeful that the injury is not serious.

“He is still being assessed by the medical department. I still hope it is not so bad. But we will have some more news, I think, soon,” the Pirates coach said.

Ouaddou also ruled the defender out of the upcoming CAF Champions League fixture against African Stars but stopped short of confirming when he could return.

“But I think for the Champions League, definitely I cannot use him, but we will see for the next games if we can have him or not. We hope it’s not so bad,” he added as per FARPost.



Pirates will be hoping for positive news from their medical team as they prepare for a demanding run of fixtures. However, Sebelebele’s availability for the Soweto Derby will depend on the progress of his recovery.

Sebelebele has become an important player for Pirates

Since joining Orlando Pirates in 2025, Sebelebele has established himself as an important member of the squad, with his pace and attacking threat making him a valuable option on the right flank.

His performances have also earned him recognition at international level, as he has represented Bafana Bafana at the FIFA World Cup.

With the Soweto Derby fast approaching, Pirates will be eager to have the defender available for the crucial encounter. For now, the Buccaneers must wait for further medical assessments before determining whether he will be fit to face Kaizer Chiefs.

Who should replace Sebelebele?

World.title: ‘Happy valedictory day babes’: Rachel Kolisi shows Siya’s sister love
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi showed Liphelo, the sister of her ex-husband Siya Kolisi, love and support as she ends her schooling career, via an Instagram post on Saturday 17 October.

RACHEL KOLISI TO SIYA’S SISTER: ‘HAPPY VALEDICTORY DAY BABES’

Siya Kolisi’s sister, Liphelo Madlingozi is completing her matric year in 2026. Rachel Kolisi, the ex-wife of Siya, took to Instagram to celebrate Liphelo ending her school career. Take a look…

“Happy valedictory day babes 😭♥️. 2 down 2 to go! 😅,” she wrote.



Fans took to the comments section of the post to gush over Rachel.

“God bless you, sweetheart! ❤️ May He meet you at the point of your needs, enlarge your territory, and take you to even greater heights. May His favour and grace continue to follow you always! 🙏❤️,” wrote @zanndzube.



“Great support from you. Keep on with your good work🙏🌹🌹🌹,” wrote @gert.ferrerira.79.

“You’re doing such a great job. God bless you😍😍. They will never forget your constant love and support,” wrote @titusxolile.

“Well done to Phelo 🎊💯🙏🌸but Ms Rachel…this glow up is something else🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏🤏,” wrote @jacobsshelley.







RACHEL AND SIYA KOLISI LEGALLY ADOPTED HIS SIBLINGS
