Siya has two half-siblings Liyema and Liphelo. The siblings were reportedly left bouncing from orphanages to foster homes after their mother and father passed away. Siya and Rachel officially adopted his siblings in 2014, when they were financially stable enough to do so.

Siya reportedly found his siblings in foster care in Zwide – a township in Gqeberha. Siya explained that when he went to see his siblings, his sister didn’t know him.

“My little sister didn’t know me. She had been crawling when I last saw her. I told the woman taking care of them that I was going to take them for December holidays that year, which I did. But afterwards I said I can’t send them back,” he said according to reports.



“I had to go through a legal process, which I started after that holiday. It took about 18 months, but I finally legally adopted them,” he continued.

It’s been 12 years since Rachel and Siya adopted Liyema and Liphelo. Back in 2024, Rachel reflected on it being 10 years with the brother and sister duo.

“While celebrating Liphelo’s birthday last week, and having all 4 kids home for the weekend, we reflected on the fact that almost to the day, 10 years ago, Liphelo and Liyema came to spend a week with us in Cape Town to see that they were comfortable to make the move and come stay with us forever,” she wrote.



“I was 24 years old Nic was 3 months old, Liphelo had just turned 7 and Liyema 12. 10 years, of the greatest gift God could have ever given me,” she continued.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs begin their hunt for R66 million
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs begin their CAF Confederation Cup campaign away to Zambian side Red Arrows on Saturday afternoon.

Amakhosi are competing in the second preliminary round, hoping to reach the group stages for the second successive season.

Reaching that stage would guarantee Chiefs at least R6.6 million in prize money, while winning the competition could earn them a whopping R66 million.



When are Kaizer Chiefs in action?

Chiefs face Red Arrows in Ndola on Saturday at 15:00 at the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, nearly 300km from the Zambian capital, Lusaka, where their opponents usually play at Nkoloma Stadium.

The Soweto giants travelled to Zambia on Thursday with a 23-man squad following a 1-1 home draw against Stellenbosch FC in their latest league outing.

The team held their pre-match training session on Friday at 15:00 to familiarise themselves with the conditions ahead of Saturday’s encounter.



Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz will hope to guide his side into the group stages as they look to build on last season’s continental campaign.

Da Cruz has previous experience in the CAF Confederation Cup, having led Moroccan side AS FAR to the quarterfinals in the 2022/23 campaign. Their run ended against eventual winners USM Alger.

Chiefs will, however, be without regular captain Brandon Petersen, who was not included in the travelling squad as he continues his recovery from injury.



Amakhosi will be targeting a positive result away from home to give themselves an advantage ahead of the return leg.

Can Amakhosi reach the group stages of the Confed Cup?

World.title: The holiday town with beachfront property for R250 000
World.content:
Own a slice of the South Coast. Image: Pexels

If you enjoy being by the beach when the weather’s warmer, this might be the perfect time to own your own slice of it.

In one town on KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast, for R250 000 you can have the privilege of living metres from the beach.

Own your dream home on the beach

This could be your last chance to buy affordable beachfront property in a Blue Flag beach location.



According to one Private Property listing, you can get a 1 464-square-metre plot, 350 metres from Marina Beach, 1 of 11 Blue Flag beaches in the region.

The property is listed with an asking price of R250 000.

Buyers should expect to pay at least R100 000 in cash, as banks typically give a 60% loan-to-value for land over ten years.



If you don’t take out a building loan, you’ll pay roughly R2 500 a month for the property, including the R500 in rates and taxes.

But that can be worthwhile because the property has a semi-private beach entrance.

Residents use a semi-private road to get to the beach. The path is a 5-minute walk only shared with neighbours.



While other plots offering similar amenities are listed for above R300 000, buyers have plenty of options for an affordable holiday or retirement home.

Buyers can get a 2-bedroom flat in the Marina Glen Holiday Resort for R530 000.

Those who want direct beach access can buy a 2-bedroom townhouse for R830 000 that leads directly onto the golden sand.



Holidays in Marina Beach

Marina Beach is a coastal village, protected from the crowds that migrate to areas like Margate for a holiday.

This area is largely unspoiled. Wildlife like duiker, impala, and buck abound. The area benefits from 195 bird species and a 60-hectare nature reserve.

You’ll want to travel to the town year after year.



Avid golfers will enjoy the 9 golf courses near Marina Beach, including the San Lameer Golf Course.

Those who love the water will appreciate that, even in winter, the water and weather are warm enough to enjoy water activities.

Children can enjoy the water safely in tidal and rock pools.



During the sardine run, dolphins, whales and sharks visit the region.

With a year-round tourism season, buyers could earn when not using the property.

On Booking.com and Airbnb, rentals in the area typically list for R1 500 a night during peak periods and R900 a night in the low season.



The Marina Beach Property Market

The property prices in Marina Beach have been steadily rising since 2022.

That year, the average sale price was R715 000. Today it’s R1.1 million, according to data from the KwaZulu-Natal Deeds Office.

Marina Beach could experience a sharper increase in coming years as the village is the cheapest of the surrounding areas.



In neighbouring Southbroom, the average sale price is R2.4 million.

Then, in San Lameer, the average sale price is R1.6 million.

World.title: KZN Premier condemns murder of ANC members in Umgababa
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal Premier Thamsanqa Ntuli has condemned the brutal killing of two African National Congress (ANC) members who were allegedly shot dead while conducting door-to-door campaigning at Umgababa, south of Durban.

The incident happened on Thursday afternoon, 15 October.

KZN PREMIER MOURNS ANC MEMBERS SHOT AND KILLED IN UMGABABA

According to a report from the South African Police Service (SAPS) in KwaZulu-Natal, the victims, a man and a woman, were part of a five-person group comprising three ANC members and two bodyguards. The group was reportedly approached from behind by a white Isuzu bakkie, whose occupants allegedly opened fire on them.



Following the incident, Premier Ntuli conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, the ANC and all those affected by this tragic incident. He has also wished the injured woman a speedy recovery.

Ntuli said the loss of these two lives is deeply distressing.

“We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones and to everyone affected by this tragedy. We also wish the injured woman a speedy recovery,” he said.

The Premier has called on SAPS to work around the clock to identify and apprehend those responsible, and to conduct a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

“We call on the police to leave no stone unturned in their efforts to track down and arrest those responsible for this heinous crime. The perpetrators must be brought before the courts to face the full might of the law. We urge anyone who witnessed the incident or has information that could assist the investigation to come forward and share it with the police,” he said.

The Premier emphasised that the circumstances surrounding the incident must be established through a thorough police investigation and cautioned against speculation while the investigation is ongoing.



PREMIER REITERATES IMPORTANCE OF PEACEFUL CAMPAIGNING

With KwaZulu-Natal preparing for the Local Government Elections scheduled for 4 November 2026, Premier Ntuli has reiterated the importance of peaceful campaigning, mutual respect and the protection of every citizen’s right to participate freely in the democratic process

Ntuli said every political party and candidate must be able to campaign freely and safely in every community.

“There must be no ‘no-go areas’ in KwaZulu-Natal. We must respect one another’s rights and ensure that all political activities take place peacefully and within the law,” said Premier Ntuli.

ANC convenor in eThekwini, Thanduxolo Sabela also condemned the murder of fellow ANC members and called for peaceful campaigning.

“We don’t believe that when conducting a campaign the would be areas where our campaigners would be met with such hostility and be shot at,” he said.

World.title: Durban gets a newly revamped swimming pool ahead of summer
World.content:
Umlazi swimming pool has reopened with new sports facilities. Image: eThekwini Municipality / Facebook

Residents in Umlazi in Durban have a refurbished public swimming pool and new sports facilities to make use of, following the official reopening of the Umlazi BB Swimming Pool on 16 October.

The reopening was led by Chairperson of Community Services Cllr Zama Sokhabase, alongside Ward 84 Councillor Msizi Mabaso, who also handed over newly completed combi courts within the swimming pool precinct.

The courts are designed to accommodate several sporting codes, including basketball, tennis, netball and indoor soccer.



New sports facilities for the Durban community

The wait is over! It was all smiles, excitement and pride in Ward 84 today when the newly refurbished Umlazi BB swimming pool officially reopened alongside combi courts for multiple sporting codes such as basketball, tennis, netball and indoor soccer. pic.twitter.com/8sEEZiDewu — eThekwini Municipality (@eThekwiniM) October 16, 2026

The new courts are part of efforts to create more accessible recreational spaces where Durban residents can exercise and participate in organised sport.

The municipality says the facilities are intended to encourage healthier lifestyles while providing opportunities for sporting development, particularly among young people.

The upgraded precinct is expected to give residents more options for staying active, while also creating space for young athletes to develop their skills.

The refurbishment and new courts form part of the municipality’s commitment to improving community recreational facilities across the city.

World.title: March and March to challenge Constitutional Court asylum ruling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - March and March has said it will fight what it calls unfair asylum rules in response to a Constitutional Court ruling.

The apex court ruled asylum seekers must have access to the process, with every claim assessed on its merits.

But March and March argued the way these laws are implemented can work against South Africans.

Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, the organisation's leader, said they want refugee camps where officials can screen and verify asylum seekers at the border.

" Illegal immigrants must remain illegal immigrants. And we've been saying and preaching this for the longest time that if we had refugee camps, all of this would not be happening because people who are at the border and come in claiming to be asylum seekers would have one set place where they are all processed and checked and verified if they are truly indeed asylum seekers.

"But in a country where asylum seekers are given even rights to open businesses and look for jobs, obviously everyone will look for loopholes to abuse the system. So now we're just opening up ourselves to further abuse, and the reason why we further know that what we're saying is supported is that the Home Affairs department itself said that 95% of the people who are actually applying for asylum seeker status are not real asylum seekers.

"So why would we want to waste resources and time going through people who we already have a clear database of them not being really asylum seekers and migrants? And then they come into the country and once they're in the country, they start litigating against government because they don't want to leave.

"So I'm hearing a lot of people saying that people don't understand the Constitutional Court judgment and what it says. We absolutely understand what it says, but we know that the laws of the country have been used several times to go against the people of South Africa. And the implementation of those laws has never ever been to the satisfaction of South Africa, and that's why we're saying that we don't want that to happen, and we're gonna stand and fight it no- whichever way that we have to fight it."

World.title: Brother recounts desperate race to save slain sister
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The brother of one of the three Boxer managers killed in a shooting is still struggling to come to terms with her death.

He recalls rushing to the scene, desperately hoping his sister would survive.

The shooting was carried out allegedly by a former employee.

Thandiwe Chili, one of the three managers gunned down this week, is being buried.

Bheki Chili said he saw people running out of the store and though there might have been a robbery.

"In my mind, I thought it was a robbery. I thought that was why they were screaming.

But I couldn’t just leave without knowing what was happening. I tried calling her because I knew she was a manager. Someone else picked up the phone.

"I asked for the phone to be handed to its owner, but they repeatedly pushed me aside. That forced me to turn back and abandon the direction I was going in. I went back to Boxer.

I found that the authorities had cordoned off the place with danger tape and were not allowing people to go in.

"I forced my way in, even though the police didn’t want me to. I said I wanted to see my sister.

I found the other two lying on the floor together. My sister had been pulled out. I assume they were trying to find a way to rush her to hospital because she was still breathing.

"When the emergency services arrived to assist them, they kept trying to resuscitate her.

I got to her and touched her. I had hoped that, because they kept pumping her chest, she would survive.

In an instant, while I was with my cousin, I saw that they had covered her."

World.title: Hlabisa warns of extreme heat and drought risks this summer
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cooperative Governance Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa warns that this summer will bring tough weather, with soaring temperatures and heatwaves expected under El Niño.

He said government is activating disaster management systems and ramping up communication to help communities prepare for droughts and other weather risks.

Hlabisa spoke during the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction programme in Mpumalanga, which focuses on building resilience and ensuring communities know how to respond when disasters strike.

"Not only this weekend, from this summer season up to March 2027, the most difficult weather conditions under El Nino, the high temperature, but high levels of heat is also going to be a disaster that we are talking about activating our systems, ensuring communication reaches everybody, because we should be ready to mitigate the effects of drought that will be as a result of the heat waves, our farmers, our children at schools, in homes that people must not expose themselves unnecessarily."

World.title: ANC wants Western Cape back from DA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC in the Western Cape said it’s ready to govern Cape Town.

The party hopes to build on its 2021 support as it challenges the DA in the metro, which the ANC last governed in 2006.

The ANC is also taking aim at the DA’s governance record, accusing it of not addressing the needs of poorer communities.

ANC Western Cape spokesperson Sifiso Mtsweni said they are intensifying their campaign.

"Our campaign is intensifying, we are left with just 20 days before elections and the Western Cape, I'm sure you've seen, even various polling stations have been telling you that the DA will lose its maturity, particularly in the city.

"The ANC will increase its base from 2021. We've been hard at work, our structures have been on the ground and I'm sure as you drive around Cape Town you can see the ANC is well branded, our structures are ready, we've got all our candidates now and we've made sure that we follow a rigorous process of ensuring that our candidates are credible, are qualified and are people that are enjoying the confidence of their communities.

"One thing that has become very clear, particularly in the Western Cape, is that the Democratic Alliance in the last 15 years or so has proven to be an organisation that works for a few.

"We've seen various reports, I mean the Constitutional Court giving a damning finding around issues of Tafelberg where public land was used for private sales, where we've seen the public protector saying that the city of Cape Town does not deliver services particularly to our areas such as Langa, Khayelitsha and all those areas. So our people really have seen that the DA is nothing but a fuss, it's nothing but a face cut, it's an organisation that only cares for a few, does not care for our people."

World.title: Professor Wezile Chitha new UFH VC
World.content:
DIKENI – In a special meeting, the Council of the University of Fort Hare unanimously approved the appointment of Professor Wezile Chitha as the University's new Vice-Chancellor and Principal.

He will assume office during the first quarter of 2027.

In a statement, Council Chairperson Dr Siyanda Makaula, said Council considered the unanimous recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor Recruitment and Selection Committee, the outcomes of institutional voting processes and the comprehensive candidate assessments.

" Professor Chitha emerged as the highest-ranked candidate in both the Senate and Institutional Forum assessments, demonstrating consistent support across these important institutional governance structures.

"This formed an important consideration in Council's final determination. Professor Chitha brings extensive academic leadership, executive management experience and expertise in institutional governance and transformation.

"A qualified medical doctor, health economist and accomplished academic, he holds a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB), a Master's degree in Public Health, specialising in Health Economics from the University of Cape Town, and a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Public Health from Walter Sisulu University."

Professor Chita replaces Professor Sakhela Buhlungu.

Buhlungu submitted his resignation in September, shortly before he was due to begin presenting his defence at a disciplinary hearing.

Buhlungu is facing several disciplinary charges, including gross misconduct, insubordination and bringing the university into disrepute.

Among the allegations against him is that he unlawfully appointed two executive directors.

World.title: Kubayi leads push to tackle GBVF in Soweto
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi is taking the fight against gender-based violence and femicide to Soweto.

She will host a community imbizo at Phiri Sports Ground.

It will focus on strengthening efforts to prevent abuse and support victims and survivors.

It comes as the country still reels from the discovery of the bodies of 12 women in Ekurhuleni.

The programme will begin with a 600-metre Freedom March Against GBVF from Phiri Public Library to the sports ground.

Residents will also be briefed on the National Register for Sex Offenders.

World.title: Political parties campaign countrywide
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans head to the polls for the local government elections in less than three weeks.

And political parties are in the final stretch to woo voters.

ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa is on the campaign trail in the Western Cape.

The party is trying to make inroads in Cape Town, where it has struggled to win voters for years.

Meanwhile, in Johannesburg, the DA is holding its mass rally in Soweto.

Mayoral candidate Helen Zille will address supporters on Saturday morning.

Also in Johannesburg, Al Jama-ah is launching its manifesto in Orlando.

The party will outline its plans and priorities ahead of the 4 November polls.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: From 'Chogo' to senator? Winnie Odinga steps into her own political spotlight
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

From Raila Odinga’s shadow to her own political path, Winnie sets her sights on the Nairobi Senate seat in 2027. [Courtesy]

The hat was more than a hat. Literally.

As Raila Odinga’s body made its final journey home from India, his youngest daughter, Winnie, held tightly to his familiar cream-coloured fedora. It was one of the few things she could still protect, a small piece of a man whose presence had filled her life and Kenya’s political imagination for decades.

The image of Winnie carrying her father’s hat was deeply personal. The country was mourning a political giant, but she was mourning her father.

A year later, on the first anniversary of Raila’s death, Winnie has announced her intention to contest the Nairobi Senate seat in the 2027 General Election.

The timing is poignant. On a day devoted to remembering her father, she has declared her own political ambitions, signalling a shift from being one of the most recognisable faces of the Odinga family to a politician seeking a mandate in her own right.

“As Edwin Sifuna seeks a higher office, I see an opportunity in Nairobi, which is why I have decided I will vie for Senator of Nairobi County,” she said.

And just like that, the conversation shifted from the daughter who carried Baba’s hat to the politician who wants a seat of her own.

The last-born girl

To many Kenyans, Winnie is Chogo, the last-born child of Raila and Ida Odinga. The nickname carries the familiarity of family life, a reminder that behind the powerful surname is a daughter who grew up in a household where politics was never far from the conversation.

Her father was no ordinary political figure. His name could summon crowds, ignite debate and divide opinion. His decades-long career placed the Odinga family at the centre of Kenya’s political story.

Growing up as Raila’s youngest daughter meant sharing him with a country that claimed a piece of his time, energy and, eventually, his final goodbye.

Yet Winnie was not simply a spectator in her father’s political world. She worked around his campaigns and communications before stepping into politics herself, eventually winning a seat in the East African Legislative Assembly.

In November 2022, Parliament elected her to represent Kenya in the regional legislature, where she took office in December that year. Based in Arusha, Tanzania, she became part of the East African Community’s legislative institution, serving a five-year term running to 2027.

The EALA offered Winnie a political platform beyond her father’s immediate circle and an opportunity to participate in regional affairs. Her current tenure has also given her experience in legislative politics before her proposed move into elective politics at home.

The Nairobi Senate bid would take her into a different contest, one in which voters will have to decide whether her experience, ideas and political programme merit their support.

The hat she could not let go

For years, Raila’s trademark headgear had been part of his public identity, appearing at political rallies, meetings and public ceremonies. But in Winnie’s hands, it became something else: a personal possession tied to the final journey of a daughter and her father

She explained how protective she had been of it throughout the journey, describing it as one of the few things she could still hold on to.

The image captured a kind of helplessness that public figures’ families rarely get to show. Crowds could mourn Raila, politicians could speak of his legacy, and supporters could debate who would inherit his political movement. Winnie, however, had been left with the painful task of bringing her father home.

The symbolism of the hat has since acquired another layer. At a ceremony in Bondo earlier this month, elders placed a traditional hat on Winnie’s head in a symbolic gesture associated with the possibility of her carrying forward her father’s political mantle.

Winnie’s political journey has not started with this Senate announcement.

Her election to the East African Legislative Assembly placed her among Kenya’s representatives in a regional institution whose work concerns cooperation among East African Community partner states.

The role gave her a platform in regional legislation while her father remained a central figure in national politics.

The Senate is responsible for representing counties, participating in lawmaking on matters concerning counties and exercising oversight over revenue allocated to county governments. A Nairobi senator must therefore make a case on issues that touch residents directly, from public spending and service delivery to the accountability of county leadership.

The capital is also a demanding political terrain. Its electorate is diverse, its concerns immediate and its contests fiercely competitive.

A famous surname may open doors, but it cannot replace a convincing programme on jobs, housing, transport, healthcare and the management of public resources.

Winnie will have to demonstrate that she understands Nairobi beyond its place in her father’s national political story.

Can she translate the loyalty associated with Raila into support for her own agenda? Can she persuade voters that she is more than the daughter of a political icon?

Those questions will follow her into the campaign.

The Odingaism

Political inheritance can be both an advantage and a burden.

Raila’s name carries a formidable history of opposition politics, democratic reform and a loyal support base. It also invites comparisons that few politicians have to contend with.

Winnie’s challenge will be to honour that history without allowing it to become the entirety of her political identity.

Raila’s death left a space in the Orange Democratic Movement and among supporters who had looked to him for direction through decades of political contests. The question of who will carry his legacy has inevitably turned towards his family and the wider political movement he helped build.

Winnie’s Senate bid will require her to turn recognition into a political proposition that voters can interrogate. Her experience at EALA gives her a legislative starting point; the Nairobi contest will demand that she demonstrate how that experience can serve residents of the capital.

She must also navigate the expectations attached to her father’s name while making room for her own ideas, priorities and leadership style.

There is a temptation to see Winnie’s future entirely through the lens of inheritance. She is Raila’s daughter, the last-born known as Chogo, the woman who carried his hat and the politician whom some supporters hope will continue his legacy.

But she is also a woman making a decision about her own future.

The Senate bid offers her an opportunity to define what that future means, beyond the grief surrounding her father’s death and the weight of a name that has shaped Kenyan politics for decades.

The hat remains an unforgettable image from Raila’s final journey home. A daughter attempted to protect the last tangible thing she could hold on to.

The Senate will demand something different: a political vision, a campaign and the votes of Nairobi residents.

Chogo has announced her next move. Will Winnie Odinga turn the memory of Baba into a mandate of her own?

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Here’s why Moody’s has upgraded Egypt’s credit rating
World.content:
The credit rating agency Moody’s has upgraded Egypt’s long-term credit rating from Caa1 to B3, while maintaining a positive outlook.

This upgrade is supported by several factors, including the stabilization of the exchange rate against the US dollar, a sustained period of fiscal consolidation, and structural economic reforms that have successfully reduced public debt indicators.

The agency highlighted a track record of robust primary budget surpluses—which reached 4.9 percent of GDP in the 2026 fiscal year—as a key driver behind this decision.

Furthermore, efforts to mobilize revenue —combined with expenditure controls and adjustments to energy prices —have contributed to reducing total government debt to 81.8 percent of GDP as of June 2026, down from 95.2 percent three years earlier.

Economic strengthening

According to Moody’s, reforms initiated since the beginning of 2024 have also significantly strengthened the economy’s capacity to absorb exchange rate volatility.

The shift toward a flexible exchange rate regime and a tighter monetary policy has eliminated chronic foreign currency shortages, allowing official reserves to rise to US$57 billion by September 2026.

Egypt’s updated policy frameworks have shown their resilience in the face of regional geopolitical developments and rising global oil prices, preventing a sharp depletion of reserves.

Official foreign currency inflows—driven by tourism and remittances—have rebounded sharply, helping to offset the decline in Suez Canal revenues and the broader trade deficit in the hydrocarbons sector.

This continued positive outlook reflects expectations that sustained fiscal discipline could help reduce government debt and borrowing costs more rapidly than currently anticipated in the baseline scenario.

Further gains remain contingent upon potential divestments under the State Ownership Policy, as well as a prospective recovery in domestic energy production and maritime traffic.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egypt named among 7 destinations recommended by Forbes for 2027
World.content:
Forbes magazine has included Egypt in a list of seven tourist destinations recommended for a visit in 2027, based on selections by OvationNetwork, a company specializing in luxury travel.

This recognition highlights the appeal of Egypt as a diverse tourist destination— with offerings ranging from ancient monuments to luxurious Nile cruises.

According to the report, Egypt has once again caught the attention of travelers seeking profound tourism experiences.

This is bolstered by the country’s rich array of archaeological and historical sites, as well as an expanding selection of luxury Nile cruises that connect Luxor and Aswan, offering visitors the chance to explore temples and ancient landmarks along the banks of the Nile.

The report cites a travel advisor at OvationNetwork as noting that improved political stability has brought Egypt back into the tourism spotlight—a trend bolstered by an expanding range of luxury Nile cruise offerings.

The report also recommends visiting the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, highlighting it as a premier cultural attraction alongside the Pyramids of Giza, which stand as an extraordinary symbol of ancient Egyptian civilization.

The list further includes the Dolomites in Italy, Lima (the capital of Peru), the coast of Montenegro, Bangkok and northern Thailand, Ireland, and Brazil’s Pantanal region—an area renowned for its ecological diversity and wildlife.

World.title: Egypt ranks 3rd in Africa for tourism in 2026 Travel & Tourism Development Index
World.content:
Egypt has secured the third position in Africa—and 63rd globally—in the 2026 Travel & Tourism Development Index, published by the World Economic Forum in collaboration with the Zurich Insurance Group, as reported by the African economic news agency “Ecofin.”

Mauritius ranked first in Africa (59th globally), followed by South Africa in second place (61st globally), with Egypt placing third.

The index does not directly measure the number of tourists, the volume of spending, or tourism-related revenue.

It instead assesses the environment that enables countries to attract tourism and develop it sustainably, as well as their capacity to provide the conditions necessary for the sector’s growth.

The index covers 110 countries and is based on 102 sub-indicators—categorized into five key dimensions—that encompass security and stability, infrastructure and air transport, policies and visa regulations, price competitiveness, digital services, tourism resources, and sustainability.

While Egypt’s achievement of the third-place ranking in Africa is significant, the results also highlight areas for improvement—specifically regarding the quality of services, the streamlining of procedures, the expansion of hotel capacity, the enhancement of the tourist experience, and the strengthening of sustainability and air connectivity.

Egypt’s true challenge lies in transforming substantial assets into greater outcomes—namely, higher tourist numbers, increased average spending, and longer stays—thereby propelling the country toward a more prominent global standing.

World.title: Air Cairo extends suspension of flights to Riyadh until Tuesday
World.content:
Air Cairo announced the continued suspension of all flights to King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh—departing from Cairo, Assiut, and Sohag—until Tuesday, October 20, pending the resumption of normal airport operations.

The airline explained in a statement that this decision was made in coordination with the civil aviation authorities of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, in light of temporary operational measures affecting air traffic to and from the airport.

Air Cairo said that it is closely monitoring developments and advises customers with bookings for Riyadh-bound flights to contact the airline or their travel agent for the latest information regarding their reservations, and to stay updated through the company’s official announcements.

World.title: Egypt, Sudan FMs reject attempts to undermine bilateral ties, reaffirm support for Sudan’s stability
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and Sudanese Finance Minister Gibril Ibrahim reaffirmed the deep-rooted historical and fraternal ties between Egypt and Sudan, rejecting any attempts to undermine relations between the two countries and their peoples. During a meeting on Friday, October 16, 2026, on the sidelines of the World Bank’s autumn meetings in Thailand, the two ministers stressed that bilateral relations are founded on mutual respect for sovereignty and borders, as well as the principles of good neighborliness, particularly between brotherly nations.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Nader Zaki said the meeting also focused on ways to strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation in various fields in line with the shared interests and aspirations of the Egyptian and Sudanese peoples.The talks also addressed the political process and the latest developments in Sudan, Zaki added.

Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s longstanding support for Sudan’s unity, territorial integrity and state institutions, underscoring Cairo’s commitment to continued efforts to resolve the crisis and alleviate the suffering of the Sudanese people.

World.title: Finance Minister: IMF raises its forecast for Egypt’s economic growth to 4.7% in 2027
World.content:
Minister of Finance Ahmed Kouchouk said that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised its forecast for Egypt’s economic growth to 4.7 percent in 2027, up from its previous estimate of 4.4 percent.

He noted that clarity and transparency in dealings with investors increase predictability and strengthen confidence in Egypt’s economic trajectory.

Speaking during an open dialogue with international investors at two meetings hosted by JPMorgan and Bank of America on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, the Minister said, “Our economy is moving in the right direction, and indicators are improving as economic and fiscal reforms are implemented.”

“We are pursuing a balanced approach to sustain improvements and financial stability, stimulate investment, and increase production and exports,” he added.

“We have adopted a proactive approach to addressing shocks, which has received positive responses from investors and markets. We also have promising investment opportunities, along with incentives and tax and customs facilitations that support economic activity and the business community,” Kouchouk said.

He added that Egypt had achieved strong fiscal performance, supported by growth in economic activity and increased private-sector investment. The primary surplus rose to 4.9 percent, while the budget deficit fell to 5.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) during the last fiscal year.

He noted that the government’s approach of providing tax facilitation, fostering partnerships and building trust with taxpayers had helped increase voluntary compliance and boost tax revenues by approximately 27 percent, without imposing any additional burdens.

Kouchouk also pointed out that Egypt is committed to reducing the external debt of budget-sector entities by approximately one billion dollars to two billion dollars annually.

“The government also aims to diversify its funding sources and instruments and extend debt maturities to meet financing needs at the lowest possible cost and over the longest possible repayment period,” according to him.

World.title: NCW urges expanded economic empowerment, social protection
World.content:
The National Council for Women underlined the need to expand rural development and shift from direct aid to economic empowerment during a Cabinet preparatory session on Friday, October 16, 2026.

Speaking ahead of “Egypt Forum 2026” on Oct. 19–24, the NCW’s Vice President Nesreen al-Baghdadi urged greater private-sector involvement in village development and called for integrated social protection databases. She also advocated support for foster families and elderly care to strengthen family stability.

The session highlighted digital transformation, enhanced civil society coordination, and sustainable job creation to build self-reliance among vulnerable households.

World.title: FM, Syrian Finance Minister discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty had talks with Syrian Finance Minister Mohammed Yisr Barnieh on Friday, Octobor 16, 2026, on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group in Bangkok to discuss prospects for strengthening bilateral relations.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Nader Zaki said the talks focused on expanding cooperation between Egypt and Syria, particularly in the economic and financial fields.

The two ministers also reaffirmed the deep-rooted historical and fraternal ties between the two countries and their peoples. Abdelatty welcomed the successful visit of an Egyptian economic delegation to Syria, describing it as an important step toward advancing bilateral economic cooperation, Zaki added.

He also noted that preparations were underway for Abdelatty to visit Damascus in the coming period.

World.title: Curated Cultural Gifts Expands to Roberts International Airport
World.content:
Monrovia, Liberia – Curated Cultural Gifts, a Liberian-owned business founded by entrepreneur Brenda Brewer Moore, has expanded its operations with the opening of a new kiosk at Roberts International Airport (RIA), located in the Departure Hall.

Established in 2021, Curated Cultural Gifts was founded with a mission to showcase African arts and crafts, celebrate cultural heritage, and provide meaningful gifts that reflect Liberia’s rich history, creativity, and traditions.

The business currently operates a store on Old Road in Monrovia and is preparing to open another location at Kpatawee Waterfalls in Bong County.



According to founder Brenda Brewer Moore, the airport expansion represents an important opportunity to introduce Liberian and African craftsmanship to an international audience.

“Although the kiosk is a small space, we see it as a big opportunity to share our culture with the world. Our goal is to promote Liberia positively through arts and crafts while creating greater visibility and economic opportunities for local artisans,” Moore said.

Curated Cultural Gifts is also inviting talented Liberian and African artisans to submit their products for consideration as the business expands its collection of culturally inspired gifts and souvenirs.

Moore expressed appreciation to customers, partners, and supporters who have contributed to the business’s growth over the past five years.

“Every purchase, referral, and word of encouragement has helped us reach this point. We are grateful and excited about what lies ahead,” she added.

Curated Cultural Gifts continues to position itself as a destination for authentic African crafts, meaningful cultural gifts, and products that celebrate Liberia’s heritage.

World.title: Liberia: U.S. Trial of Former Army Commander Moses Wright, Linked to Lutheran Church Massacre, Postponed Until February
World.content:
U.S. Homeland security agents arrest Moses Slanger Wright at his home in Philadelphia in 2022.

Summary:

The trial of Moses Wright, 73, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of lying to immigration agents about his involvement in Liberia’s civil conflict has been postponed to February. It was set to start in November. The court has yet to give a reason for the delay.

U.S. prosecutors allege that Wright concealed his involvement in wartime atrocities when seeking immigration benefits and citizenship. He faces immigration-related charges, because the U.S. did not have laws in place to try citizens for war crimes committed in international jurisdictions when the alleged crimes took place.

Wright faces a maximum possible sentence of 165 years in prison and a US$7 million fine.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

The U.S. trial of Moses Wright, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of ordering and overseeing the 1990 St. Peter’s Lutheran Church massacre in which an estimated 600 men, women and children were killed, has been postponed again.



Wright’s trial, previously scheduled for November in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, has been rescheduled for February, the latest in a series of delays.

“We see it as a setback to our quest for justice,” said Marcus P. Quoigoah, executive director of the Lutheran Massacre Survivors Association, in a phone interview. “We are frustrated. Looking at the lives of so many that have been shattered as a result of Wright and his men, delaying this, we feel that justice is still being halted.”

The postponement comes more than 36 years after the massacre, for which no one has been criminally convicted in Liberia. It also comes as legislation to establish a War and Economic Crimes Court has stalled at the Liberian Legislature, while survivors continue to pursue accountability through legal proceedings abroad.

Wright, 73, faces federal immigration fraud and perjury charges over allegations that he concealed his involvement in atrocities during Liberia’s first civil war to obtain immigration benefits and eventually U.S. citizenship.

According to a June 2022 indictment announced by the U.S. Department of Justice , Wright allegedly committed atrocities against civilians or ordered troops under his command to carry them out, including the persecution of members of the Gio and Mano ethnic groups, murder, assault, unlawful arrests and imprisonment.

Wright is believed to be a cousin of the late President Samuel Doe, and his alleged role during the First Liberian Civil War was General Commander of the Armed Forces of Liberia, which would make him one of the most prominent figures in the conflict. Liberia’s 2009 Truth and Reconciliation Commission report also named Wright, Moses Thomas, James Chelly and George Dweh in the June 1990 massacre of 27 Gio and Mano family members of Armed Forces of Liberia personnel living at the Barclay Training Center barracks in Monrovia. The killings were carried out “reportedly under orders of Samuel Doe,” according to the report. The commission also implicated Chelly, an army captain, in military operations against civilians in Nimba County, stating that he and Edwin Voker “commanded the onslaught.”

Dweh, a senior figure in the Movement for Democracy in Liberia, rebel group who became Speaker of Liberia’s transitional legislature in 2003, died in April 2020 without facing prosecution for his alleged involvement in the massacre or other wartime abuses.

The massacre occurred in July 1990, when soldiers of the Armed Forces of Liberia attacked civilians sheltering at St. Peter’s Lutheran Church in Monrovia during the country’s first civil war. Although it is not explicitly mentioned in Wright’s indictment, he commanded the army when the massacre took place. He oversaw Moses Thomas, a more junior commander, who was found civilly liable for the massacre in a 2021 case. The court ordered him to pay $84 million in damages to four survivors and relatives of victims. He fled the United States for Liberia avoiding enforcement of the fine.

“We still hold him responsible for the over 600 lives that were murdered,” said Quoigoah. “Wright had a hand; he had a big stake in it.”

Prosecutors say Wright obtained asylum in the United States in 2000, permanent residency in 2008 and applied for citizenship in 2013. He allegedly concealed his wartime conduct during the immigration process and repeated false statements under oath during an August 2016 naturalization interview.

Wright is not being prosecuted directly for violations of international law including war crimes or crimes against humanity because of limitations in U.S. federal law. The United States enacted so-called “universal jurisdiction” laws that allow government to prosecute people for crimes committed outside the country, after the alleged atrocities in Liberia in 1990. Those laws cannot be applied retroactively to conduct that occurred before they took effect.

Instead, prosecutors have brought immigration fraud and perjury charges, an approach previously used against other Liberian war criminals, including Mohammed Jabateh and Thomas Woewiyu, who were convicted in Philadelphia in 2017 and 2018, respectively. Jabateh is serving a 30-year sentence. Woewiyu died while awaiting sentencing. In 2026 former Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy commander Layee Sekou Camara, known as during the war as “K1,” pleaded guilty after being charged with immigration offenses. He is serving a nearly five-year sentence.

Other former Liberian rebel commanders have also been deported from the United States over immigration violations linked to their wartime activities. They include George Boley, former leader of the Liberia Peace Council, who was deported in March 2012 after a U.S. immigration court found that he had engaged in extrajudicial killings and recruited and used child soldiers. Mayama Sesay, known as “Black Diamond,” a former commander of the Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy rebel group, was deported in September 2025 after an immigration judge found that she had lied about recruiting and using child soldiers during her immigration applications.

Wright has denied the charges. If convicted on all counts, he faces a maximum sentence of 165 years in prison and $7 million in fines.

The proceedings against Wright have been accompanied by security concerns involving Liberian investigators. In September, the Global Justice and Research Project, a leading Liberian war crimes investigation organization, relocated a senior investigator following repeated death threats allegedly linked to Wright’s sympathizers .

Among the survivors still seeking accountability is Rufus Kartee, 65, who says a bullet struck his left hip during the massacre, damaging the bone and leaving him dependent on a crutch for more than three decades.

A mass grave inside the compound of St. Peter’s Lutheran Church in Monrovia, where an estimated 600 people were massacred in July 1990.Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Kartee spoke to FrontPage Africa/New Narratives before undergoing surgery at the John F. Kennedy Memorial Medical Center in Monrovia this month. He said he hoped to see those responsible brought to justice before more survivors died.

“The main, main people them dying on a daily basis,” he said. “Even people from our side too are dying on a daily basis.”

Kartee said seeing alleged perpetrators face trial remains a priority.

“So, we that are alive today, if I will survive, I will still be happy to see the people going through court process.”

World.title: Gov’t of Liberia Begins Validation of Draft Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy
World.content:
— As acting Commerce Minister describes the document as an essential instrument for enterprise development, investment promotion, industrial growth, and economic diversification.

Front row: Acting Minister of Commerce and Industry Hon. Stephen Yekeson (second from left), with Mr. Emmanuel Rugomboka, Counsellor in WIPO’s Division for Africa, and Hon. Garmai Koboi, Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office.

The Government of Liberia has begun the validation of its draft National Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy (NIPPS) to guide short-, medium-, and long-term actions in the protection, administration and commercialization of intellectual property rights.



The ongoing validation exercise, which runs from October 15 to 16, comes as President Joseph Boakai’s administration has made intellectual property protection and development a key policy priority under Pillar One of the ARREST Agenda.

Opening the validation workshop, Acting Minister of Commerce and Industry Hon. Stephen Yekeson said the exercise represents a step toward a national framework that recognizes the economic value of knowledge and protects the legitimate interests of creators and innovators.

“In today’s increasingly knowledge-driven global economy, national competitiveness depends not only on the natural resources a country possesses or the goods it produces, but also on its ability to generate ideas, protect innovation, develop valuable brands, commercialize creative works, and transform knowledge into economic value,” Hon. Yekeson added.

Min. Yekeson further noted that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry sees the NIPPS as an important document that connects to Liberia’s wider trade, investment, and economic development priorities, as an effective intellectual property system is key to a more supportive business environment, encourages responsible investment, and reinforces Liberia’s broader efforts to improve trade competitiveness and private sector growth.

“Today’s validation workshop is particularly important because the success of a national policy depends not only on the quality of the document, but also on its relevance to national priorities, its responsiveness to practical challenges, and the commitment of the institutions and stakeholders responsible for its implementation,” the Minister also noted while stressing the importance of the validation exercise.

Acting Minister of Commerce and Industry Hon. Stephen Yekeson opens the validation workshop on Liberia’s draft National Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy.

The ongoing workshop, which brings together stakeholders from government circles, the creative industries, the business community, higher education institutions and civil society, is convened by the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO) in collaboration with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with technical assistance from the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

It comes after a national review of the IP Audit findings last year, which identified gaps in institutional capacity, infrastructure, coordination, and access to intellectual property services as constraints that continue to limit the use of the intellectual property system.

The draft NIPPS responds to these findings by seeking to strengthen the country’s intellectual property system and increase its usage and responsiveness. The document, which was developed by experts in intellectual property, aligns with the Government’s national development priorities in the ARREST Agenda and brings coherence to the work of LIPO and other government institutions, while positioning Liberia to take full advantage of regional and global opportunities.

Speaking earlier, LIPO Director General Hon. Garmai Koboi said the draft was made possible through high-level engagement with WIPO in order to align the country’s IP regime with international intellectual property standards and frameworks administered by WIPO, the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization (ARIPO), and others.

Hon. Koboi noted that the workshop gives stakeholders an opportunity to confirm that the draft reflects their experiences, challenge impractical measures and examine institutional responsibilities.

“We extend our profound appreciation to the World Intellectual Property Organization for its invaluable technical and financial support. This partnership reflects WIPO’s long-term commitment to helping member states build intellectual property systems that serve their development aspirations, and Liberia is proud to count WIPO among its steadfast partners,” Hon. Koboi added.

“I also recognize both the national and international consultants, whose expertise guided the preparation of this draft; the members of the Technical Steering Committee, who gave their time and recommendations; and the many institutions, enterprises, creators, and individuals who participated in the National IP Audit and the stakeholder consultations,” noted the Director General.

Also speaking, WIPO Representative Emmanuel Rugomboka, a Counsellor in the organization’s Division for Africa, said the document could help connect intellectual property protection with economic diversification, stronger local enterprises and opportunities for women and young entrepreneurs.

He illustrated this potential with a hypothetical Liberian cocoa or coffee cooperative. “Imagine a Liberian agricultural cooperative producing high-quality cocoa or coffee. With the right policy framework, the cooperative could receive support to develop a distinctive brand, protect its trademark, meet quality standards, and explore geographical indication protection where appropriate,” Mr. Rugomboka said.

“By combining intellectual property protection with improved production, processing, packaging and market access, the cooperative could differentiate its products, negotiate better prices and reach higher-value domestic and international markets,” he added. “The resulting benefits could include increased incomes for farmers, new opportunities for young entrepreneurs, and jobs in processing, packaging, marketing and distribution.”

According to Mr. Rugomboka, WIPO stood ready to support implementation of NIPPS in line with Liberia’s priorities and available resources, including efforts to help businesses build competitive brands, researchers bring discoveries to market and creators benefit from their work.

World.title: Liberia’s Science Conference Opens With Calls to Turn Research Into Action
World.content:
Researchers, health officials and partners at the opening of the 5th Emmet A. Dennis National Scientific Conference in Congo Town this week.

By Joyclyn Wea, gender and health correspondent with New Narratives

Summary:

The 5th Emmet A. Dennis National Scientific Conference opened in Monrovia this week, bringing researchers and policymakers together to examine evidence from Liberia’s health system.

Organizers said the conference is helping young scientists present and publish research. Officials promised to take its findings into health policy discussions.

Experts said new research on Ebola preparedness and previous findings on Lassa fever show why local evidence matters, and the measure of success is what changes in communities afterward.

CONGO TOWN, Monrovia — Scientists, health workers and government officials gathered for the Emmet A. Dennis National Scientific Conference, a national gathering of Liberian researchers presenting evidence they hope will shape how the country prevents disease and cares for patients. This is the fifth annual conference.



The three-day meeting at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex brings together Liberian researchers, students and health policymakers to discuss infectious diseases, maternal health, health financing, climate-related health threats and other challenges. Organizers said nearly 100 research paper summaries were submitted for the conference, with roughly 90 accepted for oral or poster presentations.

“We want to find Liberian solutions for Liberian problems and perhaps for global problems as well,” said Dr. Sia Wata Camanor, acting director general of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia, in her opening remarks.

The conference offers a snapshot of Liberia’s growing research community since the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic, the biggest outbreak anywhere of the deadly disease which left nearly 5,000 Liberians dead. Experts said it also poses a test: whether findings presented before government officials will become decisions that make health services safer and more effective for ordinary Liberians.

The Ebola epidemic exposed serious weaknesses in disease detection, laboratory testing and emergency response. Liberia established the National Public Health Institute in its wake in 2016. Two years later, the Institute and its partners launched the scientific conference, named for Dr. Emmet A. Dennis, a pioneering biomedical researcher and former University of Liberia president.

One goal was to help district and county surveillance officers turn information gathered in clinics and communities into research they could analyze, present, and publish. Another was to develop younger Liberian scientists and ensure that national health priorities were not set entirely by foreign partners.

At the opening, Camanor said the conference now connects students, universities, laboratories and public health agencies. She announced that organizers would issue a communiqué after the meeting and share it with the government, the Ministry of Health and partners.

Bode Ireti Shobayo, the Institute’s director of public health and biomedical research and chair of the conference planning committee, said selected presentations can be turned into policy briefs and scientific manuscripts. The Institute will also mentor researchers to prepare papers for international academic journals.

“We want to go beyond just presenting for presenting’s sake,” Shobayo said in an interview before the conference.

Uriah Harrington, speaking on behalf of President Joseph Boakai, said the conference is key to helping the country shift away from responding only after crises emerge.

“We must transition from reactive passive response to proactive science-driven governance,” he said. The administration pledged to support domestic research capacity, mentoring and evidence-based health policy, but the remarks did not specify new funding amounts or plans.

Partners said the success of the conferences to date could be seen in changes in Liberia’s scientific workforce. A representative of the African Field Epidemiology Network, a non-profit network that trains African health workers to be “disease detectives,” said its field epidemiology training work in Liberia has expanded since it was established in 2015 from frontline to intermediate training, with some professionals pursuing advanced courses abroad. A U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention representative said Liberian epidemiologists now lead outbreak investigations and produce their own research.

Dr. Stephen B. Kennedy, a University of Liberia researcher and Institute board chair, said Liberians have developed the skills to study infectious diseases and contribute to international vaccine research, even as shortages of money, laboratory infrastructure and supplies limit what they can do. “We have the expertise, we have the capacity.”

But the ability to present a paper is different from changing policy or action. Shobayo could not say how many recommendations from earlier editions had been adopted or provide a public record showing which decisions and services had changed.

He pointed to recent work on Lassa Fever as one example of the promise offered by Liberian researchers. A 2022 study co-authored by Shobayo found the disease appearing outside its traditional hotspots in Nimba, Bong and Grand Bassa counties and contributed to the government’s decision to expand its activities to other counties.

But some experts have questioned whether the conference’s contributions to national policy and actions have been enough. Joseph Somwarbi, a pharmacologist and former chair of the House Committee on Health, said policymakers should make those links visible to the public.

“What are the indicators?” he asked, calling for evidence of the decisions taken and benefits to affected communities.

Alpha Tamba, with the World Health Organization, urged organizers to publish the findings and make them accessible, including to the communities they are meant to serve. He said that would give health workers, journalists and residents a way to follow what happens after the speeches and presentations.

This year’s presentations included The National Public Health Institute’s nationwide Ebola preparedness assessment done earlier this year. Officials previously reported a 69 percent overall readiness score and 47 percent for logistics. The Institute has not published the detailed scoring method or facility-by-facility findings that experts said were necessary to fully interpret them. When the results were released in September, health workers welcomed the assessment but said the government needed to follow up to close the gaps to make sure they feel safe.

For three days, the conference will put Liberian evidence before people with the power to act on it. Its larger measure will come later: which recommendations the government accepts, what resources follow, and whether patients and communities can see the difference.

This story was produced in collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. The funder had no say in the story’s content.
