This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How STAMICO Revenue Rose to US$56 Million

STAMICO’s revenue was TZS 1.3 billion (about US$0.5 million) in 2018/19 and TZS 147.8 billion (about US$56.2 million) in 2025/26. That is roughly 114 times higher, by newsroom arithmetic, and both outlets give the same two figures.

In August 2023 the Daily News reported revenue of TZS 61.1 billion (about US$23.2 million) for 2022/23. It said STAMICO began paying dividends to the government: TZS 2.2 billion (about US$0.8 million), then TZS 2.5 billion (about US$0.9 million).

Conversions use TZS 2,632.01 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of Saturday 17 October 2026 (00:02 UTC). Older amounts are converted at today’s rate, so the US$ values for 2018/19 and 2022/23 are only a rough guide.

STAMICO calls its turnaround strategy “Make STAMICO Shine Again”, known as Mastasha. Dr Mwasse said the aim is to improve commercial results, attract investment and raise Tanzanians’ share of mineral wealth.

What STAMICO Owns and Builds Today

The Daily News says STAMICO fully owns three mines: the Biharamulo gold mine, the Kiwira coal mine and the Chigongwe gravel mine. Biharamulo is in Kagera Region and Chigongwe is in Dodoma Region, while the outlets give different regions for Kiwira.

Beyond mining, the corporation has built five coal briquette plants using Kiwira coal, the Daily News reports. A larger plant is complete and due to be inaugurated towards the end of October, as an alternative cooking fuel.

STAMICO also plans an industrial park at Chigongwe in Dodoma Region to make construction aggregates. It has set up a salt plant in Kilwa District, Lindi Region, and acquired 18 modern drilling rigs for exploration services.

The Daily News adds that a listing on the Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange is a long-term goal. Dr Mwasse said the corporation first needs to strengthen existing projects, consolidate reforms and improve operating capacity to attract investors.

Small-Scale Miners and the Financing Plan

The Citizen reports that small-scale miners’ share of mining sector revenue has risen from 3 percent to 40 percent. STAMICO says it wants to widen their role in mining and in mineral trading.

STAMICO is pursuing a proposal for a bank dedicated to small-scale miners, The Citizen says. Miners lack capital, geological data, technology and markets, it adds, and the idea was discussed with the Bank of Tanzania governor.

Both outlets say STAMICO works with Azania Bank, CRDB Bank and NMB Bank on miner loans. The Citizen adds that a Bank of Tanzania guarantee fund can cover 80 percent of the risk, and the miner 20 percent.

Tanzania Editors Forum chairman Deodatus Balile praised the results but urged STAMICO to use current data and strengthen research. He said Tanzania’s mineral exports averaged US$5.4 billion and that more local processing would create jobs and earn foreign exchange.

What It Means for US Readers

Neither outlet names a US company or a US government role in the three planned mines. The only foreign partner named is South Africa’s Plantcor, on the Kigosi gold licences.

STAMICO says it is seeking investment partners with capital and technology for its biggest projects. That could open Tanzanian mining deals to foreign funds, but no terms, prices or partners have been announced.

The Citizen says STAMICO holds 20 licences for strategic minerals, but neither outlet says where the graphite mine would be. Graphite buyers should treat the plan as an early signal, not a supply commitment.

Rio Times has covered the state’s other mining moves, including a push for local firms to win US$1.9 billion of mining spend. It has also covered Tanzania’s gold reserves of US$3.8 billion, held by the central bank.

What Is Not Known

The figures come from STAMICO’s own briefing as carried by The Citizen and the Daily News. The newsroom found no audited accounts, and the reports give revenue, not profit, so earnings after costs are not known.

Neither outlet gives a cost, a start date or an output target for any of the three new mines. The location of the graphite mine and the name of the second gold project were not reported.

Only The Citizen reports the 100 percent graphite ownership, the 20 licences, the 40 percent small-scale share and the 80 percent guarantee. The newsroom could not confirm these at STAMICO or the Ministry of Minerals, so they are attributed to The Citizen.

The Citizen dates the briefing 16 October, though its report of that day says “yesterday”. The Daily News of Saturday 17 October also says “yesterday”, so Friday 16 October is used, and no STAMICO release was found.

The Kiwira coal mine is placed in Songwe Region by The Citizen and Mbeya Region by the Daily News. The bank for small-scale miners is a proposal only, and no capital, owner or date has been announced.

What Comes Next

The larger briquette plant is due to be inaugurated towards the end of October, the Daily News reports. Exploration at Kigosi is due to finish soon, in the third month of its completion, according to Dr Mwasse.

No dates were given for the graphite mine, the second gold mine or a stock exchange listing. Any investment agreement would have to be announced by STAMICO or the Ministry of Minerals.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is STAMICO?

STAMICO is the State Mining Corporation, the state-owned mining firm of Tanzania, led by managing director Dr Venance Mwasse. It explores, mines, drills and trades minerals and runs coal, gold and gravel operations.

What new mines does STAMICO plan?

It plans three new mines, two for gold and one for graphite, according to the Daily News and The Citizen. Exploration is under way at the Kigosi gold project in Geita Region.

How much revenue did STAMICO report?

Revenue rose to TZS 147.8 billion (about US$56.2 million) in 2025/26 from TZS 1.3 billion (about US$0.5 million) in 2018/19. The reports give revenue, not profit.

Is a foreign company involved?

Plantcor Mining and Plant Hire of South Africa signed a cooperation agreement for the Kigosi gold licences in February 2026. STAMICO is also seeking investment partners for large projects, but names none.

Will STAMICO list on the stock exchange?

The Daily News says a Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange listing is a long-term plan. Dr Mwasse said the corporation must first strengthen its projects, reforms and operating capacity.

Sources: The Citizen, report on STAMICO’s three new mines and revenue, 16 October 2026; Daily News, STAMICO plans three new mines, 17 October 2026; Daily News, How Stamico made incredible revenue rise, 29 August 2023; TanzaniaInvest, Kigosi gold mining project agreement with Plantcor, 26 February 2026; STAMICO, corporate website; open.er-api.com exchange rates (all accessed 17 October 2026).

World.title: Mauritius Plans Nationwide Curfew Powers
World.content:
MAURITIUS · SECURITY AND LAW

Key Facts — What is happening Mauritius’ Cabinet agreed on Friday, 16 October 2026 to put a Police (Amendment) Bill to parliament that would let a curfew order cover the whole island and raise penalties for carrying an offensive weapon.

— Why it matters Curfew orders are now limited to named localities, so the bill would remove that limit after riots that began on 12 October, and it would reach residents and visitors across the island.

— The numbers Police have arrested 151 people, including 16 minors, since the riots began on 12 October, and a new curfew runs from 22:00 to 04:30 on three nights to Monday morning.

— Who is who The Commissioner of Police heads the Mauritius Police Force and makes curfew orders under the Police Act; the Cabinet is the government’s decision body, and the National Assembly must pass the bill.

— What to watch Watch for the bill’s text, the size of the new penalties and the date of the National Assembly sitting at which it is presented, none of which has been published yet.

— What it means for you US travellers on the island should follow the police and local authorities, expect night curfews through Sunday, 18 October, and check US State Department travel guidance before they fly.

Mauritius plans to let police impose a curfew across the whole country, not only in single localities. The Cabinet also approved tougher penalties for people caught outdoors with offensive weapons during a curfew.

The Mauritius nationwide curfew plan advanced on Friday, 16 October 2026. The Cabinet agreed to introduce a Police (Amendment) Bill in the National Assembly.

The bill would let the Commissioner of Police order a curfew for the whole of Mauritius instead of one locality. It follows riots that began on 12 October and matters to US travellers because it could cover the entire island.

What the Mauritius Nationwide Curfew Bill Changes

The Cabinet’s official summary says the bill amends the Police Act. A curfew order by the Commissioner of Police would no longer be limited to a locality and could cover all of Mauritius.

The bill also provides harsher penalties for anyone found outdoors with an offensive weapon in a curfew area during curfew hours. The summary gives no figures for fines or prison terms.

Defimedia, a Mauritian news site, reported the decision on Friday evening, 16 October. Le Mauricien, a Mauritian daily, followed on Saturday morning, 17 October, with the same account.

Le Mauricien adds that the current law limits a curfew to a specific locality. Both outlets say the bill will be presented to the National Assembly, which must still pass it.

The Curfew Now in Force

Separately, the Cabinet agreed to a new Curfew Order for three nights. It runs from 22:00 to 04:30 on Friday 16, Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October.

The Cabinet summary does not list the areas covered by this order. Under the law as it stands, the order must name localities.

An earlier curfew order, issued on Tuesday, 13 October, covered specific regions from 20:30 to 06:00. On Wednesday, 14 October the Cabinet agreed two more nights, from 20:30 to 05:00.

The Riots Behind the Decision

The Cabinet noted the Commissioner of Police’s report on the situation since riots broke out on 12 October. Police say 151 people have been arrested, including 16 minors.

Cases against 12 of them were lodged and they appeared in court on Friday. Three others have already been sentenced by district courts.

Seven police officers have been injured. Eight police stations were damaged, including Barkly, Abercrombie, Pointe aux Sable, Petite Riviere, Bambous, Camp Levieux, Black River and Bel Ombre.

The report also lists 31 police vehicles, 162 Safe City cameras at 75 sites and 27 traffic lights as damaged. Around 17,000 tonnes of sugar cane were burnt, and an assessment of the financial impact is under way.

A separate police case, an arrest over a WhatsApp group, is covered in Jayesh Julloo Held in Mauritius Molotov Plot. This article covers only the Cabinet decision on curfew powers.

Other Decisions From the Same Cabinet Meeting

The Cabinet examined lowering the age of criminal responsibility from 14 to 12 years but chose wider consultation instead. It agreed to a motion at the next Assembly sitting for a Select Committee on the causes of juvenile delinquency and violence.

The Cabinet also set up an Inter-Ministerial Committee on the emergency water situation, chaired by the prime minister. It revised the dates of school assessments and extended the secondary school term by three days, to end on Thursday, 5 November.

What It Means for US Readers

Mauritius is a popular holiday destination in the Indian Ocean, and visitors are subject to the same curfew orders as residents. A nationwide order would apply to every part of the island, including areas that have seen no unrest.

Travellers should follow the instructions of the police and local authorities and check US State Department guidance before they travel. Any change to flights or hotel services is a matter for airlines and operators, and none is announced in the sources.

What Is Not Known

The bill text is not in the sources, so the new penalties for carrying an offensive weapon are not known. It is also unknown which weapons count as offensive or whether exemptions would apply.

The date when the bill is presented in the National Assembly is not given, and passage is not assured. The Cabinet summary does not say whether the current curfew order covers the whole country.

The decision rests on the Cabinet’s official summary, which Defimedia and Le Mauricien repeat without further detail. No government minister or the police have been quoted on how a nationwide curfew would be used.

What Comes Next

The bill goes to the National Assembly, where members will debate it before any vote. The Select Committee on juvenile delinquency is to be proposed at the next sitting.

The current curfew order lapses at 04:30 on Monday, 19 October, unless a new one is issued. The Cabinet decision does not itself impose a nationwide curfew.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Mauritius nationwide curfew bill?

It is a Police (Amendment) Bill approved by the Cabinet on 16 October 2026. It would let the Commissioner of Police order a curfew covering the whole of Mauritius.

Is there a curfew in Mauritius now?

Yes, the Cabinet agreed a new Curfew Order from 22:00 to 04:30 on 16, 17 and 18 October. The last night ends at 04:30 on Monday, 19 October.

What are the new penalties for offensive weapons?

The bill provides harsher penalties for anyone found outdoors with an offensive weapon during a curfew. The Cabinet summary does not state the amounts or sentences.

Has the bill become law?

No, the Cabinet has only agreed to introduce it in the National Assembly. Parliament must still debate and pass it.

Does this affect US travellers in Mauritius?

A curfew applies to everyone on the island, including visitors. Travellers should follow police instructions and check US State Department guidance.

Sources: Prime Minister’s Office of Mauritius, Highlights of Cabinet Meeting, 16 October 2026; Defimedia, 16 October 2026; Le Mauricien, 17 October 2026 (all accessed 17 October 2026).

World.title: Guinea Bauxite Boss Sees US$1.2 Billion Tax
World.content:
GUINEA · BAUXITE

Key Facts — What is happening Guinean businessman Fadi Wazni said in Conakry on Friday 16 October that Guinea may export 200 million tonnes of bauxite this year, and that his alumina refinery will be ready by end 2027.

— Why it matters Guinea has mostly sold raw ore, and a local refinery would turn some of it into alumina, the step before aluminium, keeping more value at home.

— The numbers He projects US$1.2 billion in direct bauxite tax at about US$6 a tonne, plus about US$2.5 billion spent with local firms, and says three alumina refineries are under construction.

— Who is who Wazni is a private mining executive who has run Société Minière de Boké; he is not a minister, and the figures are his own estimates, not a government release.

— What to watch Watch for official 2026 export and tax figures from the mines and finance ministries, and for visible progress at the refinery site before the end 2027 target.

— What it means for you Guinea bauxite feeds the global aluminium chain that US and European buyers rely on, so a refinery or a tax change could shift where alumina is sourced.

Fadi Wazni, a Guinean mining businessman, says Guinea bauxite exports may reach 200 million tonnes this year. He also says his alumina refinery will be ready by the end of 2027.

Guinea bauxite could pay the state about US$1.2 billion in direct tax this year, businessman Fadi Wazni said on Friday 16 October. He spoke at a Conakry round table, and the figure is his own projection, not an official budget number.

Wazni also said an alumina refinery built by his group and its partners should be ready by the end of 2027. Guineenews, a Guinean news site, reported the remarks on Friday, and no government statement on them has been found.

Who Said It and Where

Guineenews calls Wazni a businessman, homme d’affaires in French, not a minister. In June 2024 it described him as head of Société Minière de Boké (SMB), which runs the Dapilon export terminal.

He spoke at the second round table of the Observatoire guinéen de conjoncture économique (OGCE), an economic monitoring forum in Conakry. Guineenews says the audience included mining industry figures, public officials and former prime minister Ahmed Tidiane Souré.

Guineenews also lists the minister of the environment and the minister of national education among those present. It does not say that any of them commented on Wazni’s figures.

The Guinea Bauxite Numbers He Gave

Wazni projected that Guinea will export about 200 million tonnes of bauxite in 2026. He said that would be more than ten times the volume of a decade ago.

Financial Afrik reported in January that official data put 2025 exports at 182.8 million tonnes, up 25% on 2024. His projection is therefore about 9% above that level, by newsroom arithmetic.

He said direct tax from bauxite could reach US$1.2 billion this year, based on an average of US$6 a tonne. The sum matches 200 million tonnes at US$6, and he said it leaves out profit tax and other corporate levies.

He added that about US$2.5 billion was spent with local companies, without saying over what period. He said direct jobs linked to bauxite could run to several hundred thousand, but that studies are still needed for precise data.

The Alumina Refinery Due by End 2027

Alumina is the white powder made from bauxite that is smelted into aluminium. Guinea has mostly sold raw ore, and a refinery would keep part of the value at home.

Wazni said three alumina refineries are under construction in Guinea, including the one built by his group and partners. He said, “we are already on site” and the refinery “will be ready at the end of 2027.”

He did not name the partners, the capacity or the cost in this speech, as reported. In June 2024 he announced a refinery beside the Dapilon port costing €1.4 billion (about US$1.6 billion), Guineenews said.

He also said his group has taken control of processing units in France. He argued that Guinean alumina could help the European Union diversify away from some Asian and Russian suppliers.

Wazni conceded that making aluminium in Guinea is harder than making alumina, because of technical and energy needs. He announced a training centre for alumina trades in Boké, called CPAF, which he said will open soon.

What It Means for US Readers

Guinea sits at the start of the aluminium chain, and its bauxite ends up in cars, cans and aircraft. A shift from raw ore to alumina could change supply routes for US and European manufacturers.

Nothing in the reported remarks involves a US company or a US policy decision. Readers should treat the tax and refinery claims as one executive’s view until the Guinean government publishes its own numbers.

Background on the country is in the Rio Times Guinea explainer. The earlier piece on Guinea’s bauxite boom covers the growth story.

What Is Not Known

This report rests on one outlet, Guineenews, whose article on Friday 16 October was updated on Saturday 17 October. No transcript, recording or government statement has been found to confirm the quotes and numbers.

The 200 million tonne forecast and the US$1.2 billion tax figure are Wazni’s estimates. Guinea’s mines and finance ministries have not published matching 2026 figures that could be found.

The refinery’s partners, capacity, financing and construction progress are not stated in the reported speech. The claim that three refineries are being built is also his, and it is not independently verified.

The US$2.5 billion of local spending has no stated period or source. Likewise the jobs estimate, which Wazni himself said needs further study.

What Comes Next

Official 2026 export and tax data from Guinea’s government would show whether the US$1.2 billion estimate holds. No release date has been announced.

The next test is the end 2027 refinery target, which has no confirmed milestone before then. The remarks do not mean that Guinea has changed its mining tax rules or its export policy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Fadi Wazni a Guinean government minister?

No, the Guineenews article calls him a businessman. He has been described as the head of the mining company SMB.

Did Guinea confirm US$1.2 billion in bauxite tax?

No, it is his own projection from 200 million tonnes at about US$6 a tonne. No official 2026 figure has been found.

When will the alumina refinery be ready?

Wazni says the end of 2027. No independent confirmation of the schedule has been found.

What is alumina?

Alumina is a refined powder made from bauxite ore. It is smelted into aluminium metal in a later step.

How much bauxite did Guinea export in 2025?

Financial Afrik reported official data of 182.8 million tonnes, up 25% on 2024. Wazni projects about 200 million tonnes for 2026.

Sources: Guineenews, 16 October 2026; Guineenews, 7 June 2024; Financial Afrik, 29 January 2026 (all accessed 17 October 2026). Conversion of the 2024 euro figure uses EUR 0.89 per US$1 (open.er-api.com, 15 October 2026).

World.title: Oyo Police Rescue Baby Sold for US$1,500
World.content:
Key Facts —Who. Oyo State Police Command in Nigeria, which rescued a one-month-old baby girl and arrested two suspects, Cecilia Amos and Dr Adeleke Ebenezer. —What. A baby allegedly sold for ₦2 million (about US$1,500) was rescued; the alleged buyer is still being sought. —Where. Ido Local Government Area, Ibadan, the capital of Oyo State in south-west Nigeria. —When. Reported to police on Thursday 15 October 2026; announced on Saturday 17 October 2026. —As of 17 October 2026, 12:45 GMT

Police in Oyo State, Nigeria, say they have rescued a one-month-old baby girl who was allegedly sold for ₦2 million (about US$1,500). Two suspects have been arrested, according to the state police command, in a case reported on Saturday 17 October 2026.

Child-trafficking cases draw close attention from US readers who follow adoption, family law and Nigeria’s large diaspora. The Oyo case began with a single complaint from a family.

What We Know

The announcement came from DSP Ayanlade, the Oyo State Police Public Relations Officer, known as the PPRO. The PPRO is the officer who speaks for the state police command in public.

BusinessDay and Blueprint, two Nigerian news outlets, carried the police statement on 17 October 2026. Both reports describe the rescue of the baby and the arrest of two suspects.

The two people arrested are Cecilia Amos, the baby’s 23-year-old mother, and Dr Adeleke Ebenezer, aged 40, who owns a health facility in Ido. Police say the baby girl was rescued, and the investigation continues.

The alleged buyer, Odunayo Folawewo, is still being sought by police. A fourth name, Hassan Oludunni, appears in the police account, but the reports do not list him among the two arrested.

Oyo State is in south-west Nigeria, and Ibadan is its capital city. Ido is a Local Government Area, the lowest tier of government in Nigeria, comparable to a county in the United States.

The Alleged Sale and the Timeline

Mary Amos, who lives in the Ogunwade area of Ido Local Government Area in Ibadan, reported the matter to police on Thursday 15 October 2026 at about 18:00. She told officers that her 23-year-old daughter, Cecilia Amos, gave birth to a baby girl on 6 September 2026 at Ebepraise Health Centre in Ido.

File photo: a road in Abuja, Nigeria. It does not show the location of the case.

According to the complaint, the daughter disappeared with the baby about seven days after the delivery. The family then raised the matter with police.

Under interrogation, Cecilia Amos allegedly confessed that Dr Ebenezer, the owner of the health facility, and Hassan Oludunni facilitated the sale of the baby to Odunayo Folawewo. These are allegations attributed to her by police, not proven facts.

The alleged price was ₦2 million (about US$1,500 at ₦1,330 per US$, the EODHD rate on 17 October 2026). The naira, written with the symbol ₦, is Nigeria’s national currency.

Police allege the money was shared out, with Cecilia Amos receiving ₦1 million (about US$750). Ebenezer and Oludunni allegedly received ₦500,000 each (about US$375 each).

These figures are the police account of the allegations, not findings of a court. Every person named is a suspect, and each is presumed innocent until a court rules otherwise.

The complaint was made on Thursday evening, 15 October. Police have not said exactly when the baby was rescued.

What Is Not Known

Police have shared the outline of the case but not its legal detail. Several important questions remain open while the investigation continues.

It is not known what formal charges will be brought, or when any suspect will appear in court. Reports also do not say which court will hear the case.

The baby’s health and where she is now being cared for have not been detailed. Out of respect for the child, this article gives no further detail about her.

Hassan Oludunni’s whereabouts are not reported, because reports name him among those accused but not among those arrested. It is also not known whether the alleged buyer, Odunayo Folawewo, has been found.

Beyond the name given by police, nothing is reported about the buyer’s identity or background. Nor is it known whether anyone else is being investigated.

Police have not given a motive beyond the allegations summarised above. This article does not speculate about the reasons behind any person’s actions.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

This is a local criminal investigation in one Nigerian state, and the police statement, as reported, does not address visitors. It will matter most to readers who follow child-protection cases in Nigeria.

Child trafficking is a criminal offence in Nigeria, and police say this case is still under investigation. Readers should wait for formal charges and court records before drawing conclusions.

Nigerians in the diaspora with relatives in Oyo State may follow the case through local outlets such as BusinessDay and Blueprint. Wider background on the country is available in the Rio Times coverage of Nigeria.

Families considering adoption from Nigeria should use only official legal channels and licensed agencies. Anyone with concerns about a child’s safety can contact the police or a recognised child-protection body.

The Oyo case began with a family complaint to police. What happens next depends on the charges and the court process, neither of which has been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened in the Oyo baby sale case?

Oyo State police say they rescued a one-month-old baby girl who was allegedly sold for ₦2 million (about US$1,500). Two suspects were arrested, and the investigation continues.

Who has been arrested in Oyo?

Police arrested Cecilia Amos, the baby’s 23-year-old mother, and Dr Adeleke Ebenezer, 40, who owns a health facility in Ido. The alleged buyer, Odunayo Folawewo, is still being sought.

How much was the baby allegedly sold for?

Police allege the sale was for ₦2 million (about US$1,500 at ₦1,330 per US$, the EODHD rate on 17 October 2026). They allege Cecilia Amos received ₦1 million (about US$750), and two others ₦500,000 each (about US$375 each).

Has anyone been convicted?

No. All those named are suspects, and a court has not ruled on the case.

Sources BusinessDay · Blueprint

World.title: What to Do in Rio in October 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro · Culture

A Leblon theatre keeps up its bossa nova weekends until 8 November, The Color Purple plays as a musical in Barra until the 25th, and the CCBB’s October programme is free. The rest of the month, day by day.

The rotunda of the Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil in Centro, where the October programme is free. (Photo: Bruna Prado)

RIO DE JANEIRO — There is a great deal to do in Rio in October, and very little of it is written down anywhere in English. This guide is the monthly selection for people who live here rather than visit: what is on, where, when, what it costs, and why it might be worth crossing the city for.

Until 8 November the Teatro Café Pequeno in Leblon keeps up its eighteen-concert bossa nova season, and until 25 October the musical A Cor Púrpura plays a short run in Barra. Here is the rest of the month.

Until 8 November: Bossa Nova Weekends in Leblon

Fridays and Saturdays 8pm, Sundays 7pm Bossa Nova Sessions at the Teatro Café Pequeno Teatro Café Pequeno, Av. Ataulfo de Paiva 269, Leblon · From R$50 (about US$10) Eighteen concerts over five weekends in the neighbourhood where the genre was born. The line-up runs from harmonica player Maurício Einhorn and singer Ithamara Koorax to guitarist Victor Biglione, who marks fifty years on stage this year — his 1995 Montreux live album, co-produced by Quincy Jones, has just been reissued. Small room, reserved tables, the most accessible October programme in the city for a listener without Portuguese.

Mid-October

Wednesdays and Thursdays, until 22 October, 7pm “Pra Quem Não Me Conhece” returns to the Laura Alvim Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Ipanema · Price from the venue Nicole Musafir’s comedy about her own life, extended after sold-out shows at its premiere. In the first run her grandmother, the pianist Lydia Musafir, played in public for the first time at 91. In Portuguese.

Until Sunday 25 October A Cor Púrpura — The Color Purple, the musical, fifth Rio season Teatro Multiplan, Shopping VillageMall, Av. das Américas 3900, Barra da Tijuca · From R$60 (about US$11) · Wednesday to Friday 8pm, Saturday 4pm and 8pm, Sunday 3.30pm and 7.30pm Fourteen performances only of the Brazilian production of the Alice Walker musical, with Suzana Santana again as Celie and Tadeu Aguiar directing. English-speaking audiences know the story from the novel and the films, which makes this the easiest musical in town to follow in Portuguese. Tickets through Sympla and the box office; every section also has a solidarity ticket at a special price against one kilo of food.

Thursdays through November, 8pm “Jazz dos Muertos” on Thursdays at La Esquina in Lapa La Esquina, Lapa · Price from the venue A new weekly jazz night in the heart of Rio’s bohemian district, built around jazz, Latin jazz, bossa nova, samba jazz and soul. It opened on 15 October with “Aura Jazz” by the Giovana Adoracion Quinteto, and the name is a playful nod to the idea that the old masters are gone but their music is still on stage. Simple to enjoy without Portuguese.

Saturday 17 October Ana Carolina, “25 Anas” tour Qualistage, Via Parque Shopping, Av. Ayrton Senna 3000, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue The singer-songwriter marks twenty-five years of career with the tour “25 Anas”.

Sunday 18 October Vanessa da Mata at Vivo Rio Vivo Rio, Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo · Price from the venue One of the defining voices of Brazilian pop of the last two decades, in the big auditorium inside the Flamengo park. Her catalogue crosses MPB, pop and reggae, and most of the room will know every word.

Its Banking segment offers various products and services, including…

Late October

Tuesday 20 October to Sunday 1 November Cine Uruguai: Novos Horizontes at CAIXA Cultural CAIXA Cultural Rio de Janeiro · Free Twenty-one Uruguayan films, sixteen features and five shorts from the last ten years, with talks and a masterclass. It opens with “Agarra-me Forte”, a Goya nominee for best Ibero-American film, and 23 October is a tribute day to the former president José “Pepe” Mujica with “Uma Noite de 12 Anos” at 2.30pm and the documentary “Os Sonhos de Pepe” at 5pm.

Thursday 22 October, 8pm Naiara Martins launches “Terras do Sem-Fim” at Acaso Cultural Acaso Cultural, Rua Vicente de Sousa 16, Botafogo · Price from the venue The singer, songwriter and literary critic, nominated for a 2024 Jabuti Prize in philosophy, presents the show built on her first album. It runs from bossa and samba to songs with words in Yoruba and Kayapó, under the musical direction of Pedro Braga.

Thursday 22 October, 8.30pm Suzy Mac presents her EP “Amor e Atitude” at the Dolores Club Dolores Club, Rua do Lavradio 10, Lapa · R\$60 (about US\$12), half-price R\$30 (about US\$6) The Brazilian-American singer released the EP on 16 October and brings it to Lapa on 22 October. Her sound mixes samba, bossa nova, soul and jazz, so the language is no barrier.

Friday 23 October John Pizzarelli at Vivo Rio Vivo Rio, Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo · Price from the venue The American jazz guitarist and singer, a regular visitor to Brazil, with the songbook between Nat King Cole and bossa nova. The month’s most expat-friendly evening in a big room.

Saturday 24 October, 8pm Black Pantera open their Brazil tour at the Circo Voador Circo Voador, Lapa · Price from the venue The trio from Uberaba, Rock Artist of the Year 2025, starts its Continental tour in Rio. Hard, political rock from the interior of Minas Gerais. Details here.

Saturday 24 October, 9.30pm Oswaldo Montenegro at the Qualistage Qualistage, Av. Ayrton Senna 3000, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue The songwriter and filmmaker with the melodic catalogue that half of Brazil grew up on. Melodic, unhurried, and a good introduction to mainstream Brazilian songwriting.

Sunday 25 October, 11am Quarteto Atlas plays Villa-Lobos string quartets in Tijuca Centro da Música Carioca Artur da Távola, Rua Conde de Bonfim 824, Tijuca · Free, tickets at the box office from one hour before Leading players from the Theatro Municipal orchestra, the Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira and the Petrobras Symphony take Heitor Villa-Lobos’s string quartets from the French-tinged No. 1 of 1915 through the folk-song No. 5 to No. 17, written two years before his death. The musicians introduce each piece in Portuguese, but the music needs no translation; the tour opens on Tuesday 20 October at 7pm at the Teatro da UFF in Icaraí, Niterói, also free.

Free at the CCBB Through October

Until Monday 19 October Soy Loco por Ti, Centroamérica — Central American cinema Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, Centro · Free Twenty-one features and shorts from Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama, most of them never before screened in Brazil, in their original languages with Portuguese subtitles. It runs three weeks into October and costs nothing.

Until 16 November Amazônicas — Poéticas Femininas Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, Centro · Free Women artists from the North of Brazil, curated by Sissa Aneleh, with Afro-indigenous ancestry at the centre and virtual- and augmented-reality elements. It runs well past the end of the month, so there is no rush.

Running All Month

Until Sunday 1 November, Fridays 8pm, Saturdays and Sundays 7pm “Heathers – O Musical” in a new Rio staging Teatro Nathalia Timberg, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue A new Brazilian staging of the Broadway musical, directed by Rafaela Amado with musical direction by Anna Hannickel. It runs on weekends from 9 October, in Portuguese.

Until Sunday 25 October, Fridays and Saturdays 7pm, Sundays 6pm “Café, Almoço, Jantar” at the Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Ipanema · Price from the venue A comedy of manners that follows one family through 1987, 1994 and 2018, three breakfast, lunch and dinner scenes in a boarding house, to show how Brazil’s politics and economy reach private life. Written by Ivan Fernandes, back for a short run after a September premiere at the CCJF.

Every Saturday, from midnight Rock-blues at the Bukowski, the oldest rock bar in the city Bar Bukowski, Rua Álvaro Ramos 270, Botafogo · R$39.90 (about US$8) at the door, free from 1am on the guest list The Saturday-night residency continues through October: the Charles Zanol Trio from midnight, with Pedro Leão on guitar and Dawton Mendes on drums and cajón. R$39.90 (about US$8) at the door includes a drink if you arrive before 10pm; R$99.90 (about US$19) gives you R$80 (about US$15) back in food and drink. Names on the guest list through @barbukowski enter free from 1am. The bar runs from 7pm to 5am.

Until 4 December The Jazz Room: a Sinatra and Armstrong tribute Teatro Rival Petrobras, Rua Álvaro Alvim 33, Cinelândia · From R$100 (about US$19) The Rival’s long-running tribute evening — the American songbook with a live band in the Art Deco theatre off Cinelândia. The reliable option when nothing else on this list fits the night.

Through October October season at the CCJF: four new exhibitions, film festivals and concerts Centro Cultural Justiça Federal, Av. Rio Branco 241, Centro · Price from the venue The federal-justice cultural center opens four exhibitions this month (word-and-image rooms, an eleven-artist audiovisual collective, a show on native bees and an artist working with state-school children), alongside theater, two film festivals with retrospectives, open-air cinema and concerts ranging from a flute orchestra to MPB choirs, opera and jazz. The full day-by-day program is on the CCJF site.

17 to 31 October, three stops “Um Rio Dentro de Mim” — the award-nominated musical tours greater Rio Madureira (17 Oct) · São João de Meriti (22 Oct) · Nova Iguaçu (31 Oct) · Price from the venue Carol Botelho and Deborah Marins sing Vinicius de Moraes and Aldir Blanc in a musical that reads as a mother’s love letter to Rio — twice nominated for the Prêmio Musical Rio and on the road through the Sesc network until the end of the month.

Football in Rio in October: The Last Clássico

Thursday 29 October, 8pm One derby left in October: Vasco against Flamengo Vasco home fixture, stadium to be confirmed · Tickets from the clubs Vasco host Flamengo on Thursday 29 October, which the Brazilian football confederation (CBF) has set for 8pm; confirm the stadium before you go. It is the last clássico of the month, so buy only through the clubs’ own sites, and go early.

Planning Your Rio in October

Sunday 25 October is the second round of the general election: the presidential race and the contest for Rio de Janeiro governor both go to a runoff, with voting from 8am to 5pm. Rio de Janeiro state did not restrict alcohol sales in the first round; check nearer the date whether that holds for the runoff.

Where we have not printed a ticket price, the organisers had not published one at the time of writing — check with the venue before you travel. Programmes at the CCBB and the theatres change during the month, so confirm on the day.

Dollar values use the RT rate of about R$5.22 to US$1 on 5 October 2026.

This guide to Rio in October runs monthly, and returns in November. If you run a venue, a gallery or a production in Rio and would like to be considered, write to the newsroom with the date, the time, the address and the ticket price.

Those four things are what get an event into the list.

World.title: Mexico Eyes US$12.5B Solar and Wind Plan
World.content:
Wind turbines at La Venta in Oaxaca, southern Mexico. (Photo: Daniel Cravioto, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

MEXICO · ENERGY

Key Facts — The country Mexico, the United States’ manufacturing neighbour, runs a power grid that has seen seasonal blackouts, most visibly in the Yucatán peninsula.

— Why it matters The government wants renewables to rise from 24% to at least 38% of electricity generation, and factories that supply US customers need steadier power.

— Why now The state utility CFE is expected to vote on Tuesday 20 October on more than 60 projects, most of them wind and solar parks.

— What happened On Wednesday 7 October CFE said it had already awarded 38 solar and wind projects in 16 states and plans 58 renewable projects of more than 10,400 megawatts in all.

— The numbers The proposed batch is put at about 8.2 gigawatts and US$12.5 billion, a figure CFE has not confirmed and that depends on transmission costs.

— What it means for you US factories in Mexico and their American customers gain if the plants arrive on time, while a smaller approval would keep blackout risk in nearshoring plans.

— Still open Whether the board votes on 20 October, how many projects win approval, and which companies are behind them.

— Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

Mexico’s state power company CFE is expected to vote on Tuesday 20 October on a solar and wind plan covering more than 60 projects, put at about US$12.5 billion. For US readers, the batch matters because factories that serve American customers depend on a grid that has suffered seasonal blackouts.

The figures come from Bloomberg, which cited one unnamed person and was carried in Spanish by El Financiero on 16 October. CFE did not answer a request for comment, so the numbers are not confirmed by the company.

What the Solar and Wind Plan Would Add

The proposed plants are mostly wind farms and solar parks, and together they would add about 8.2 gigawatts of capacity. A gigawatt is 1,000 megawatts, the standard measure of a power plant’s maximum output.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The estimated cost of US$12.5 billion depends on transmission spending, according to the same source. A second person said the number of projects that win final approval could be lower than 60.

The vote is described as a preliminary approval, not a final award. CFE has not published a project list, so the companies and sites involved are not public.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Mexico’s Government Confirmed on 7 October

CFE director Emilia Calleja told the president’s morning press conference on Wednesday 7 October that a first call for projects had already awarded 38 solar and wind plants in 16 states, from Baja California to Yucatán. She said CFE plans 58 renewable generation projects of more than 10,400 megawatts in all, including mixed schemes in which the state utility works with private developers.

We found no official statement linking the 8.2 gigawatts now described to those 58 projects or to the 38 already awarded. It is therefore unclear whether the list CFE’s board will vote on is new or largely the same group.

The awarded plants are spread across Baja California, Campeche, Coahuila, Nuevo León, Sonora, Tamaulipas, Veracruz and Yucatán, among other states. The full list covers 16 states in the north, centre and south-east of the country.

Energy Secretary Luz Elena González said the government wants renewables to rise from 24% to at least 38% of electricity generation by 2030. The plan adds about 32,000 megawatts of new capacity by 2030, and Calleja said nine more combined-cycle plants of more than 9,300 megawatts are due by then.

How Private Money Fits Into a State-Led Grid

The government says CFE must keep at least 54% of electricity generation, a commitment the energy ministry restated on 7 October. That leaves room for private firms to join new plants under mixed schemes with the state utility.

The approach is a change from the previous government of Andrés Manuel López Obrador, which largely restricted foreign investment in the sector. President Claudia Sheinbaum has kept the state at the centre while inviting private companies back in.

Our earlier report on Mexico Throws Open Its Power Grid to Private Renewables explains the first round of the mixed model. Our report on Mexico’s State Power Firm Charts US$39.8 Billion Power Expansion Through 2030 sets out the utility’s own spending plan.

Why Mexico’s Grid Needs the Power

Years of weak investment left Mexico with too few power plants and transmission lines, and blackouts have hit the Yucatán peninsula in the hot, humid months. Our report on Mexico Blackouts Hit Yucatán Businesses as CFE Restores Power After ‘Vandalism’ covers an earlier outage there.

The ministry says the state is spending about 1.17 trillion pesos (about US$63 billion) on generation, transmission, distribution and gas pipelines. That includes 161 billion pesos (about US$8.7 billion) for transmission lines, converted at Banxico’s reference rate of 18.493 pesos per dollar for 16 October.

What It Means for You

US manufacturers with plants in Mexico, and the American firms that buy from them, gain if more power reaches industrial regions on time. Delays would keep blackout risk in the planning of nearshoring projects, a theme our guide to Mexico nearshoring explores.

Investors should watch the 20 October vote and any CFE statement rather than the first headlines, because the board may approve fewer projects than reported. Readers in the Yucatán peninsula, including Mérida, should not expect the new plants to change this year’s grid, since approved projects still have to be built.

Our Mexico economy outlook and the guide to Mexico in North America show how energy fits into US-Mexico trade. For another US-Mexico story this week, see Sonora Cattle Exports Halt After 1 Lesion.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether CFE’s board will vote on 20 October as planned, because the date comes from one unnamed person and the company has not confirmed it. It is also not known which companies submitted the projects or how many will win approval.

The US$12.5 billion total depends on transmission costs that have not been published, and we found no official document listing the projects. Whether the 8.2 gigawatts are new or part of the 58 projects CFE described on 7 October also remains unconfirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Mexico’s solar and wind plan?

CFE is expected to vote on 20 October on more than 60 mostly solar and wind projects worth about US$12.5 billion. The figures come from one unnamed source and CFE has not confirmed them.

How much power would the projects add?

The projects would add about 8.2 gigawatts of capacity, according to the report. CFE separately said on 7 October that it plans 58 renewable projects of more than 10,400 megawatts in all.

Who controls Mexico’s electricity?

CFE, the state utility, must keep at least 54% of generation, and private firms can join through mixed schemes. Energy Secretary Luz Elena González and CFE director Emilia Calleja presented the plans on 7 October.

Why does Mexico need more power?

Years of low investment left too few plants and transmission lines, and blackouts have hit the Yucatán peninsula. The government wants renewables to reach at least 38% of generation, up from 24% today.

What does this mean for US readers?

US factories in Mexico and their American customers depend on steady power. A smaller approval or a delay would keep blackout risk in nearshoring plans.

Sources: El Financiero, 16 October 2026 (Bloomberg report); Infobae, 7 October 2026 (press conference); Tiempo, 7 October 2026.

World.title: Vance Visit to Chile Eyed for Late November
World.content:
La Moneda, the presidential palace in Santiago, Chile, seat of the government that would receive a Vance visit. (Photo: Jaime Soto Ceura, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CHILE · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → — The country Chile is a copper-exporting democracy in South America, led by conservative President José Antonio Kast, whose government has moved closer to Washington.

— Why it matters A Vance visit would be the highest-level US trip to Chile of President Donald Trump’s second term, and it would test ties over security, China and the Strait of Magellan.

— Why now The plan surfaced on 16 October, after Argentine media described a Vance stop in Buenos Aires on 1 October.

— What happened Sources close to the preparations place a Chile stop in the third or fourth week of November, but neither La Moneda nor the White House has confirmed it.

— The numbers It would be the first visit by a sitting US vice president to Chile since Mike Pence in August 2017, and the Argentine leg is planned for two to three days.

— What it means for you A confirmed visit would show how far Washington leans on Chile for security cooperation and critical minerals, though nothing is official yet.

— Still open Whether Chile is confirmed, the exact dates, and whether Brazil, Peru, Ecuador or Colombia join the itinerary.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

A Vance visit to Chile is being prepared for the second half of November, according to the Chilean outlets Meganoticias and Ex-Ante, but it is not confirmed. Neither the Chilean government nor the White House has confirmed the trip, and the dates could still change.

For US readers, it would be the highest-level trip to Chile by an official of the second Trump administration, Meganoticias said. Vice President JD Vance is preparing his first tour of South America, and the Argentine government is already making ready for the Buenos Aires stop.

What the Reports Say About the Trip

Meganoticias reported on 16 October that Vance is preparing a first South American tour for November and that Chile is among the destinations, citing sources close to the planning. Ex-Ante, a Chilean political news site, wrote the same day that senior government sources describe advanced talks between the governments of Kast and Trump.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Both outlets place a Chile stop in the second half of November, and Meganoticias points to the third or fourth week. Argentine government sources expect Vance in Buenos Aires in the third week of November for two to three days, Diario de Cuyo and Infobae said.

The trip is being handled with great secrecy for security reasons, so sources expect confirmation only at the last minute, Meganoticias said. The State Department announced on 16 October that Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau and Juan Pablo Segura, the assistant secretary for Western Hemisphere affairs, will visit Paraguay and Argentina between 19 and 26 October, Infobae reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Chile Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why a Vance Visit to Chile Would Matter

Meganoticias attributes the interest to the political closeness of the Kast government, and Ex-Ante says the trip would seal a rapprochement that cooled under former President Gabriel Boric. Chile joined the US-led Shield of the Americas, a regional crime-fighting coordination group, on 22 September, as covered in Chile Joins US-Led Crime Coalition and Drops Observer Role.

Both outlets say the sensitive items could also come up, including that pact, which the opposition and former presidents Boric and Bachelet have criticised, and Chile’s ties with China, its largest trading partner. Kast has said the pact means no loss of sovereignty and no treaty, Infobae reported on 25 September.

Washington has also raised concerns about the proposed Chile-China Express undersea cable over security and critical infrastructure, Emol reported on 7 October. Our report Chinese Undersea Cable to Chile Still Under Review Despite US Objections covers where that review stands.

The Strait of Magellan Row Before the Trip

The reports land during a diplomatic spat over remarks by the US ambassador in Santiago, Brandon Judd, at a trade event hosted by the shipping company CSAV. Judd said that if Chile wants help protecting its rights over the Strait of Magellan, it must also work with the United States on issues that matter to Washington, CNN Chile and Emol reported.

Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna replied that the strait “was, is and will always be Chilean” and that Chile does not need anyone’s support to defend its sovereignty. Judd later said his words were taken out of context and that he did not condition Chilean sovereignty, as covered in US Envoy to Chile Clarifies Magellan Strait Remark.

Fourteen opposition lawmakers wrote to the foreign minister asking that Judd be declared persona non grata, El Desconcierto said. The sources do not say whether the government has answered that request.

The Argentina Leg Comes First

Argentina is the stop that Argentine media treat as settled, with a meeting between Vance and President Javier Milei at the Casa Rosada, the presidential palace, as the centrepiece. Milei’s government wants Argentina admitted to the US Visa Waiver Program, which Chile already belongs to, Meganoticias and Diario de Cuyo said.

The visit would come as Argentina’s central bank rebuilds its reserves, with US$642 million of dollar purchases in the week to 16 October, as covered in Argentina Central Bank Buys US$642M in Week. Press reports of the bank’s daily data put gross reserves at US$50.236 billion at the close of that week.

Forbes Argentina listed trade, finance, energy, security, investment and infrastructure as topics of the bilateral agenda on 1 October. Milei’s contact with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on trade and investment is covered in Milei Rubio Call Covers Trade on 16 October.

Other Possible Stops

Meganoticias lists Brazil as a possible stop that depends on the 25 October runoff, because a win by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, whom Trump has backed, would make a visit to the new government more likely. Peru, Ecuador and Colombia, which are also in the Shield of the Americas, are mentioned as other options.

Canal 9 Bío Bío Televisión noted that Rubio spent a week in Peru, Ecuador and Colombia in September. The last sitting US vice president to visit Chile was Mike Pence in August 2017, when he met then-President Michelle Bachelet, Meganoticias recalled.

What It Means for You

For US investors and companies in Chile, a confirmed visit would signal that Washington is putting security and economic ties with the Kast government first, including the Shield of the Americas. Infobae said that framework also covers critical-minerals supply chains and digital infrastructure, and the resource base is described in Chile Natural Resources Explained 2026.

Travellers and expats should treat the November dates as provisional, because the plan is unconfirmed and Meganoticias says confirmation may come at the last minute. The wider setting is in Chile Geopolitics Explained 2026 and the Santiago City Guide for Expats and Visitors.

What Is Not Known

No official source has confirmed the Chile leg, the dates or the agenda, and the reports rest on unnamed sources close to the planning. Meganoticias speaks of the third or fourth week and Ex-Ante of the second half of November, and the White House has published no schedule.

It is not known whether Brazil, Peru, Ecuador or Colombia will be added, or whether the Magellan row will change the programme. What Chile would ask for and what Washington would ask on China are not stated in the reports.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is JD Vance visiting Chile?

It is not confirmed. Chilean media report that he is preparing a first South American tour for November and that Chile is under consideration.

When would the visit take place?

Sources point to the second half of November, and Meganoticias cites the third or fourth week. No official date exists.

Which other countries would Vance visit?

Argentina is the stop being prepared by the Argentine government, with a meeting with President Milei. Brazil, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia are mentioned as possible additions.

Why would Vance visit Chile?

Sources cite the closeness of the Kast government to Washington, with security, economic ties, the Shield of the Americas and China as topics. Neither government has published an agenda.

When did a US vice president last visit Chile?

Mike Pence visited Santiago in August 2017 and met then-President Michelle Bachelet. Meganoticias recalled that he was the last sitting vice president to do so.

Sources: Meganoticias, 16 October 2026; Ex-Ante via T13, 16 October 2026; El Desconcierto, 16 October 2026; Canal 9 Bío Bío Televisión, 16 October 2026; Diario de Cuyo, 13 October 2026; Forbes Argentina, 1 October 2026; Emol, 7 October 2026; CNN Chile, 7 October 2026; Infobae, 25 September 2026; Infobae, 16 October 2026; iProfesional, 16 October 2026. The Chile leg rests on unnamed sources and is not officially confirmed.

World.title: Costa Rica Searches Guácimo Farm for the Bodies of 10 Missing People
World.content:
Costa Rican investigators spent today searching a remote farm in Guácimo, in the Caribbean area of Limón, for the remains of at least 10 people reported missing from the area. The property belongs to a man arrested in September on suspicion of belonging to a criminal group tied to a drug-trafficking figure killed by police in July.

Agents from the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) in Pococí searched seven homes and the surrounding land in Carambola, about 15 kilometers (9 miles) from central Guácimo. Prosecutors from the Pococí office, led by Deputy Prosecutor José Mena, took part in the operation.

Dogs trained to find human remains swept the property, which sits in an isolated area of banana plantations. The OIJ said the search followed confidential tips and other investigative work suggesting the bodies of the missing people could be buried on the farm. The agency said that hypothesis still has to be confirmed through judicial proceedings.

As of this afternoon, authorities had not reported finding any remains or making any arrests. The missing people are residents of Pococí and Guácimo. The OIJ has not released their names, how long they have been missing or the circumstances of their disappearances.

The farm belongs to a man with the last name of Cortés Hernández. He was arrested in September along with a man known as “Coco Cigarros,” whom police describe as the contraband chief of an organization linked to alias “Coco Guácimo.” Neither man has been convicted. Authorities have not said whether all seven homes searched Thursday are connected to Cortés Hernández.

Coco Guácimo, identified by authorities as Roney José Ríos Oconitrillo, was shot and killed by OIJ tactical agents in July during the operation that ended with the capture of Alejandro Arias Monge, alias “Diablo,” who had spent a decade as our most wanted fugitive. The Diablo investigation has since reached into institutions in the area. As an example, in September, two Pococí judges and a judicial agent were detained on suspicion of links to the network.

The OIJ asked anyone with information about the missing people to call its confidential line at 800-8000-645.

World.title: Flood alert issued across Belize as heavy rainfall threatens rivers and low-lying areas; 2 – 4 inches of rain possible over some areas
World.content:
Flood alert issued across Belize as heavy rainfall threatens rivers and low-lying areas; 2 – 4 inches of rain possible over some areas

By Hugh O’Brien: A flood alert across Belize has been issued as additional rainfall is expected to affect the country over the weekend.

According to the National Meteorological Service (NMS) in the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change, rainfall forecasts of “2 – 4 inches are possible over portions of Belize during the next four days”.

Residents in low-lying, flood-prone and riverside communities especially are advised to remain alert and to closely monitor official weather and flood updates as conditions may change rapidly.

During periods of heavy rainfall, the NMS advises caution “near rivers, streams, low-level crossings and other flood-prone areas” and residents are advised “to not attempt to cross flooded roads or waterways”.

According to the NMS, “several rivers are currently at normal or below-normal levels”. However, additional rainfall could cause smaller streams and tributaries to rise quickly, while larger river systems may respond more gradually as rainfall accumulates. Particular attention is being urged for rivers that are already elevated or approaching bankfull levels.

In its latest weather forecast, the NMS reported that in the north, rivers are near or below normal. In the west, the Mopan River, in particular, has shown a moderate increase in water level, but remain near or below normal. The Belize River is “above normal levels at More Tomorrow” but further downstream toward the coast, and at the Crooked Tree Lagoon, levels are below normal.

In the south, the Sittee River is rising toward bankfull levels and is a cause for concern for increased flooding. The Gales Point Lagoon, Moho River, Temash River and Sarstoon are rising above normal levels

Despite the current conditions in the nation’s rivers, the NMS warns that further rainfall could lead to rapid changes, particularly in smaller waterways and areas that are already vulnerable to flooding.

The NMS says it will continue to monitor rainfall and river conditions and that the flood outlook may be updated if forecast conditions or field observations change.

World.title: Police seek public’s help to identify two-year-old girl found in Belize City
World.content:
Police seek public’s help to identify two-year-old girl found in Belize City

UPDATE: The 2-year-old girl has been reunited with her parents.

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department is appealing to the public for assistance in identifying a two-year-old girl who was found on Carissa Street in Belama Phase Two, Belize City, on Friday, October 16, 2026.
