The ruling BJP and opposition leaders on Saturday traded sharp remarks over the use of the phrase âregime changeâ during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with the Congress defending peaceful protests and the BJP accusing the Opposition of attempting to create political instability.Union minister and BJP leader Pralhad Joshi criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his support for student activist Neha Bora, who referred to the Gen Z movement in Bangladesh. Joshi asserted that India's constitutional democracy could not be destabilised along the lines of Bangladesh, Pakistan or Nepal.Speaking to reporters, Joshi questioned the Congress's association with those drawing inspiration from the Bangladesh uprising."Unlike Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Nepal, this cannot happen in India. Neha Bora has said, 'Bangladesh has inspired us.' What does that mean? What happened in Bangladesh? First of all, an elected government was overthrown, and the sitting Prime Minister was forced to flee. Then, a huge number of minority Hindus are being killed. Do you want that model? And Rahul Gandhi is constantly associating with her? What are you expecting to happen in this country?" Joshi said.He also urged the Congress to strengthen its grassroots presence instead of blaming Prime Minister Narendra Modi for its electoral setbacks, citing the party's record in several states."If you want to fight elections, if you want to occupy the chair of either the Prime Minister or a Chief Minister, you have to work. Look, you haven't won in Tamil Nadu for 49 years. Back then, the BJPâs presence was very meagre, yet even at that time, you lost. You have been losing Gujarat for the past 30 years... in Madhya Pradesh for 25 years. You are losing in Bihar. In Jharkhand, you are non-existent. And all that happened before our rise, before Modi came to power. So this is completely foolish logic," he said.Joshi added that the low turnout at recent Opposition demonstrations showed that people had rejected its narrative.The controversy intensified after defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday accused the Congress and its allies of attempting to bring about a change of government along the lines of Bangladesh by using the energy of young people to spread âanarchyâ.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Singh said democracy did not give anyone the licence to create disorder or undermine the credibility of constitutional institutions.âIt appears that the Congress and its political allies, directly and through their supporting organisations, are trying to use the energy of the youth to fuel political confrontation and spread anarchy instead of channelling it towards constructive work and nation-building,â he said.âThe youth of the country are being made pawns in the politics of anarchy,â Singh added, alleging that the Congress and its allies wanted a change of government on the lines of Bangladesh.Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal hit back at Singh on Saturday, arguing that it was the people who wanted a change of government and that the current dispensation's time in office was over.In a post on X, Sibal said, âRajnath Singh: You allege that Congress wants 'regime change' the Bangladesh route. No. People want 'regime change'.ââProtests with the slogan 'India against corruption' brought you power. Then: You embraced corruption; captured institutions; manipulated voters list. Time to go!â the Independent MP said.Senior Congress leader and former Union minister P Chidambaram also defended the phrase, saying the Opposition's responsibility was to challenge the government politically, scrutinise it in Parliament and seek to replace it through elections.In a post on X, Chidambaram questioned the BJP's reaction to the expression and said, âWhy is the BJP apoplectic with feigned rage on the use of the phrase 'regime change'?'Regime change' is normal in a democracy. The duty of the Opposition is to 'oppose, expose and depose' the government Which means: oppose in politics, expose in Parliament and depose through elections,â he wrote.The row began after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan described the ongoing agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as a âfight for regime changeâ, while Bora referred to the Gen Z movement in Bangladesh.The BJP interpreted the remarks as evidence of an attempt to remove the Narendra Modi government outside the electoral process. The Opposition rejected the allegation, maintaining that peaceful protests against an elected government and efforts to replace it through elections were legitimate democratic activities.BJP MP Rajeev Chandrasekhar also criticised Sibal over his remarks, rejecting allegations of vote manipulation and accusing the Opposition of spreading misinformation.In a post on X, Chandrasekhar said:"No one is going anywhere , just bcoz u want it @KapilSibal. No Anarchist peddling a regime change narrative will prevail. Not even with your enthusiastic support. No one bought your âZero lossâ theory some years ago. You know how that titanic sank or shd we replay that? No sane Indian buys your current silly propaganda of vote manipulation thats more consistent with your earlier Zero loss type fraud than any reality or truth. A well heeled Supreme Court lawyer shdnt delude himself into believing hes an arbiter of Democracy nor his dubious posse of Marxist Leninists.Voters in India are only ones who can decide who they will elect. Judiciary can determine Election petitions. Thats the way Democracy functions.The reason the govt u were in, was thrown out in 2014 is because VOTERS ie Citizens threw you out for your corruption. I didnt hear you huff and puff abt EVMs, Voter lists or other things you trot out now.Politics of Anarchy, Lies and Dividing people will never prevail over the collective resolve of a strong, developed India with equality of opportunity for all.So give it a rest. Save your energy for your advocacy. Not wild allegations and misinformation."The exchange comes amid protests in the national capital over alleged irregularities in the electoral process and broader questions raised by Opposition leaders about the conduct of elections.While BJP leaders have accused the Opposition of using the protests to encourage unrest, Congress leaders have defended the right to protest and argued that governments can be changed through democratic means.

World.title: Sanjay Raut submits explanation in SC contempt case, says ‘we expect justice’
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(UBT) MP

on Saturday said he respected the

and would continue to seek justice from it, after the apex court issued show-cause notices to him and journalist Nikhil Wagle over remarks targeting

Chief Justice of India

(CJI) Surya Kant and the judiciary.

âThe Supreme Court is the highest court in the country. When it delivers a judgment, whether we agree with it or not, we say that it is the court's decision and must be respected,â Raut said in Thane.

He added that if the Supreme Court or any other court believed someone's remarks amounted to contempt, it was their duty to respect the court and apologise.

âBut what wrong have I said? Many people have previously spoken about judges travelling to London, but it has now been revealed that the claim was false.

No one had earlier clarified or explained this to you. We have now submitted an explanation regarding our conduct,â Raut said.

He reiterated that his party respected the Supreme Court and expected justice from it, alleging that the Shiv Sena and its election symbol had been taken away from his faction.

âOur party, Shiv Sena, and its symbol were stolen from us. For four to four-and-a-half years, we have been waiting for justice at the Supreme Court's doors.





Two Election Commissioners and four Chief Justices have changed, but we are still not getting justice. We will continue to appeal for justice before you,â he said.

SC issues show-cause notices to Raut, Wagle

The Supreme Court on Friday issued show-cause notices to Raut and Wagle, asking why criminal contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them over their remarks targeting the CJI and the judiciary.

âWhen personal liberty or any rights are jeopardised, each one of them has, in the past also, come to the court seeking rescue.

Probably the courts have never lagged behind in protecting those rights. And if the same people condemn, criticise, take the courts left and right, it is very unfortunate. Very, very unfortunate,â CJI Kant observed.

âMay better sense prevail. We can only pray,â he added.

World.title: DMK seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, rules out joint protests with Congress
World.content:
CHENNAI: Escalating its attack on the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the DMK parliamentary party meeting on Saturday adopted a resolution demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an investigation into his role.

It also resolved to support the CJP's protest demanding Kumar's immediate removal and the withdrawal of the SIR, and condemned the police crackdown on youth protesters at Jantar Mantar.

The DMK launched a sharp attack on its former ally, Congress, branding it a âhabitual backstabberâ that takes credit for others' work and betrays its allies. These positions were part of four resolutions adopted at the meeting chaired by DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin at the party headquarters, Arivalayam.

The party declared that it would not join any joint political action with Congress, accusing it of âdouble standardsâ for opposing the SIR at the national level while remaining silent on its selective impact across states. The DMK cited the deletion of more than 97 lakh voters from Tamil Nadu's electoral rolls during the revision exercise.

The DMK also accused Vijay's TVK of double standards, citing reports linking voter deletions in Tamil Nadu to the party's electoral gains. It questioned TVK chief and chief minister C Joseph Vijay's refusal to criticise the BJP or Gyanesh Kumar and alleged an âunder-the-table nexusâ between the ruling party in Tamil Nadu and the BJP-led dispensation at the Centre.

World.title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
World.content:
âBefore the dhak begins: The money and machinery behind a Durga pujoâ

The quiet work before the dhak

The budget

The pandal takes the biggest share

The idol costs a fifth

A theme, decided half a year early

Two months, or more

Six months, one theme, lakhs of rupees

Where the money comes from

The people who are paid

What it costs to raise a Durga Pujo

What the numbers leave out

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Everything, from beginning to end

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the cost of a medium-scale Durga Puja should be capped to keep it accessible? Yes, absolutely! No, let it vary based on demand. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Long before the first beat of the dhak, a Durga Pujo has already been decided, priced and partly built. The goddess arrives in autumn, but the people who bring her to a neighbourhood start months earlier, with a theme, a budget and a list of permissions that must be collected one office at a time.To the crowds who walk through a pandal's gates, a pujo is a few days of colour, light and sound. To the club that puts it up, it is a yearly project that runs on money raised from the neighbourhood, a small circle of skilled craftsmen and a large number of people who all have to be in the right place on the right day. In West Bengal that project is repeated in locality after locality, each with its own ledger.The ledger is not small. A medium-scale pujo costs several lakh rupees, and the biggest share does not go to the idol at the centre of it all. It goes to the structure built around her. Most visitors never see the figures, the deadlines or the people behind them, and that is exactly how the organisers want it. A pujo is meant to arrive as a finished thing.Nirmal, a pujo organiser from West Bengal who has run one for the past 10 years, knows that ledger well. "A medium scale pujo in West Bengal would cost somewhere between 10 to 15 lakhs," he says. "Every year the budget increases as per the market inflation."That second sentence matters as much as the first. A committee that spent a certain amount last year should expect to spend more this year on the same pujo, before it adds a single new ambition. For a club working with money collected from its neighbours, the target keeps moving upward, and the neighbours are asked to keep up with it.Ask him what costs the most and the answer is immediate. "The pandal costs the most," he says. Not the lighting, not the idol, not the food. He puts the pandal at around Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for a medium-scale pujo, which makes it the line the rest of the budget has to work around.Next to the pandal, the idol is a modest line. "Whatever the pandal costs, the idol costs its one-fifth," Nirmal says. For a medium-scale pujo, that works out to around Rs 80,000.It is a striking ratio. The figure at the heart of the festival, the one every visitor has come to see, costs a fraction of the structure that shelters her.Within the idol's cost, the most expensive element is gold. Certain gold items are designated for it, among them an ornament that is given by the club organising the pujo. The ornament comes from the organisers themselves, which makes it a different kind of expense from the rest.A pandal needs a theme, and the theme needs time. "The theme is decided at least six months ago," Nirmal says, meaning at least six months before the pujo. That is a long lead for a festival that lasts only days.Who decides it varies. In some committees, he says, there is a specific person whose sole job is deciding the theme. In others, the pandal makers can decide it too. The choice matters for more than looks, because the budget is also decided through the theme. Once the idea is fixed, the cost of building it can be worked out, and the money follows.This is why the calendar starts so early. A theme chosen six months out leaves room to price the work, find the right artisan and settle the budget before construction begins. By the time the neighbourhood sees the first bamboo go up, the important decisions have already been made.Construction is where the calendar turns uncertain. Asked how long a medium-scale pandal takes to build, Nirmal is candid. "It depends on the workers, to be honest," he says. "Some can build the same pandal in two months, whereas some will require more time."The reason, as he describes it, is a shortage of skill. "The skilled pandal makers are not a lot in number. Mostly there is just one skilled artisan and a lot of people work under him."That structure explains a good deal. The quality of the pandal and the speed at which it rises rest heavily on one person, with a large crew following his lead. For an organiser, choosing a pandal maker is therefore as much a scheduling decision as a financial one. A maker who is slow, or one who is booked elsewhere, can put the whole timeline at risk.The funding model is local. "Every area or colony has a designated club which builds a pandal," Nirmal explains. "And then they get chanda, donations, s that ultimately make the pujo what it is."There is also help from the state. This year, he says, the West Bengal government is providing Rs 1 lakh to small-scale pujos, and electricity is completely free. Free power removes a bill that would otherwise sit beside the lighting and the pandal. The Rs 1 lakh grant, though, is meant for small-scale pujos. Set against a medium-scale budget of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh, most of the money still has to come from the neighbourhood, from donors and from advertisers.Some costs are smaller but just as fixed. The priest's expenditure, Nirmal says, is around Rs 30,000 to Rs 40,000. The dhaki, whose drumming is as much a part of the pujo as the idol, is paid around Rs 10,000. On top of that, he gets free food, lodging and clothes.Those extras are part of the arrangement. A dhaki who is housed and fed for the duration of the pujo is a cost the committee carries beyond the headline fee. Nirmal was also asked about bhog expenditure, but his answer covered only the priest and the dhaki.Add up the lines Nirmal named, the pandal, the idol, the priest and the dhaki, and the total lands somewhere between roughly Rs 4.2 lakh and Rs 6.3 lakh. His estimate for the whole pujo is Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh.The gap is considerable. It covers everything else a pujo needs, including the lighting and food he named only to rule them out as the biggest expense. Nirmal did not break down how that money is divided.Asked about the biggest challenge organisers face, Nirmal does not name a single expense. "The biggest challenge is that everything from the beginning to the end is completed properly," he says.That includes permissions. "You have to get proper permissions like the police and the fire department," he says, "and it takes a lot of people to complete a pujo and to make a pujo what it is."The pandal maker and his crew, the artisan working on the idol, the priest, the dhaki and the club members collecting funds are all working towards the same date. Seen this way, the Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh is only part of what a pujo demands. The rest is coordination, and much of Nirmal's decade in the job has gone into it.For the people who walk through the gates, the pujo arrives as a finished thing. For the club behind it, it began at least six months earlier with a decision about a theme, and it will begin again next year at a higher cost.

World.title: Argentina team visit row: Keralam govt. seeks Governor’s approval to file case against V. Abdurahiman
World.content:
The Keralam government has sought the Governor’s permission to register a case against former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman in connection with the allegations linked to the proposed visit of Lionel Messi and the Argentina national football team to the State.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan handed over the file to the Lok Bhavan on Friday (October 16, 2026).

The special investigation team (SIT) tasked with probing the allegations over the proposed visit had reportedly detected serious procedural violations and recommended action against Mr. Abdurahiman under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Findings in report

The report also contained findings against members of the former Minister’s office and others involved in arranging the visit. The SIT had probed allegations that the tendering procedures were not adhered to in granting sponsorship rights to Reporter Broadcasting Company (RBC) for the Argentina team’s proposed visit.

The SIT found that the former Minister and his staff allegedly intervened to secure undue financial advantage to the sponsor.

The State government’s move has coincided with the Union government’s decision to replace Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar with Om Prakash Mathur as Governor of Keralam. Mr. Mathur is expected to take over on October 23, Lok Bhavan sources said. Mr. Arlekar, who has taken charge as the full-time Governor of Tamil Nadu on October 15, will be in Keralam till October 22. If he does not take a decision on the Keralam government’s request, it will be left to the new Governor to take a call on it.

World.title: Forum proposes draft Bill seeking protection for advocates, their kin, staff in Keralam
World.content:
A draft Bill is being mooted by the Kerala High Court Advocates Association (KHCAA) to protect advocates and their family members or staff from assault, criminal force, intimidation and threats while discharging their professional duties.

The Keralam Advocates Protection Bill, 2021, proposes a punishment of imprisonment up to five years and a fine of ₹1 lakh. The Bill also states that a person convicted of committing an act of violence against advocates, their family or staff members will be liable to pay compensation as determined by the jurisdictional court.

An act of violence committed under the Bill would be treated as a non-bailable offence. Advocates, their family members, or staff members should immediately register a first information report (FIR), to be investigated by a police officer no less than a Superintendent of Police. Any advocate under threat of being a victim should be provided with necessary police protection for their life and property, it has been proposed.

Immediate trigger

Though lawyers have been demanding a legislation for their protection for a long time, the recent death of an advocate’s father, reportedly in an attack against the advocate for wanting to represent the estranged wife of one of the accused in a matrimonial dispute case in Kochi, served as the immediate trigger for the draft legislation.

The draft Bill, which was sent to all the advocates’ associations in the State, has proposed that the investigation in the cases shall be completed within 90 days of registration of the FIR. Every offence punishable under the Act shall be a compoundable one by the aggrieved person with the court’s permission. The court shall take into account damage or loss caused to the property of any advocate or their family members or staff while granting permission for compounding the offence, it has been proposed.

Any repeated offence by a person convicted under the Act shall attract a jail term up to 10 years and a fine not less than ₹2 lakh.

Any malicious prosecution initiated against an advocate shall be treated as an offence of prohibited act under the Act and the court concerned shall forward the matter to the police for registration of an FIR, it has suggested.

The KHCAA would convene a meeting next week to finalise the draft and forward it to the State government, sources said.

World.title: Kerala State Biodiversity Board submits policy document to mitigate threats due to invasive  species
World.content:
The Kerala State Biodiversity Board (KSBB) has come up with a seven-point strategic plan to mitigate the impacts of invasive alien species (IAS) on the State’s biodiversity.

The policy document drawn up by the board, which was recently submitted to the State government, has suggested laying emphasise on prevention and monitoring of the spread of invasive alien species and generating public awareness and capacity-building to handle the menace.

The document calls for strict quarantine measures; public awareness and capacity building; conducting risk assessments and prioritising research on invasive alien species impacts; managing of invasive alien species, which prioritises prevention, engaging local communities; and scientific identification and taxonomic validation, which lays thrust on developing methods to verify species’ invasiveness. The document also suggests economic utilisation of invasive species in instances where eradication is not feasible.

Invasive fish

A total of 32 alien species, including four plants and 28 fish species, have been documented in Keralam’s inland aquatic ecosystems. The most widespread invasive fish is the Mozambique tilapia, which is found in all 44 rivers, 18 reservoirs, and two lakes, according to the document.

The invasive species in forest ecosystems include species such as Chromolaena odorata, Lantana camara, and Mikania micrantha. These species hinder the regeneration of native plant species, leading to altered ecosystems and biodiversity loss, it notes.

The document also talks about alien invasive insect pests, which are a major concern in the State’s agriculture, causing crop damage, among others. Intentional ways of introduction of these species occur via aquaculture, ornamental trade, or agriculture, while the unintentional ways include ballast water, nursery trade, or natural disasters like floods, the document suggests.

It points out that the major pathways in Keralam include ballast water, ornamental trade, and horticulture and agriculture.

KSSB chairperson N. Anil Kumar says that the invasive species deeply affected the ecosystem by eliminating the native species.

‘Strong measures required’

“The invasive species spread fast, are competitive, and have huge ramifications on ecology and native species. The naturalised biodiversity gets disrupted as they spread rapidly, and costs much to remove them. Strong measures need to be taken to prevent the spread of these species,” says Mr. Anil Kumar.

Former Kerala Forest Research Institute director K.V. Sankaran suggests an exclusive legal framework to mitigate the threats due to invasive species.

No study

“The initiative has to come from the Union government. No study has been carried out to ascertain the native species lost to the invasive species,” says Mr. Sankaran, who is also the co-ordinating lead author of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services.

“A unified government system dedicated to addressing the invasive species is crucial,” he adds.

A recommendation to develop a policy to mitigate threats from invasive alien species was provided to the Ministry of Forests, Environment and Climate Change by the Zoological Survey of India based on discussions during a national conference on invasive species last year, he says.

World.title: Tamil Nadu rice mill owners urge public not to resort to panic buying amid shortage rumours
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Rice Mill Owners Association has urged the public not to resort to panic buying of rice due to rumours circulating on social media regarding a shortage in the State.

During a press meet held in Madurai on Sunday, association leaders clarified while there had been a reduction in cultivation caused by the Super El Niño effect, the situation is not alarming and adequate reserves remain in stock.

Association president M.R. Dinesh Singh explained that the generally preferred fine-quality rice (sannarisi)—which is minimally cultivated within Tamil Nadu and mostly procured from neighbouring states like Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka—has seen lower yields due to changing climatic patterns driven by the El Niño effect.

“It is true that the prices have gone up specifically for the fine rice quality, but other varieties like ‘ganaragam’ remain the same,” he added.

However, Mr. Singh clarified the elevated prices are expected to decrease gradually following positive cultivation outcomes in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, as well as the upcoming North-East monsoon.

“Though the Kuruvai cultivation is a failure this year, these positive developments will definitely control the prices before January,” he said.

As cultivation was affected and shortage indicators emerged, traders and farmers began purchasing rice in large numbers from neighbouring states, which subsequently triggered high demand and price increases, he observed.

To counter such challenges in future, Mr. Singh said the Tamil Nadu government—which, according to him, has not taken active steps toward promoting the cultivation of fine-quality rice varieties locally—should initiate research and development efforts to boost the State production.

“As people 15 years ago moved largely from coarse varieties to fine-quality rice varieties, the cultivation in the State could not match the need. This caused the import from neighbouring States,” he recalled.

Once fine varieties start growing successfully on Tamil Nadu land, the State can effectively manage any future shortages or scarcities, he said.

Another major demand raised by the association was the provision of adequate facilities for farmers to dry their paddy and store it for future usage.

Mr. Singh alleged although farmers are levied a 1% service tax, market committees are failing to provide sufficient facilities to store their produce.

“When this is provided and the tax is collected, it will be beneficial for the farmers and buyers too. Now the tax collected is an extra burden on the farmers,” he said.

K. Rajendran, secretary of the association, speaking on promoting the cultivation of fine-quality varieties in Tamil Nadu, stated that the government through agricultural institutions should start research on developing drought-resistant fine varieties.

“This should also include finding the right places like along the Cauvery delta regions, providing incentives and subsidies to farmers to cultivate fine-quality rice, akin to Andhra Pradesh,” he said.

Mr. Rajendran urged the public not to hoard rice, emphasising the panic created by social media influencers is fake and that sufficient buffer stocks are currently available.

World.title: BJP in Karnataka to lay siege to police stations and offices of SPs if filing of FIRs against its workers continues
World.content:
BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra on Sunday said the BJP had decided to lay siege to police stations as well as the offices of Superintendents of Police if the government continued to file FIRs against party workers with respect to the Form 7 issue.

Briefing presspersons after a meeting of the party’s State core committee in the presence of the newly appointed co in-charge Kasam Venkateshwarlu, he said the Congress government in Karnataka had created confusion with respect to SIR in general and Form 7 in particular. He said the High Court of Karnataka had pulled up the State government with respect to the filing of FIRs against BJP workers.

He said the party core committee had opposed the decision of the government to extend power to issue permanent residential certificate with respect to SIR to even Panchayat Development Officers and Municipal Commissioners.

Arguing that such a power should be vested only with officers of the grade of tahsildars and above, he said the party would write to the government seeking withdrawal of such powers, besides drawing the Election Commission of India’s attention in this regard.

He said the core committee had expressed a view that the party should field its candidate in the forthcoming Assembly byelection by taking its coalition partner, the JD(S), into confidence.

He urged the government to desist from putting off the elections to rural local bodies. The core committee had decided to appoint an in-charge leader for every district to monitor the party’s preparations for the taluk and the zilla panchayat polls. In addition to this, a poll management committee would also be set up in every district, as per instructions of the core committee, he said.

A meeting of the party State office-bearers was also held on the occasion.

World.title: Telangana to seek special financial package from Centre to tackle potential El Nino impact: Ponguleti
World.content:
A State delegation led by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will meet the Prime Minister and other Union Ministers in New Delhi to seek a special financial package to address the potential impact of El Nino on Telangana, Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said on Sunday.

Speaking at a meeting in Kusumanchi after distributing Kalyana Lakshmi cheques to beneficiaries, the Minister said the delegation would submit a representation seeking adequate financial assistance and additional workdays under the VB-G RAM G Scheme.

Citing the anticipated intensification of El Nino conditions, Mr. Reddy urged farmers to avoid taking up a second crop in view of the potential impact of El Nino.

He said the State government was making efforts to save the first crop already cultivated and appealed to farmers to follow official advisories.

On the power situation, the Minister said electricity was becoming difficult to procure, even at ₹15 per unit, compared with ₹7-8 per unit earlier. He attributed the situation to prevailing “power shortages” in the country.

He directed the officials to take advance measures to prevent drinking water shortages in the coming months in view of depleting groundwater levels.

Earlier, the Minister laid foundation stones for several development works in the mandal, including an overhead water tank, pipelines and BT roads.

World.title: Madras HC directs officials to decide on Kalingarayan Canal water release within two weeks
World.content:
The Madras High Court has directed the Erode district administration and the Water Resources Department (WRD) to decide within two weeks on a petition seeking the release of water into the Kalingarayan Canal, after hearing the views of other parties drawing water from the Bhavanisagar Dam.

Justice P.T. Asha passed the orders on October 15 on a petition filed by S. Palanikumar, president of Kalingarayan Mathagu Pasana Vivasayigal Sabai No. 4. A copy of the order was available on Saturday (October 17, 2026).

According to the association, the Kalingarayan Canal irrigates 15,743 acres in Erode district. Water has not been released into the canal during the regular irrigation season this year because of renovation works, leaving standing crops under stress.

During 2026-27, without considering the impact of El Niño, 8.812 tmc ft of water was released from the Bhavanisagar Dam to the Thadapalli and Arakkankottai canals for 120 days, from April 27 to August 24, for the first crop season, the association said. It alleged that 3.14 tmc ft of water was released from the Kundah hydropower stations and the Bhavanisagar Dam into the Lower Bhavani Project (LBP) Canal for special irrigation between August 15 and September 1, 2026, without a Government Order.

Citing Public Works Department Government Order No. 2647 dated November 2, 1966, the association said water should be supplied to the Kalingarayan Canal continuously for 320 days, from June 16 to April 30, every year. It also alleged that the water released into the Kalingarayan Canal for 15 days, from July 14 to 28, did not reach tail-end farmers at Chitta Pulla Palayam.

The association said it had petitioned the district administration and the Water Resources Department on September 1 seeking the release of water. As no action was taken, it approached the High Court to protect the standing crops. Citing the availability of water in the Bhavanisagar Dam and satisfactory rainfall in the Nilgiris hills, the association urged the authorities to release water into the canal immediately.

World.title: ‘Take action against police personnel using fake social media accounts to post objectionable comments against dept. and higher-ups’
World.content:
The Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority has urged the Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP) to issue strict directions prohibiting the police personnel from operating fake or anonymous social media accounts to post derogatory comments against government decisions, departmental orders and senior officers.

In a letter dated October 15, the authority’s member Mohan Kumar Danappa said some police officers and personnel were allegedly concealing their identities by using fictitious names, including those of freedom fighters, to post objectionable and negative comments on various social media platforms.

He said such accounts were being used to criticise government decisions, departmental orders, circulars and official directives issued by senior police officers. Some personnel were also allegedly posting abusive and defamatory content, commenting on the social media posts of the Chief Minister, Ministers, elected representatives and official government accounts, and disclosing internal departmental issues in public.

Mr. Danappa termed these activities unauthorised and contrary to conduct rules, calling for the issue to be treated seriously.

The authority has called for the Social Media Monitoring cell to keep track of such activities and initiate suo motu cases against personnel who post such objectionable, defamatory or derogatory comments.

The letter urged the department to initiate stringent disciplinary action under relevant rules and provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and other laws against personnel found engaging in such activities.

World.title: Any miscalculation by adversaries will invite response beyond their ‘imagination, calculation’, warns CNSC
World.content:
Commander National Strategic Command (CNSC) General Aamer Raza warned the country’s adversaries on Saturday that “any miscalculation will be met with a response far beyond the imagination or the calculation of the initiator”.

“To those who harbour hostile designs across our borders, our stance remains resolute and unambiguous. There is no space for conflict or war in a nuclearised environment and any miscalculation will be met with a response far beyond the imagination or calculation of the initiator,” warned the commander of Pakistan’s strategic command.

Addressing the passing-out parade of cadets of the 154th Long Course at the Pakistan Military Academy (PMA), Kakul, he reiterated that the country’s armed forces stood ready to “defend every inch of the motherland” at all costs.

The warning by the strategic command commander comes after provocative remarks by Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. He had warned Pakistan on Thursday that any “fresh terrorist activity from across the border would invite a strike even bigger than the last time”, according to Indian news agency ANI.

Gen Raza said that in the “post-truth era”, the country’s adversaries sought to drive a wedge between the people of Pakistan and its armed forces through “calculated disinformation and narrative warfare”.

He elaborated that following the failure of Operation Sindoor, the adversaries sought to “fracture Pakistan’s social cohesion and state infrastructure” through an escalation of proxy terrorism and sub-conventional warfare.

Gen Raza further said that hostile elements continue to attempt to exploit the country’s internal vulnerabilities to “cultivate proxy instruments against our national unity”.

“You must understand unequivocally that this conflict is waged directly against the security of our people and the freedom secured by the supreme sacrifices of our predecessors.”

The strategic command commander added that the people of Pakistan must remain acutely mindful that safeguarding the country’s unity, sovereign integrity and territorial inviolability is “an absolute imperative, which we shall uphold at all costs and under every circumstance”.

Addressing the newly-graduated cadets, he added that they must remain steadfast in their duty and unwavering in their resolve and “immune to malicious propaganda and narrative warfare”.

Pakistan’s role in regional peace

Gen Raza said the recent shifts in global geopolitics, particularly amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East, had “once again underscored Pakistan’s pivotal strategic importance on the international stage”.

“Our decisive role in restoring regional stability, exemplified by the landmark Islamabad Accord, demonstrates our enduring commitment to peace and diplomacy,” he said, adding that the Makkah Accord was “a sequel to the same vision of durable peace”.

Expressing solidarity with the Palestinian people, he said: “Our hearts remain heavily burdened by the ongoing tragedy in Palestine, where innocent men, women and children continue to endure unspeakable hardship and systematic oppression.”

He said the Pakistani nation stood “resolute and unwavering in its diplomatic, moral and political support” for the Palestinians.

“The persistent violence, targeting of non-combatants and destruction of civilian infrastructure are profound violations of international law and a grave stain on the collective conscience of humanity,” Gen Raza added.

“Today, the world witnesses increasing volatility, where grey-zone warfare and hybrid threats attempt to destabilise sovereign states,” he added.

FO condemns Singh’s ‘provocative remarks’

A day earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) condemned Singh’s “provocative remarks” threatening aggression against Pakistan, saying such statements highlighting the neighbouring country’s “hegemonistic mindset”.

“Pakistan rejects and condemns the Indian defence minister’s provocative remarks entailing a threat of Indian aggression against Pakistan. Such reckless statements reflect India’s hegemonistic mindset and the risk its belligerent posture poses to regional peace and stability in South Asia,” FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said.

“We wish to remind India of the consequences of its military aggression in May last year, when Pakistan demonstrated both its capability and resolve to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and gave a befitting response and reply to Indian aggression,” he said, referring to the brief military conflict between the two countries.

He said that there should be “no ambiguity” that Pakistan remained fully prepared to safeguard its “sovereignty and territorial integrity” against any “ill-advised aggression”.

Haider said Pakistan’s “restraint and commitment to peace” should not be mistaken for weakness, warning that any aggression would be met with a “forceful response”.

“India should draw an appropriate lesson from last year’s experience and abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric and act with responsibility for lasting peace in the region,” he said.

World.title: Minister rebukes JUI-F chief for seeking ‘share’ in KP governance after imposition of governor’s rule, emergency
World.content:
State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on Saturday rebuked Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman for reportedly seeking his “share” in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province.

Addressing the media in Jaranwala, Chaudhry emphasised that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was not a political move aimed at strengthening the PML-N’s presence in the province by dismissing the PTI-led government.

“This was an administrative setup,” he said, adding that it had been formed with a “one-point agenda: combating terrorism”.

“I am upset. We did not expect Maulana sahab […] to consider this as spoils of war and seek his share in the absence of a PTI government in the province,” Chaudhry said.

“This is not spoils of war,” he reiterated, adding that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was an “immensely responsible” decision taken after every other option had been considered.

He said the federal government had no intention of establishing a political setup in KP.

“I am unable to understand why Maulana sahab says that he was forced to accept defeat [in elections],” he said, arguing that Fazl’s party had been defeated by the PTI in KP and the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party in Balochistan.

Chaudhry said the JUI-F was worthy of respect only if it stood by Pakistan’s interests.

The state minister also rejected the impression that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule was aimed at taking control of KP’s natural resources.

He also criticised Fazl for bringing up the 1971 separation of East Pakistan — now Bangladesh — from Pakistan in his recent statements.

“You bring up 1971 after losing the 2024 elections,” Chaudhry said.

“This KP setup is not about distributing shares, forming coalitions and governments, or engaging in politics,” he stressed, clarifying that only one member of the KP Advisory Council has a political background, as she represents the families of martyrs.

Chaudhry again offered to implement the National Action Plan and combat terrorism jointly with all stakeholders. “Politics is possible only where there is peace,” he said.

At the outset of his address, Chaudhry reiterated that there must be “a relationship or a mutual interest arrangement between the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the PTI”.

“Since 2015, no PTI leader, gathering or member has been targeted by terrorists,” Chaudhry said. “On the other hand, over the past 11 years, no political or religious party, security force, public office, funeral or wedding has been spared terrorist attacks.”

He said the federal government had exhausted all avenues to bring together stakeholders and urge them to condemn terrorism by naming those involved, whether the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), or groups funded by India or Afghanistan.

The state minister claimed that in 2013, when the government decided to hold talks with the TTP and representatives were proposed by both sides, the TTP had nominated PTI founder Imran Khan to its committee.

He also alleged that the PTI founder had allowed the TTP to open offices in Peshawar.

During his address, Chaudhry also criticised the PTI, showing a press release issued by the TTP, that condemned the dismissal of the party’s government.

Speaking at a press conference in Sialkot, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said that the sacrifices made by the security forces, officers, and the public in the fight against terrorism were “matchless”. Criticising the JUI-F chief, Asif said that he constantly targeted the country’s security forces.

The defence minister referred to Fazl’s accusations that the emergency and governor’s rule was imposed to capture KP’s mineral resources, saying that he had shared a full list of people who had the mining contracts in KP.

Asif maintained that the whole PTI and opposition leadership was engaged by the government before the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule.

“But it was fruitless,” he said.

“The situation will improve in KP […] parliament can roll back the decision of imposing the emergency only if the improvement of the situation in the province is guaranteed,” the defence minister said.

He said that some individuals in KP were expecting to get a share in the administrative changes in the province.

“We will ensure free and fair elections. Whenever the time comes, everybody can take part in it,” he said.

A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had also said that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship,” Naqvi alleged while speaking to journalists in Lahore.

He was seemingly referring to Fazl who has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP.

This politician, Naqvi said, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”.

“These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged.

He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced.

Naqvi’s remarks came days after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan.

In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations.

And after the federal government imposed governor’s rule in KP, Fazl accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediation.

On Thursday, Fazl again censured the Centre, accusing it of depriving the provinces of their rights. Addressing a rally in Multan, he further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into KP after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018.

“We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger.

Raising doubts over the Centre’s reasoning behind imposing governor’s rule that there was a lack of cooperation on counterterrorism, he said the security situation in Balochistan was worse than it was in KP.

He alleged governor’s rule was not imposed in Balochistan because the province’s chief minister “praises you”.

Naqvi further said KP was facing serious security challenges, and called on political leaders to play a constructive role in restoring peace and combating terrorism.

“Instead of fanning the flames and creating unrest, political leaders should play their role in restoring law and order and eliminating terrorism,” he said, maintaining that the province needed peace, stability and collective efforts rather than political confrontation.

Separately, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz railed against Fazl in a post on X.

She said it was not expected of a senior politician such as him to support those who facilitate terrorism — an apparent reference to the PTI, which the Centre accuses of backing terrorism.

She added it was unfortunate that he was supporting the party instead of “holding those accountable who were responsible for the ruin of KP because of their incompetence, ineptitude and corruption”.

She also criticised Fazl for his remarks about Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, seemingly referring to his comments during the Multan address about the centralisation of power.

She concluded her statement by saying that no one but the PTI was “responsible for the end of its government in KP”.

World.title: Armed men abduct 20 under-training police personnel in Mastung: officials
World.content:
QUETTA: Unidentified armed men kidnapped 20 police recruits undergoing training at the Kalat Police Training Centre while they were travelling in a passenger van along the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Mastung district, officials said.

A senior Balochistan government official confirmed the abduction to Dawn on condition of anonymity, saying the recruits were heading home for the weekend when armed men intercepted their van.

“Yes, 20 police personnel who were going home for the weekend were taken away by armed men while they were travelling in a passenger van on the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Mastung,” the official said.

He said a group of armed men riding motorcycles and carrying automatic weapons intercepted the van and took the recruits away along with the vehicle to an undisclosed location. The armed men, however, released the driver and three other passengers travelling in the van.

Police officials in Mastung also confirmed the abduction, saying the recruits belonged to the Levies Force, which has since been merged with the police.

The abducted personnel belonged to the Rakhshan division, government officials said.

Security forces have launched a search operation in the nearby mountains to trace the abducted recruits. However, no information about their whereabouts has emerged so far.

No group has claimed responsibility for the abduction.

A day earlier, Rakhshan Division Commissioner Asad Ullah Kakar was abducted in Balochistan’s Kharan district.

In a separate incident, Kharan Deputy Commissioner Munir Ahmed Soomro was released safely on Oct 3 after nearly two weeks in captivity following negotiations between local tribal elders and the armed men who had abducted him from the Noshki-Kharan highway the previous month.

On July 21, three excise officials were kidnapped after an attack on a checkpost in Balochistan’s Chagai district.

World.title: Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said on Saturday, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”.

Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour.

“Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican.

The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”.

“He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment,” the Vatican said.

The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square.

But in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis, similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli, have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms.

The Vatican’s press office said that Leo celebrated Mass on Saturday, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital where he has been recovering.

Up in air

News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.

But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take.

Flowers, candles and a picture of Pope Leo XIV are laid at the statue of John Paul II outside the Gemelli University Hospital, where Pope Leo XIV is recovering after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, in Rome, Italy on October 17, 2026. — AFP

Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky. Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

Pope watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors.

Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20.

The pope himself announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed.

World.title: Egypt's President Sisi pledges to leave office when term ends in 2030
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as “completely settled”.

Sisi, 71, a former army general who became president in 2014, made the remarks at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy in the New Administrative Capital, one of his flagship megaprojects.

Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution “would not be touched”.

“The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive. This is completely settled and there will be no discussion about it,” he said.

The Egyptian constitution, approved in 2014 following the 2013 military ouster of late president Mohamed Morsi, originally limited presidents to two four-year terms.

Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term.

Under those amendments, Sisi was re-elected in 2023 for a six-year term that is due to expire in 2030.

Critics and opposition figures have speculated about the possibility of further constitutional changes that could allow him to remain in office beyond 2030.

Before running for president, Sisi denied having political ambitions, but he resigned from his position as defence minister in 2014 and entered the race he went on to win.

On Saturday, he said the run-up to 2030 would be used to groom a new generation of leaders, with the Military Academy training hundreds of prospective officials, ministers and presidential candidates in statecraft and leadership.

During his 12 years in power, Sisi has overseen an ambitious state-led development programme centred on megaprojects which critics say have relied heavily on borrowing and contributed to Egypt’s mounting debt burden and economic pressures.

Sisi’s presidency has also faced sustained criticism from international human rights organisations over restrictions on political opposition, civil society and freedom of expression, allegations the government rejects, saying its policies are necessary to preserve stability and security.

World.title: Pakistan has enough energy supplies to last through November, planning for winter spike: Aurangzeb
World.content:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Saturday told AFP that Pakistan had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices due to the US-Israeli war on Iran, but that attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were “worrying” for the country’s longer-term economic outlook.

In an interview on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Aurangzeb said the country had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike.

“The first-order impact has been negotiated well by Pakistan,” he said.

“We’ve had no shortage, no queues at the gas stations, and no law and order situation, which at times we have seen in some of the countries.”

He added that unless the government saw “an absolute dire need”, it would not be procuring spot cargoes on the LNG front, which tend to be far more expensive than previously contracted shipments.

Since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, global energy prices have surged as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies.

With Yemen’s civil war flaring back to life as well, the Houthis there have repeatedly attacked Saudi infrastructure, including energy facilities and airports, in recent days.

Aurangzeb expressed alarm at the escalation, saying damage to such sites would delay a return to economic normalcy.

“What is now [the] worrying part of it is when the energy infrastructure starts getting hit,” he said.

“I, to be very honest, I don’t know where that would go. But one thing is very clear: that if the infrastructure continues to get hit, the return to normalcy, even if things subside, will take longer.”

Pakistan has been a frequent customer at the IMF, the lender of last resort to countries on the brink of default.

It is currently in the midst of its 25th programme with the Fund — at least 11 of which have been outright bailouts — since gaining independence in 1947.

With global debt stocks running high, the IMF has called at this year’s annual meetings on all economies, even those most vulnerable to the Iran war shock, to engage in fiscal consolidation to avoid a potential crisis.

“Fortunately for us, we have been on this fiscal consolidation path for a while,” Aurangzeb said with a rueful smile.

The country’s tax revenues have grown significantly in recent years, and the finance minister said the government was targeting the theft of taxes by private sector businesses that collected sales tax from consumers but never deposited it in government accounts.

Such theft accounted for billions of dollars, Aurangzeb said, adding that there remained “room for improvement” on increasing income tax collection as well.

He said the government’s reform agenda had faced resistance from industry, lobbying groups and vested interests.

“Every reform, everything that you try to do when you try to change the status quo, there is pushback,” he said.

The minister is leading Pakistan’s delegation and is holding high-level engagements with international financial institutions, finance ministers, policymakers and investors.

Yesterday, he met World Bank Group President Ajay Banga at a dinner hosted by the Thai prime minister on the sidelines of the annual meetings, state-run Pakistan TV reported.

“The occasion provided an opportunity for informal interaction alongside the high-level engagements at the annual meetings”, it said.

Pakistan remains engaged with the IMF under a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).

World.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
World.content:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine.

The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.

The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — had allowed Trump the authority to impose duties up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.

The legislation, which Trump signed into law last month, targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials, as well as Moscow’s so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent Western sanctions.

Trump’s reversal on the Russia sanctions comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel into global markets.

The US president’s war in Iran has sparked crippling oil shortages and price spikes, creating major headwinds for his Republican Party ahead of midterm elections next month.

Asked if he was being made a scapegoat for Trump’s domestic woes ahead of the vote, Zelensky just smiled.

“This is my answer,” he told journalists in Brussels, after an extended pause.

In another sign of strained relations between the United States and Ukraine, Trump branded Kyiv’s actions a “disgrace” after Zelensky ordered his forces to resume strikes on Russian refineries.

“I defend the interests of Ukraine and the Ukrainian people exclusively,” Zelensky said after talks with EU leaders.

The breakdown between Trump and Zelensky has fuelled fears that the US leader is siding with Moscow.

Those concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine’s ability to counter Russia’s intense bombardments.

Ukraine uses technology from Elon Musk’s SpaceX for battlefield communications, but the tech billionaire — a virulent Zelensky critic — said his company was not behind the disruption, while a US official denied any intervention by Trump.

European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky as he grappled with Trump.

“This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” European Council chief Antonio Costa said.

“Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.”

Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that “the situation in Ukraine is currently truly dire, with numerous Russian attacks and a tense relationship between Ukraine and the US.”

“It is crucial that we, as Europe, demonstrate our unconditional support for them today — and explore what additional steps we can take,” he said.

Zelensky asked the bloc — Ukraine’s biggest international backer — to provide more Patriot missiles to shoot down Russian missiles and come up with an extra 70 billion euros ($79 billion) in support next year to help Kyiv keep fighting.

Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter, when temperatures can plummet to as low as -20°C and Moscow’s attacks threaten electricity, heating and water systems.

Russian strikes on the southern cities of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia killed a 64-year-old man and at least 17 people, including an 11-year-old girl, Ukrainian authorities said Saturday.

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen confirmed that Zelensky’s 70-billion euro plea “has to be covered” and urged partner countries to “step in” and help.

French President Emmanuel Macron said Kyiv’s backers will analyse the demand, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the European Union will discuss it before the end of the year.

The EU is currently paying out instalments of a 90-billion-euro loan for Kyiv that was set to help cover funding to the end of 2027.

But Ukrainian authorities have warned they will still face a major budget black hole as Russian strikes have battered the country’s economy.

The talks on new funding have reignited calls for the EU to tap around 200 billion euros in frozen Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine.

“The frozen assets are there. That’s what should be used for supporting Ukraine,” said Latvian premier Andris Kulbergs.

But there seems little momentum on that front as Belgium, where most of the funds are held, remains opposed.

World.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder arrested after detention, media reports say
World.content:
Police arrested Indian “cockroach” movement founder Abhijeet Dipke, according to several media reports on Saturday, after he was ​detained on Friday ahead of a Delhi rally that drew hundreds of people ‌waving the national flag and demanding the resignation of India’s election chief.

Dipke was arrested to prevent a breach of the peace and will be called before a Special Executive Magistrate on Saturday, broadcasters NDTV and ​India Today said.

Delhi police did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.

The ​youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), opposition groups and student organisations have held near-daily protests ⁠this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over a revision of voter lists that ​they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted ​during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Student activist Neha ​Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she ​tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.

“Please, spare the people of India. ‌Impeach ⁠Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured,” Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of ​a house in central ​Delhi, with police hauling ⁠him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument.

Dipke had called Friday’s protest in support of two CJP leaders detained ​and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at ​a protest ⁠site in violation of a ban.

Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced ⁠by ​Modi and the BJP in the prime minister’s 12 ​years in power.

A weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the movement earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over ​exam paper leaks.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters.
