At the same time, Pashazade supported the government’s position. He said the school uniform regulations do not mention the word “hijab” and that the country has no ban on wearing it. Children can study in hijabs at madrasas, he added, “but a different decision was taken regarding state schools”.

The Sheikh-ul-Islam stressed that “religion is separate from the state, and school is separate from religion”. He also accused certain “internal and external forces” of politicising the issue and trying to turn citizens against the state.

Araz Aliyev sees Pashazade’s statement as evidence that the authorities made the decision hastily:

“If the decision had been carefully considered and prepared over many years, the authorities should have consulted someone. It appears they made the decision in haste.”

For more on the legal aspects of the hijab ban, protests at schools and detentions, see JAMnews’ earlier report.

How will relations develop?

None of the experts interviewed expects Azerbaijan and Turkey to break off their alliance. However, they all believe the chill between the two countries will persist for some time.

Araz Aliyev believes the tensions will remain at the political level and gradually ease:

“Turkey needs Azerbaijan, while Azerbaijan needs Turkey even more in terms of national security, the economy and defence. Companies close to the leadership in both countries may face pressure from one another, but I do not believe their alliance will be threatened. After some time, we will hear declarations of brotherhood again.”

He notes that the two countries have weathered similar crises in the past. In particular, tensions in the late 2000s, when Turkey and Armenia were discussing protocols to normalise relations, led to Turkish flags being taken down in Baku. Aliyev believes the summit of the Organisation of Turkic States, which is expected to take place in Turkey at the end of the month, could indicate the direction in which relations between Baku and Ankara will develop.

Gergerlioğlu also does not expect Erdoğan to distance himself from Baku solely over the hijab issue. He says Ankara places much greater importance on revenue from the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline, Turkey’s ambition to play a leading role in the “Turkic world” and the support of its nationalist-conservative electorate.

“Behind closed doors, they will probably say politely: ‘Wouldn’t it have been better not to introduce such a ban?’ However, if Aliyev begins openly supporting Israel, Turkey will also start signalling its discontent with the relationship more openly.”

The MP also points to declining electoral support for the ruling party. He claims that some voters dissatisfied with the AKP’s “two-faced” policy towards Israel backed the New Welfare Party in the last election. In his view, the hijab issue could deepen this discontent further.

Javid Agha reaches a similar conclusion. He believes that no matter how often Erdoğan repeats the slogan “one nation, two states”, he will have to take into account the views of the religious-conservative electorate that forms the foundation of his political support and adjust his position accordingly.

Fidan’s statements in Baku also offer insight into this diplomatic strategy. Ankara does not deny that problems exist, but seeks to move discussions about them out of the public arena and into closed-door diplomatic channels. So far, however, there are no signs that Baku intends to make concessions either on the hijab issue or on its relations with Israel.

Strained relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan

World.title: Millions spent on Patriarch’s funeral: scandal involving Georgia’s former culture minister Tinatin Rukhadze
World.content:
Scandal involving former officials in Georgia

On 14 October 2026, Davit Okitashvili, a supporter of the Georgian Dream party, publicly accused former Culture Minister Tinatin Rukhadze of misusing funds allocated for the funeral of the Patriarch of Georgia and called on the prosecutor’s office to launch an investigation. Okitashvili also criticised former State Security Service chief Mamuka Mdinaradze, whom he described as Rukhadze’s political patron.

Other Georgian Dream supporters also responded to Okitashvili’s allegations. Opposition figures believe such attacks on former senior officials may be intended to pave the way for their arrests.

How much did the Patriarch’s funeral cost?

Patriarch Ilia II was buried on 22 March 2026. The government allocated a total of 5.59 million lari to organise the funeral, distributing the funds among six government agencies. The largest share — 3 million lari — went to the Ministry of Culture, which Tinatin Rukhadze headed at the time.

It later emerged that the authorities had not spent more than half of the allocated funds. On 8 May, the government revised the funding to reflect actual expenditure, reducing the total to 2.56 million lari.

Georgian minister quits politics shortly after ex-PM’s accusations

From ‘crown prince’ to prisoner: Irakli Garibashvili’s break with Georgia’s ruling party

Patriarch’s funeral: farewell ceremony of unprecedented scale in Tbilisi. Photos/videos

The Ministry of Culture spent just 722,600 lari of the 3 million lari originally allocated to it. The remaining 2.28 million lari went unspent.

However, it remains unclear exactly how the ministry spent the 722,600 lari: who received the money, what services they provided and how transparently the ministry selected contractors.

September: first questions and the prime minister’s response

Questions about spending on the Patriarch’s funeral emerged in September, following an investigative report by the Pirveli television channel.

Acting Culture Minister Mikheil Kiknadze initially said that the audit documents reflected the shortcomings investigators had identified. However, he later added: “I did not say that there had been any violations.”

Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also commented on the issue on 14 September. He said the Ministry of Culture had spent only 722,000 lari of the 3 million lari allocated to it.

“If anyone had wanted to steal the money, they could easily have taken all three million,” Kobakhidze said.

He also made the following promise:

“This is preliminary information. I will examine the matter in greater detail and provide the public with a detailed account.”

The Patriarchate defends Rukhadze

On 16 September, Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Patriarchate’s public relations service, issued a statement.

He said the Patriarchate had known from the outset that a significant portion of the money allocated for the funeral would remain unspent.

“During that period, we were in frequent contact with Ms Tika Rukhadze, and we knew from her that most organisations and individuals who provided various services had declined any remuneration or payment,” Jaghmaidze wrote.

He expressed hope that people would stop using the Patriarch’s name as a pretext for unfounded accusations and slander.

What links Tika Rukhadze to Tikhart?

According to Transparency International Georgia, Tinatin Rukhadze earned 410,000 lari as a consultant for Tikhart, an event management company, in the two years before she became culture minister.

The organisation also reports that Tikhart secured government contracts worth a total of 3.8 million lari through direct procurement, bypassing competitive tenders.

These circumstances raise questions about whether the company also received payment for organising the Patriarch’s funeral. However, no publicly available information confirms that it did.

Transparency International Georgia has called on the Ministry of Culture to disclose who received the 722,600 lari spent on the funeral and specify which services they provided.

Another problem is that the government does not have to disclose procurement information for purchases financed through the government’s reserve fund. This makes it harder for the public to scrutinise how the authorities spend public money.

The minister’s resignation and a new political climate

Tinatin Rukhadze became culture minister in October 2024. On 28 July 2026, she left the post, citing health reasons. No evidence has established a link between her resignation and the allegations concerning funeral expenditure.

On 15 September, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze appointed Maia Bitadze, a Georgian Dream MP, as culture minister, specifically praising her integrity.

Around the same time, Mamuka Mdinaradze also left his political post as head of the State Security Service. Rukhadze and Mdinaradze subsequently became targets of coordinated public attacks.

October: accusations from a Georgian Dream supporter

On 14 October, Davit Okitashvili, president of the Georgian Chamber of Culture and an active Georgian Dream supporter, publicly accused Tinatin Rukhadze of obstructing his projects and damaging his reputation. He also described Mamuka Mdinaradze as the former minister’s patron.

Okitashvili raised questions about the cost of the Patriarch’s funeral and called on the prosecutor’s office and the State Audit Office to investigate the spending. In a post, he asked Rukhadze:

“Ms Tika, where did the millions go?!”

Other Georgian Dream representatives supported Okitashvili’s post, including party activist and MP Dimitri Samkharadze.

What does Mamuka Mdinaradze have to do with it?

Okitashvili did not limit his attacks to the former culture minister.

He claimed that Mamuka Mdinaradze had acted as Rukhadze’s political patron. According to Okitashvili, Mdinaradze helped secure her appointment as minister, and she subsequently acted under his influence.

In an interview with Palitranews on 15 October, Okitashvili repeated these allegations. He also claimed that both Rukhadze and Mdinaradze had betrayed Georgian Dream.

However, he noted that the prosecutor’s office had not contacted him.

Georgian Dream representatives also responded to Okitashvili’s accusations.

MP Tengiz Sharmanashvili said the prosecutor’s office should ask Okitashvili what evidence he had. If his claims proved credible, investigators should question those involved, including Rukhadze and Mdinaradze.

Opposition warns of possible arrests

The opposition also reacted to the October developments.

Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, said Okitashvili’s statements might be intended to prepare the public for the possible arrests of Tinatin Rukhadze and Mamuka Mdinaradze.

Gvaramia suggested that Bidzina Ivanishvili could be behind the process.

Ana Tsitlidze, a representative of the United National Movement, accused Rukhadze and Bakur Bakuradze, the former director general of Rustavi 2, of embezzling funds allocated for the Patriarch’s funeral. She also suggested that authorities might arrest Mamuka Mdinaradze.

Former MP Eka Beselia suspected that Okitashvili’s statement might form part of a pre-planned process. She said that if an investigation began immediately after his statement, it would confirm her suspicions.

Scandal involving former officials in Georgia

World.title: ‘Deadly consequences’: How lack of proper prison in Abkhazia leads to further crimes
World.content:
The recent murder of a Russian tourist has exposed problems with prison sentences in Abkhazia. Edgar Abukhba, who stands accused of murdering Amina Bikbova, received a nine-year sentence for a previous serious crime. In practice, however, he served only half that time. This proved fatal for his next victim.

Amina’s murder prompted Abkhazian society to take a closer look at how courts enforce their rulings. It emerged that in Abkhazia, a sentence tells you very little about how long someone will actually spend in prison. The republic has no proper prison, and a complicated system of “penitentiary arithmetic” determines how much time a person spends behind bars. Even those who apply the rules struggle to make sense of them.

One last coffee

Amina Bikbova’s family had a rule: call her mother every evening. The 26-year-old followed it without fail when she travelled to Abkhazia with her friend Adila for a holiday in September 2026. But one evening, she did not call and failed to answer her phone either. The next day, her phone remained silent. Her family then realised that something serious had happened.

Amina Bikbova

The circumstances surrounding Amina’s final day are known from accounts given by her family and witness testimony reported by Abkhazian and Russian media. Amina and Adila met Edgar Abukhba, a 25-year-old fruit seller. A couple of days later, he invited Amina for coffee. Adila says she tried to talk her friend out of going, but failed. Amina went to meet Edgar and never returned.

During his initial questioning, he denied any wrongdoing. He claimed that he and Amina had simply had coffee, after which she got into someone’s car and drove away. Investigators quickly disproved this account, and Edgar admitted that they had argued, that he had strangled Amina and left her body in bushes beside the road.

A familiar name

Edgar Abukhba

For Abkhazians who follow local crime reports, the surname Abukhba sounded familiar. In July 2019, a 24-year-old Russian tourist suffered a brutal attack in central Sukhum. Her assailants beat, raped and robbed her. Everyone familiar with the case said they had rarely encountered such brutality. Authorities arrested Edgar Abukhba on suspicion of the crime. The case took more than two years to reach court, and in 2021 a judge sentenced him to nine years in prison.

If the nine-year sentence is counted from 2019, when Abukhba entered pre-trial detention, he should not have been released before 2028. Yet by the summer of 2026, he was already selling fruit in Gagra.

Sentences without a prison

Court rulings specify the regime under which a convicted person must serve their sentence, and this affects the time they spend in prison. But Abkhazia has no prison colony with different security regimes, which creates confusion. Officials recalculate sentences differently depending on how much time a prisoner has spent under various conditions. The final figure depends on the coefficient they apply and can differ significantly from the court’s verdict.

Got that? No, of course not. For anyone unfamiliar with the system, it is almost impossible to understand. Even staff at the relevant institutions struggle to explain on the spot how they calculate a particular sentence, how long a specific prisoner will serve and when they will be released.

Perhaps this explains why a man who, on paper, received a nine-year prison sentence attacked another woman long before that term had expired.

Leniency vs prudence

There is another legal complication in Edgar Abukhba’s case. He was still a minor when he committed his first crime, and under Abkhazian law, courts must not take juvenile convictions into account in the future.

There are two opposing views on this rule.

The logic of juvenile justice holds that a teenager’s actions should not determine the rest of their life. But this approach conflicts with public safety concerns, which suggest that authorities cannot simply ignore a proven threat posed by an individual.

Many countries face this dilemma, but they also assess risks before releasing offenders and supervise them afterwards. They may also restrict where former prisoners can work or live and impose other measures. Abkhazia, however, has no such safeguards in place.

A tarnished reputation

Cynical as it may sound, Abkhazia’s tourism sector — and, consequently, its budget — can also be counted among the “victims” of this tragedy.

Abkhazia effectively lives off Russian tourists, who provide the republic’s main source of income. Its reputation as a safe holiday destination is vital to its survival. Now, Amina Bikbova’s murder has left a major black mark on that reputation. This is particularly troubling because it is not the first attack on tourists.

Tourists may forgive reckless taxi drivers or poor service. But they are unlikely to accept the idea that killers who have not served their full sentences can freely walk the streets in search of new victims.

Many Abkhazian lawyers believe the authorities should publish a breakdown of Edgar Abukhba’s first sentence, including the coefficients they applied and his release date. In other words, they should at least explain why he regained his freedom so quickly. Perhaps the authorities should also review the system for calculating prison sentences. Better still, they should finally build a proper prison colony so that no one has to perform these calculations in the first place.

The public, meanwhile, wants an open trial in this case. People are waiting for an explanation of how this mysterious coefficient can allow rapists and murderers to walk free earlier than petty thieves.

World.title: IRENA identifies priorities for boosting global energy transition by 2035
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) has identified accelerating electrification, modernizing energy infrastructure, expanding investment, and strengthening international cooperation among the seven key priorities for boosting the global energy transition by 2035.

This was reflected in the World Energy Transition Outlook 2026 report, published on the website of IRENA.

According to the report, the primary task for the coming decade lies not so much in setting new long-term goals as in the practical implementation of commitments already made.

IRENA identified the development of comprehensive plans and market mechanisms as the first priority, mechanisms that align the growth of renewable energy, electrification, infrastructure modernization, and investment activity. Such frameworks should provide predictable, long-term conditions for investors and help identify and remove barriers to project implementation, while still allowing for market-based decision-making.

The second priority involves developing national energy transition roadmaps tailored to the specific circumstances of each country. These should integrate measures for expanding renewable energy sources, advancing electrification, improving energy efficiency, utilizing sustainable fuels, and ensuring a just transition away from fossil fuels.

The third priority, according to the agency, is to accelerate investment in the expansion and modernization of energy infrastructure—most notably power transmission and distribution grids, energy storage systems, solutions for grid flexibility, and digital infrastructure. At the same time, market reforms are required to provide effective price signals and incentivize investment in the reliability and flexibility of energy supply.

The fourth priority entails the development of comprehensive industrial strategies to foster competitive clean energy sectors. Specifically, this involves strengthening national and regional supply chains, building professional expertise, and increasing domestic value-added, all while maintaining access to international markets and technological partnerships, IRENA noted.

The fifth priority is to create a stable environment for investment, reduce the cost of capital, and develop national financial markets. According to IRENA, public funding should be strategically directed toward supporting renewable energy, infrastructure, workforce training, and industrial transformation, while also serving to attract additional private capital, particularly in developing countries.

The sixth priority involves ensuring that the energy transition delivers social, economic, and environmental benefits. This requires measures to maintain energy affordability for the public, strengthen social and environmental protections, expand equal economic opportunities, and involve the public in decision-making processes.

As a seventh priority, IRENA highlighted the importance of strengthening international cooperation, including technology transfer, the diversification of supply chains, the development of regional industrial partnerships, collaboration among Global South nations, knowledge sharing, and expanding access to affordable financing.

The report placed particular emphasis on the electrification of end-use energy consumption. The agency identified this as a core pillar of the energy transition by 2035, as it bridges the gap between the expansion of clean electricity generation and the transformation of the transport, building, and industrial sectors.

IRENA pointed out that while international efforts are already focused on accelerating the deployment of renewable energy capacity, improving energy efficiency, strengthening power grids, and developing sustainable fuels, the transformation of end-use energy consumption has received comparatively less attention.

"Elevating electrification to a key priority will help link existing international commitments to practical changes within the energy system, accelerate the reduction of reliance on fossil fuels, and keep within reach the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius," the report added.

World.title: Global economy can gain about $47T from energy transition by 2050
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Accelerating the energy transition could deliver a cumulative gain of about $47 trillion to the global economy by 2050, under a scenario that limits global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

This was reflected in the World Energy Transitions Outlook 2026 report, published on the website of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA).

According to the report, under this scenario, global gross domestic product (GDP) would be, on average, about 1.1% higher annually than it would be if current policies were maintained.

"In an alternative scenario involving a deeper energy system transformation (DES), global GDP would be, on average, about 0.7% higher through 2050 compared to the Planned Energy Scenario (PES). The cumulative economic gain in this case is estimated at approximately $32 trillion," noted IRENA.

The primary driver of this economic growth will be increased investment in renewable energy, electrification, power grids, and energy efficiency. These areas will stimulate development in construction, manufacturing, engineering services, the power sector, and business services.

At the same time, the structure of the economy will gradually shift: the share of activities related to the extraction and processing of fossil fuels will decline, while the production of high-value-added equipment, the development of power infrastructure, and the provision of services related to the energy transition will become increasingly significant.

The report also noted that the development of renewable energy could help lower electricity costs for end-users.

"By 2035, under the DES scenario, average electricity prices will be approximately 9% lower than they would be under current policies, and by 2050, this gap could widen to 15%. This is due to an increasing share of renewable energy and a reduced dependence on fossil fuel prices," the report mentioned.

According to IRENA estimates, by 2050, employment in the renewable energy sector under the DES scenario will reach approximately 84.2 million jobs—a 60% increase compared to a scenario where current policies remain in place. The solar energy sector will continue to be the largest employer, potentially accounting for around 38.3 million jobs.

Overall employment in the energy sector is also expected to grow, driven by investments in power systems, energy efficiency, infrastructure, and new technologies.

At the same time, the report emphasizes that the economic benefits of the energy transition will not be distributed evenly. Countries with a well-developed industrial base stand to gain significantly from manufacturing clean energy equipment and providing related services.

Conversely, economies dependent on fossil fuels will face a more challenging structural transformation as revenues from the extraction and processing of these fuels, along with employment in these sectors, decline.

Developing nations could also derive substantial economic gains from such investments. However, IRENA pointed out that to do so, they must build their own manufacturing capabilities and integrate more actively into global value chains, rather than relying primarily on the import of technologies.

In this context, the agency underscored the growing importance of industrial policy. According to IRENA, countries should develop competitive advantages at the national and regional levels by investing in workforce training, production capacity, innovation, and competitive industries, rather than attempting to build every link of the global supply chain on their own.

World.title: Iran approaches diplomacy responsibly to reduce regional tension - minister
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Iran approaches diplomacy responsibly in order to reduce regional tensions, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said during a meeting with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, held on the sidelines of the 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad, Iraq, on October 17.

This was stated in a statement by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

"However, the U.S. side has failed to fulfill its diplomatic commitments; most recently, it halted the implementation of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, which concerned the cessation of hostilities, just two weeks after it was signed," he noted.

Araghchi pointed out that the current situation in the Strait of Hormuz is a consequence of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes against Iran.

During the meeting, the Iranian minister provided an update on the status of diplomatic consultations being conducted through intermediaries.

The two sides also exchanged views regarding developments on the Arabian Peninsula. Stating that Iran is prepared to provide any assistance toward halting the confrontations between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, the Iranian minister noted that 12 years of tension demonstrate that there is no solution to the issue in Yemen.

The next escalation in U.S.-Iranian relations began on July 8. On that day, for the first time since the signing of the memorandum between Washington and Tehran, U.S. forces launched a series of strikes on Iranian territory, allegedly in response to an attack on a merchant ship in the Strait of Hormuz. On the same day, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the suspension of the ceasefire with Iran. In response, Tehran began striking U.S. targets located in Bahrain, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, and Oman. As a result of the conflict, maritime trade in the Strait of Hormuz came to a standstill.

World.title: Global energy efficiency to rise 3% annually through 2030 – IRENA
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Global energy efficiency is expected to improve by 3% annually through 2030 under current policies, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA).

The forecast is outlined in the World Energy Transitions Outlook 2026, published on IRENA’s website.

The report notes that the average annual rate of improvement in global energy efficiency remained slightly below 2% over the past three years. Achieving the global target of doubling the rate of improvement by 2030 requires annual gains of around 4%.

Under IRENA’s Planned Energy Scenario (PES), energy efficiency is projected to improve by only around 3% annually between 2026 and 2030. By contrast, IRENA’s 1.5°C Scenario, which aims to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius, requires annual improvements of more than 4% over the remaining years to 2030 to make up for the shortfall in previous years.

The report identifies electrification as one of the key drivers of improved energy efficiency. Electric vehicles, heat pumps and electric industrial technologies can replace fuel-burning processes in which a significant share of energy is lost as heat.

“Developing renewable-based energy systems and expanding electrification can provide greater mobility, comfort and productivity while consuming less primary and final energy,” the report states.

A reduction in primary energy consumption under a scenario consistent with limiting global warming to 1.5°C does not necessarily mean lower economic activity or fewer energy services. To a large extent, it reflects improvements in the efficiency of the energy system.

However, electrification alone will not be sufficient to achieve the required targets. Other important measures include improving building energy efficiency, setting standards for household appliances, making industrial processes and transport systems more efficient, managing demand and changing consumption patterns.

The report warns that if energy efficiency improvements do not accelerate while electricity demand continues to grow, significantly more renewable generation capacity, infrastructure and investment will be needed to deliver the same level of energy services.

According to IRENA, improving energy efficiency, expanding power grids and ensuring flexibility in energy systems are becoming essential to the pace of the energy transition.

“These areas should not be viewed as secondary additions to renewable energy expansion, but as fundamental factors determining whether the transition can be implemented rapidly, reliably and at an affordable cost,” the report states.

World.title: Wallaroos not content with simply being 'better versions' of themselves
World.content:
Among Siokapesi Palu Sekona's many impressive qualities as Wallaroos captain is her uncompromising approach.

Wallabies outclassed by All Blacks The Wallabies fall to the All Blacks for the 13th straight time, as their trans-Tasman rivals record a convincing 43-21 win in Sydney.

As such, it does not come as a shock to learn she feels the Wallaroos still have much room for improvement following their dominant 56-12 win over Scotland in this afternoon's Global XV Series Test.

The eight-tries-to-two victory did not represent a complete performance in Palu Sekona's eyes, which should serve as music to the ears of Wallaroos supporters.

Why?

It shows the Wallaroos are setting the highest possible standards for themselves.

"We still know there is room for improvement and we definitely know what to do to clean that up," Palu Sekona said.

Wallaroos skipper Siokapesi Palu Sekona put in a solid shift on both sides of the ball. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

The Wallaroos defeated Scotland 30-10 three weeks ago in Edinburgh during their three-Test swing through Great Britain and France as part of the Global XV Series.

The victory snapped a six-match losing streak but left Wallaroos players and coaches dissatisfied.

It was a sign of the Wallaroos' quickly developing harder edge, which Palu Sekona wants carried through to the 2029 Women's Rugby World Cup.

"We knew we could put together a better performance," she said.

"Ultimately results and scores are what people look at. But if we want to break down our rugby, there are so many things to clean up.

"From discipline, to our ruck, to the accuracy of our set-piece. There are things we can continue to work on."

Wallaroos set bar high

The Wallaroos, ranked seventh in the world, are starting from behind scratch when compared to teams such as England and New Zealand.

Both enjoy the benefit of being full-time programs, with their respective governing bodies making a wise move to invest in the women's game.

The Wallaroos are still semi-professional, but a shift to full-time status — as part of an integrated program alongside the women's sevens squad — is in progress.

There is no doubt the Wallaroos' rate of improvement will be accelerated once they go full-time in the lead-up to the World Cup, which Australia will host.

"We don't want to only be the better versions of ourselves," Palu Sekona said.

" We want to be the best in the world. "

Winger Amelia Whitaker scored a double in the Wallaroos' victory. (Getty Images/Corbis: Steve Christo)

The Wallaroos' makeshift coaching team, under the leadership of Rugby Australia's director of women's high performance Tim Walsh, has had a positive influence on the playing group.

Sione Fukofuka will take over as head coach next year and work alongside Walsh, who enjoyed tremendous success in charge of the Australian women's sevens squad.

Like Palu Sekona, Walsh was not completely satisfied with the Wallaroos' display against Scotland.

But he saw enough to know they are heading in the right direction.

"I think it was another step forward, for sure," Walsh said.

The Wallaroos will complete their 2026 Test season when they meet Scotland in Canberra on Friday night.

World.title: Kangaroos halfback's World Cup ends with calf muscle injury
World.content:
Mitchell Moses will miss the remainder of the Rugby League World Cup, after being ruled out of the Kangaroos' title defence with a lower leg injury that continues his representative misery.

The Parramatta playmaker suffered the injury during Australia's 24-22 win over New Zealand in the tournament opener on Thursday night in Sydney.

He attempted to play on but eventually left the field less than two minutes into the second half.

Meanwhile, Papua New Guinea's men's and women's sides began their tournaments with wins, and England eased to victory over Wales in the women's competition.

Moses was injured during the Kangaroos' World Cup opener against New Zealand. (Getty Images: Matt King)

While initially believed to be a calf issue or a hairline fracture, scans following the match revealed Moses had suffered an unspecified "high-grade muscle tear", meaning his World Cup campaign is over.

It's a blow to the Kangaroos, who are already missing Nathan Cleary with a serious leg injury, with Moses the Kangaroos' strongest last-tackle kicker.

World Cup opener a reminder of Australia's glory days There was a time when Test matches were rugby league's biggest, best and bloodiest spectacles, and last night's World Cup opener between Australia and New Zealand was a reminder of those days.

Moses switched allegiance to play for Australia at this tournament after captaining Lebanon at the 2022 World Cup.

Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters said the 32-year-old was understandably disappointed to miss the remainder of the campaign.

"Mitch made a wonderful contribution to our World Cup preparations during the camp in Sydney and very bravely tried to play through the injury until he eventually had to come from the field on Thursday night," Walters said in a statement on Saturday.

"He is naturally disappointed at the outcome today, and the fact that he tried to stay out there when he was clearly injured shows just what it means to him to represent his country and play in the Kangaroos jersey."

In Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea's men's side earned a gritty 42-18 win over Lebanon hours after the country's women's team had dispatched France 58-4.

Veteran Rhyse Martin began his farewell tournament in style, scoring a try and going perfect from seven conversions against a dogged Lebanon outfit.

His try with nine minutes left on the clock finished off the Cedars, who were fading in humid conditions.

But Lebanon never stopped trying, with fullback Jacob Kiraz (207 metres) and winger Tony Frances (292 metres) constant threats in attack, while Wests Tigers stalwart Alex Twal led the defence with 48 tackles.

Winger Naomi Kelly crossed four times in the women's game as the Orchids ran in 12 tries to one.

England ended the day's women's action in comprehensive fashion against Wales, with Connie Boyd and Anna Davies both scoring hat-tricks in the 70-6 rout in Perth.

AAP/ABC

World.title: Yagera woman Jayda Allen Bonner remembered at Melbourne vigil
World.content:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article contains the name and image of an Indigenous person who has died, used with the permission of their family.

Hundreds have gathered in Melbourne to pay tribute to a young Indigenous woman killed at an inner-suburban apartment complex last weekend.

A smoking ceremony was held in honour of 21-year-old Jayda Allen Bonner, who was remembered as "a beautiful soul" by her mother and aunt.

Jayda Allen Bonner, 21, was described by her aunt as a "gentle soul with a heart of gold". (Supplied)

This week, a 31-year-old man was charged with murder and appeared briefly in the Melbourne Magistrates Court.

Police say he was known to Ms Allen Bonner.

Supporters of the Bonner family then marched to Victoria's Parliament to demand changes to domestic violence procedures and reform to better prevent violence against women.

Ms Allen Bonner's mother, Jade Allen, took part in the vigil, wearing a t-shirt emblazoned with an image of her daughter and the phrase 'Justice for Jayda'.

Many attendees carried 'Justice for Jayda' posters in memory of the 21-year-old woman. (ABC News)

"Jayda loved her family fiercely. She had a heart of gold — she would do anything for anybody," Ms Allen said.

"I want everyone to stand up and stop keeping all of this quiet.

"I want to make sure Jayda's name isn't forgotten. She was one-of-a-kind."

Jade Allen and Kellie Carter Bell urge Australians to do more to prevent violence against women. (ABC News)

Ms Allen Bonner's aunt Kellie Carter Bell said all Australians need to do more to speak out against violence against women.

"We're living with wars behind our doors," she said.

"We need recognition, we need people to understand what this stuff looks like.

"The question should be: What can I do to help (victim-survivors) get out safely?"

Questions raised over police response

Antoinette Braybrook, chief executive of Melbourne-based Aboriginal family violence service Djirra, said the 21-year-old's death was "devastating".

She said it was "outrageous" and "shocking" that Ms Allen Bonner could "fall through the cracks".

Ms Allen Bonner's family has previously said the young woman had made a complaint to police about her safety which she later withdrew.

Her family has also said they tried to contact police themselves, but were told that because Ms Allen Bonner was an adult, there was nothing they could do.

Ms Braybrook said that wasn't true.

Antoinette Braybrook says the police response leading up to the death must be investigated. (Supplied)

"They have the power to investigate violence in the home and initiate their own intervention orders and charge people; my question is, why didn't they do that?"

Ms Braybrook added that it was not uncommon for women experiencing violence to withdraw their complaints to police, even if they were still in danger.

Speaking generally, she said women experiencing violence might be pressured into doing so or be threatened with further violence by their abusers.

"The perpetrator has absolute control, power and control over her in that situation," Ms Braybrook said.

"It's a consistent issue in our work."

While Djirra was now in contact with the young Yagera woman's family, Ms Braybrook said given the history of concern for Ms Allen Bonner's safety, it was "extremely disappointing" police or other authorities had not connected her with the service before her death.

"That's one of the concerns that we have as a specialist Aboriginal community-controlled organisation working on the frontline of Aboriginal women and children's safety," she said.

"I am just at a loss — I sit at the table, many tables, with police, with corrections, with courts and others, talking about how we can improve the safety of women.

"When things like this happen to women, it just makes those talks that we participate in all of the time seem like a joke."

A Victoria Police spokesperson said the death of a young woman in Carlton on October 10 was suspicious.

"The investigation is being led by the Homicide Squad," the police spokesperson said.

"As part of investigations, Victoria Police will thoroughly examine any interactions between police and the victim in the lead-up to her death.

"We are unable to comment further while the investigation remains ongoing."

World.title: Police release e-bike rider image in 'sexual touching' case, increase patrols
World.content:
Police have increased patrols on walking trails surrounding a lagoon in Sydney's northern beaches after multiple women reported being "sexually touched" allegedly by a man on an e-bike.

The incidents, which number six to date, took place between October 1 and October 12 in broad daylight while the women were walking or running at Narabeen Lagoon and in the surrounding bushland.

The incidents took place between October 1 and October 12 in broad daylight. (ABC News)

In an update on Saturday afternoon, Superintendent John Duncan said it was alarming that women were being harassed.

"We take these matters very, very seriously," he said.

"In consultation with State Crime Command and the Sex Crime Squad, we've got a number of overt and covert activities.

"We have a number of our uniformed and plain-clothed officers in the area."

Most of the alleged offending occurred between 4pm and 6pm.

In some cases several incidents occurred on one day, which according to police "tends to suggest it's probably someone who is local and someone nearby".

Police say the man is believed to be aged under 25 years and of Caucasian appearance. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Earlier, police released an image of a man they would like to speak to.

He is riding an e-bike and is described as "being of Caucasian appearance, believed to be aged under 25 years, about 175cm tall and of medium build".

Police believe just one person is involved, but are "keeping their options open".

"I'd imagine that person, or their families or friends, will actually know who that is," Superintendent Duncan said.

"And we encourage them to come forward and help with our investigations."

'Rode away on an e-bike'

The first reported incidents happened on October 7 and October 8.

"In each incident, a male allegedly approached women on walking trails, sexually touched them and then rode away on an e-bike," police said in a statement.

"In one of the incidents, the man also made inappropriate sexual comments."

The first incidents reported to police took place on walking trails near the lagoon. (ABC News)

After a public appeal for information on October 12, police received an additional three reports — one dating back to the first of that month.

The woman alleged she was approached by a man near South Creek Road at Wheeler Heights about 4.30pm and allegedly sexually touched before he rode away on an e-bike.

On October 12, in two separate incidents between 5pm and 5:30pm, two women reported being sexually touched by a male riding an e-bike.

There have been no reports since then, Superintendent Duncan said, but he feared there may be more cases.

"We do believe that there are probably more victims out there that may have some information or may have been a victim of this particular crime," he said.

"And we'd like them to come forward and contact either Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or Dee Why Police Station."

Anyone with dashcam footage is also urged to contact police.

World.title: More teens arrested over alleged assault of 15yo boy
World.content:
Two more teenagers have been arrested over an alleged group assault in the western Victorian town of Stawell earlier this month.

Police say a 15-year-old-boy was attacked by a group of teenagers near the intersection of Wakeham and Doye streets about 5:45pm on October 5.

They allegedly stole his shoes and clothing before running away.

The boy was taken to hospital but has since been released.

On Saturday, police said a 14-year-old boy had been charged with several offences, inlcuding recklessly causing injury, while a 16-year-old girl was also expected to be charged.

It follows the arrests of two 15-year-olds and a 14-year-old on Tuesday. They were charged with affray, robbery, recklessly causing injury, and theft.

They will appear in the children's court at a later date.

A spotlight on security

The incident comes as community pressure grows on the Northern Grampians Shire Council to install CCTV in police-identified crime hotspots at Stawell.

The alleged assault has renewed the conversation about public safety in Stawell. (ABC News: Sarah Mullins)

After the three initial arrests made earlier this week, Mayor Karen Hyslop said the council's policy had not changed "for now", but "priorities can be re-evaluated".

She said council had looked into "the financial cost and privacy concerns", and found CCTV installation would involve "allocating hundreds of thousands of dollars from the budget".

But Stawell resident Jessica Lees, who, alongside two other mothers, ran an online survey earlier this year to collect data in support of cameras being installed, was not happy with that response.

She said more than 300 people filled out the survey and had questioned why the council had not explored every option, including available state government grants for the cameras.

"If other councils across Victoria can find ways to fund CCTV, why can't we?" she asked.

World.title: Australia's first Vietnamese heritage museum opens in Melbourne
World.content:
Before the days of bánh mì takeaways and discount flight holidays, to most Australians Vietnam was known only for the horrors of conflict and conscription.

That was to change with the end of the Vietnam War.

Thousands of Vietnamese refugees made the perilous journey to Australia in the mid-1970s, saying an abrupt goodbye to Saigon and an apprehensive hello to Melbourne's Sunshine and St Albans or Sydney's Cabramatta and Canley Vale.

Tammy Nguyen's parents escaped Vietnam on a perilous six-day, seven-night boat journey. (Supplied)

Five decades on, refugee beginnings and generational achievement were recognised with the opening of the nation's first museum dedicated to Vietnamese-Australian history.

Constructed on a council car park in Sunshine, the unveiling of Vietnamese Museum Australia marked the culmination of a decade-long campaign to establish a permanent monument to the community's pioneering generation.

The parents of the museum's chief executive, Tammy Nguyen, escaped Vietnam on a perilous six-day, seven-night boat journey.

"There are more than 350,000 people of Vietnamese-origin living in Australia and everyone has their own unique story to tell," Ms Nguyen said.

" This museum is a living monument to all those who courageously left their homeland behind — often as refugees on overcrowded and unseaworthy boats — seeking freedom and a better future. "

The project has received bipartisan support, with Victorian Premier Ben Carroll officially opening the centre on Saturday alongside MPs from across the political divide.

Both the federal and Victorian governments contributed millions to the project, alongside grassroots community contributions.

The Vietnamese-Australian community worked for more than a decade to establish the museum. (Supplied)

Liberal MP Trung Luu, who represents the Western Metropolitan Region in the state's upper house, said the museum's opening was a significant day for the Vietnamese community.

"As someone who came to Australia as a refugee from Vietnam, today is deeply personal for me," he said.

"This museum honours the courage of every family who made that journey."

Lan Anh Hoang says racial anxieties lingered due to the legacy of the White Australia policy. (Supplied)

University of Melbourne development studies professor Lan Anh Hoang said public attitudes towards Vietnamese refugees in the 1970s and 1980s were mixed as the nation adjusted to life post-White Australia policy.

"In the immediate aftermath of the fall of Saigon, there was a great deal of sympathy and compassion, particularly because of Australia's own involvement in the war," she said.

"But as boat arrivals continued towards the end of the 1970s, concerns grew about uncontrolled migration, and the legacy of the White Australia policy meant that racial anxieties still lingered."

Professor Hoang said Vietnamese migrants to Australia who relocate in 2026 find themselves in a more welcoming environment.

But she added that they also tended to be more educated or skilled, with better English proficiency than the refugees who came in the 1970s.

"Many describe the kindness and generous support of churches and community organisations (in the 1970s)," she said.

"At the same time, Vietnamese families and their children faced more than their fair share of racism in the community and at school.

"It was not easy to be a Vietnamese kid growing up in Australia at that time."

Flashback: Members of the Vietnamese community pay their respects to Malcolm Fraser at the former prime minister's 2015 funeral. (ABC News: Clement Paligaru)

University of Technology Sydney sociology professor Andrew Jakubowicz said the mid-1970s intake of Vietnamese-Australians under the Fraser Government was the first real test of the post-White Australia policy consensus.

Malcolm Fraser became a champion of the Vietnamese-Australian diaspora and members of the community paid tribute to the ex-PM at his 2015 funeral.

"(Vietnamese-Australians) were admitted as the first big group of refugees from a group that had almost no prior presence," Professor Jakubowicz said.

"Initially, most were Catholic southerners and pro-Saigon. Their actual travel to Australia was traumatic — they were the first modern boat people.

"They arrived in the shadow of the end of White Australia into a country that was trepidatiously ready to accept Asians.

"Before then, most Asians admitted after 1967 were English-speaking professionals."

World.title: 'Terrible to watch': Ohope Wins euthanased after fall in Caulfield Cup
World.content:
New Zealand mare Ohope Wins has been euthanased after a fall in the Caulfield Cup that also included 2025 Melbourne Cup winner Half Yours.

With about 200 metres to go in the 2,400m race, which was won by Gavin Bedggood's Kingswood, Half Yours was in the middle of the pack when there appeared to be contact with Kings Valley.

Half Yours went down hard, sending jockey Mark Zahra into the turf, with Ohope Wins also coming down after Jye McNeil was unable to avoid the fallen McEvoy Racing product.

Racing Victoria Stewards later confirmed Ohope Wins, from Chris Waller Racing, was euthanased by the on-course veterinarian.

Jye McNeil on Ohope Wins in the mounting yard before the Caulfield Cup. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri)

"The mare was unable to be saved due to the nature of the injury sustained," a Racing Victoria (RV) statement read.

"RV extends its condolences to Yulong, the owners of Ohope Wins, her trainer Chris Waller and their stable staff who cared for the horse and are deeply saddened by their loss."

Yulong and Waller released a statement, saying "few words can express our current emotions".

"Ohope Wins was a true star of the turf, but to the people who looked after her everyday, she was so much more," the statement read.

"She was brave. She was kind. She was full of character, but more importantly, she was loved.

Ohope Wins won the Oaks at Randwick in April. (Getty Images: Vince Caligiuri)

"Our hearts go out to all involved throughout her career, especially those who cared for her on a daily basis."

Half Yours, the defending Caulfield Cup victor, got up and eventually crossed the finish line without a jockey.

The stewards said Half Yours would undergo a "thorough veterinary examination" after falling in "a racing incident", which would be subject to an inquiry.

Half Yours got up and crossed the line without a rider. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Half Yours returned to his stall, while stewards said Zahra and McNeil were both "conscious and alert" and transported to hospital for further assessment.

Trainer Tony McEvoy said after the race that Half Yours had suffered some abrasions but looked OK, all things considered.

"That was terrible to watch," McEvoy said.

"The horse, he's got a couple of lacerations, he seems bright, he seems composed in himself.

"He's got a laceration under his arm, he's got a laceration on a hind leg. They look superficial."

The final race of the day at Caulfield was delayed.

World.title: Australia's deadliest asylum seeker boat disaster remembered 25 years on
World.content:
Mourners have gathered at a national memorial in Canberra to mark the 25th anniversary of Australia's deadliest asylum seeker boat disaster, the sinking of the SIEV X.

On October 19, 2001, 353 people died when the fishing boat, heading to Christmas Island, sank in international waters off the coast of the Indonesian island of Java.

Of the dead, 146 were children.

The 20-metre-long boat, which was carrying more than 400 people, capsized and sank when its engine failed in heavy seas.

More than 20 hours after the vessel went down, 45 survivors were rescued by Indonesian fishing boats.

The name SIEV X is a naval acronym, standing for Suspected Illegal Entry Vessel X.

Mourners gathered at the SIEV X Memorial on the shores of Lake Burley Griffin in Canberra for the 25th anniversary of the disaster. (ABC News: Caitlin Maloney)

While the vessel sank 70 kilometres south of Java, not in Australia's waters, the disaster occurred in a border protection surveillance area temporarily designated by Australia.

Questions still remain about the SIEV X tragedy 25 years after it occurred, with many of the victims never publicly identified and no full judicial inquiry held.

The victims are remembered at the SIEV X Memorial in Canberra's Weston Park, where each wooden pole — decorated by school, church and community groups — marks one person who died.

Advocacy group Refugee Action Campaign (RAC) Canberra organised the 25-year memorial service along the shores of Lake Burley Griffin to honour the lives lost in the "preventable tragedy".

The SIEV X Memorial covers 400m of shoreline at Weston Park along Lake Burley Griffin. (Supplied)

The RAC said the service also allowed attendees "to stand in solidarity with [the victims'] loved ones, and to show support and compassion for refugees and people seeking asylum".

"In today's environment in which migrants and refugees are being blamed by politicians with nothing else to offer for the failures of governments to prioritise the needs of ordinary people, the SIEV X Memorial remains as relevant as ever," Refugee Action Campaign Canberra said.

A political message 25 years on

In August 2001, more than 400 asylum seekers were rescued by Norweigian ship the Tampa, sparking a national and international crisis. (AAP)

The SIEV X tragedy occurred just weeks after the Howard government refused the entry of Norwegian freighter MV Tampa, which was carrying more than 400 rescued asylum seekers.

The Tampa affair sparked intense debate leading up to the 2001 federal election campaign, as the government hardened its stance on asylum seekers.

Memorial co-founder Steve Biddulph said on the fifth anniversary of the disaster, the Howard government opposed the memorial on Commonwealth land, and so those who gathered for the service held the memorial's poles upright.

People gathered in 2006 on the fifth anniversary of the SIEV X boat disaster and established a temporary memorial. (ABC TV)

He said a year later, with the support of John Stanhope, the then ACT chief minister, permission was given to make the memorial permanent.

"It sends a signal that ordinary Australians are not terrified of refugees, they're not terrified of people from other countries," he said.

"We're essentially a loving, caring nation, and we were being sold an image of ourselves that was completely wrong.

"And so it's a message of hope, really, that love is stronger than fear."

Co-founder Steve Biddulph says the memorial was created to show the SIEV X victims were remembered as people and not just numbers. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

President of the SIEV X Memorial Association ACT Paul Meyer said the disaster remained political 25 years on, when people were "turning against migrants in general".

"Many of us have come here ourselves; a huge proportion of Australians have at least one migrant parent, if not a grandparent, so we all know that Australia's a country that welcomes people to come as long as we can contribute to it," he said.

He said as people gathered around the memorial today, more than 100 names of the drowning victims had not been made public — something both he and Mr Biddulph sought to rectify.

Paul Meyer of the SIEV X Memorial Association says the memorial's message is even more important now as the political climate is "turning against migrants in general". (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

"We tracked down around 220 of the names, and they're written on the poles, but they should all be named ... we could really do the right thing there," Mr Biddulph said.

Mr Meyer said he hoped the memorial continued to act as a beacon of compassion.

"And it's a defiance of what today would be the Hansonite approach [of], 'Oh let's be terrified,'" he said.

World.title: Pope Leo to leave hospital on Saturday, four days after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Updated WorldEuropePope Francis Pope Leo to leave hospital on Saturday, four days after lung cancer surgery Nicole Winfield and Paolo Santalucia Updated October 17, 2026 — 10:24pm ,first published October 17, 2026 — 9:47am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Rome: Pope Leo is expected to leave hospital on Saturday afternoon (Rome local time) following surgery for lung cancer, the Vatican said, after blood tests and chest imaging found him fit to return home four days after his operation. The 71-year-old pontiff, who has not been seen in public since a procedure on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, will also hold his first public engagement since surgery on Sunday. He will lead weekly prayers with pilgrims in St. Peter’s Square at midday. This picture, released by the Vatican on Friday shows Pope Leo XIV celebrating Mass at the hospital in Rome, where he is recovering from surgery. Vatican Media via AP Pope Leo XIV gave strong indications on Friday (Rome time) that he was recovering well from lung cancer surgery and was very much in charge of running the Catholic Church, speaking on the phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin, meeting with top aides and celebrating Mass in a makeshift hospital chapel.



The Vatican said that during the call with Putin, “The Holy Father expressed his deep concern about the grave humanitarian situation in the city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, and called for a ceasefire to allow the delivery of food and medical assistance, and the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population.” The statement added that Leo “reaffirmed the Holy See’s commitment to promoting dialogue and peace”. The Gemelli Hospital in Rome. Getty Images Putin voiced support for “the Vatican’s intention to help create conditions for ensuring the safety of the local population and facilitating the delivery of essential supplies”, and an agreement was reached to coordinate efforts in this regard, the statement said. Also on Friday, the Vatican released the first images of Leo since his lung cancer surgery on October 13, showing him standing up at the altar in green vestments, as doctors said that tests confirmed his “continued improvement”.



Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed after doctors identified a suspected cancerous nodule. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. “His post-operative recovery allows him to carry out his normal daily activities completely on his own,” said a medical update signed by Leo’s personal physician Dr Luigi Carbone and the head of thoracic surgery, Dr Stefano Margaritora. Pope Leo XIV pictured in St Peter’s Square on October 7. AP Photo/Andrew Medichini The Vatican had originally estimated a weeklong hospital stay, and had cancelled his audiences through Tuesday. Even as questions swirled about the future of Leo’s young pontificate, there were signs on Friday that it was all systems go. The Vatican published the names of journalists accredited to fly on Leo’s plane with him during his November 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Leo’s ability to make the trip has been in question since his diagnosis, and the Vatican can change the plans at any time. But the posting of the media list signalled that at least on an organisational level, the trip was going ahead.



Doctors are still awaiting the results of tests to understand the precise molecular and genetic makeup of the cancer, whether it has spread beyond the lobe and whether any further treatment is necessary. World.title: AFLW round 10: Daisy Pearce reaches a ‘big decision’; Cats annihilate the Eagles in Perth
World.content:
The Cats have leapt to the top of the AFLW ladder (even if only temporarily) with a 53-point domination of the Eagles on their home Perth deck, 8.18 (66) to 1.7 (13).

Only wastefulness in front of goal prevented an even more commanding win for Geelong, who staggeringly kept the Eagles goalless until the game’s final minutes.

It was a day to forget for Lucia Painter and the West Coast Eagles. AFL Photos

Most telling was Geelong’s ability to punish West Coast on turnover – dominating that statistic 49 points to just two.

Newly re-signed Eagles coach Daisy Pearce would surely have been left scratching her head at just how emphatically her side was wiped off the park.

Georgie Prespakis continued her run of dominance with 39 disposals, six clearances and six tackles, while her teammates Nina Morrison, Amy McDonald and Mikayla Bowen finished with 27 touches apiece.

World.title: Wallabies player ratings: How the men in gold performed in Bledisloe shocker
World.content:
SportRugby UnionWallabies Wallabies player ratings: How the men in gold performed in Bledisloe shocker Christy Doran October 17, 2026 — 9:46pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

The All Blacks blew the Wallabies away during a 20-minute period to run in five quick tries in the first-half. They were bigger, faster and stronger than the Wallabies and it showed. They won the collisions, generated fast ball at the ruck and Les Kiss’ men had few answers during the 43-21 defeat. So how did the men in gold rate? 1. Aidan Ross - 4.5 Was part of a tight-five that was well-beaten by the All Blacks. 2. Josh Nasser - 5.5



Made 14 tackles and didn’t miss one. Nasser fought hard and his set-piece work was acceptable. Allan Alaalatoa of the Wallabies looks on. Getty Images 3. Allan Alaalatoa - 5 Alaalatoa made 13 tackles, but missed a few as the All Blacks’ pace got the better of the Wallabies tighthead. But he wasn’t able to influence the match like he would have wanted. 4. Jeremy Williams - 5.5



Related Article Australian rugby ‘Unacceptable’: Nightmare Bledisloe as Wallabies handed reality check Scored a try in the 29th minute but was sent to the sin bin two minutes later for getting in the passing channel of Cam Roigard. It was a tough lesson to learn. Williams later made a lineout steal in the 71st minute. The second-rower also made 13 carries for 36 metres. 5. Lukhan Salakaia-Loto - 4.5 The All Blacks’ locks Scott Barrett and Fabian Holland collectively made 48 tackles. It was work-rate aplenty. Salakaia-Loto was beaten to the punch too often and outplayed by Holland, who was brilliant on his return.



Salakaia-Loto made a couple of big carries, but it wasn’t enough. The big lock dropped the ball in the 42nd minute, and the All Blacks capitalised by scoring off the back of it. Lukhan Salakaia-Loto was a part of a forward pack that was well beaten. Getty Images 6. Rob Valetini - 5 A few tough carries, but the damaging blindside flanker wasn’t able to influence the game for long enough. He also lost the ball on the deck from a kick restart after Williams’ try and the All Blacks scored soon after. 7. Fraser McReight - 5.5



Related Article Analysis

Wallabies The Bledisloe Cup used to be a great rivalry. This year proved it no longer is The Wallabies’ openside flanker might be one of the nation’s best, but for the second straight week he had little impact. The All Blacks were all over the fetcher. McReight spilled the ball at the back of the maul in the 15th minute. It proved a coach killer, with the All Blacks only leading 5-0 at the time. Dave Rennie’s side then went down the other end and scored. The tries kept coming, too. McReight was also held up over the line in the 39th minute. It was another missed chance. Rubbing salt into the wound is that Beauden Barrett intercepted Max Jorgensen a minute later to score the side’s sixth try of the first half. While McReight topped the Wallabies’ tackle count with 16, there is a school of thought that Carlo Tizzano, who is slightly bigger and more physical, could be better suited to starting against the All Blacks. His opposite Peter Lakai, meanwhile, was named player of the match.



Harry Wilson of the Wallabies is tackled. Getty Images 8. Harry Wilson - 5 Struggled to back up his brilliant Test a week earlier. Wilson tried his backside off and carried for a team-high 14 carries. He also made 11 tackles. But the impact wasn’t there. 9. Ryan Lonergan - 5 Got on the ball a couple of occasions, including a key turnover in the 14th minute. The Wallabies countered and should have made the All Blacks pay. But along with his good work over the ball, the little No.9 missed a bunch of tackles. He also couldn’t get his running game going, nor control the Test, because of the serious pace and power the All Blacks were playing with.



10. Declan Meredith - 6 Thrown in the deep end against the All Blacks, Meredith won plenty of fans for his hearty display. The Brumbies playmaker never stopped trying. He almost scored and he denied Beauden Barrett a third try too. He also set up the Wallabies’ only try of the first half by offloading to Williams to score next to the sticks. But Meredith, 27, also kicked out on the full twice from restarts in the first half and kicked dead from a penalty in the 73rd minute. Declan Meredith almost scored for the Wallabies. Getty Images 11. Harry Potter – 4 Struggled to get into the match. The Wallabies winger found the touchline from a pass in the 37th minute.



12. Isaac Henry – 4.5 A sitting duck at times in the first half as the All Blacks’ attack burned the Wallabies. Henry made a couple of strong and direct runs, but he wasn’t seen nearly enough. 13. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii – 5 The Wallabies’ most expensive player was on show early and sparked a line break with a fine offload. He also won a kick restart in the 14th minute. But Suaalii was found out a fair bit in defence, missing five tackles. The Wallabies’ midfield missed nine tackles. Getty Images



14. Max Jorgensen - 5.5 The Wallabies’ star winger experienced a real rollercoaster of a ride. Jorgensen made seven clean line breaks but his decision-making didn’t always pay off. The rising star also coughed up two tries either side of half-time, throwing an intercept for Beauden Barrett and being outfoxed by Moorby out wide. 15.Tom Wright – 5 Just like Jorgensen, Wright had a night filled with razzle dazzle but some serious lows too. He helped the Wallabies spark a couple of line breaks inside the opening 10 minutes, and he scored in the 54th minute, but he also dropped a simple pass in the second half and threw a ball into touch. The Wallabies’ back three created plenty of opportunities but couldn’t put the All Blacks away. Getty Images



Replacements 16. Billy Pollard - 5 One or two nice efforts in the second half after replacing Nasser, but didn’t look like a world beater either. 17. Angus Bell - 6 One of the Wallabies’ best. Bell replaced Ross in the second half and immediately made a difference. The loose-head prop was direct and thundering.



18. Massimo De Lutiis - 4.5 Barely sighted after replacing Alaalatoa. 19. Josh Canham - 5 Made an immediate impact when he came on and had one surging run in the 56th minute. But Canham also gave away a few penalties, including at the lineout. The Wallabies react during their loss in Sydney. Getty Images



20. Carlo Tizzano - 6 Brought onto the bench to provide some impact and energy, Tizzano got straight into the action and won a penalty in the 49th minute. 21. Kalani Thomas - 5.5 Had limited minutes, but Thomas made the most of it during his cameo. He helped deny Samisoni Taukei’aho by holding the giant hooker up along with Jorgensen. 22. Harry McLaughlin-Phillips - N/A



Wallaby 1001, McLaughlin-Phillips got seven minutes at the end and was busy. He threw one nice pass and took the ball to the line on a couple of occasions. 23. Filipo Daugunu - 5 Another who provided some energy in the second half. Daugunu scored one try but he also gave away a penalty and dropped one ball. World.title: Jayda had a light that made people stop. Hundreds just gathered to make sure it stays burning
World.content:
NationalVictoriaCrime Jayda had a light that made people stop. Hundreds just gathered to make sure it stays burning James Costa October 17, 2026 — 9:20pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

This story contains the name and images of an Indigenous person who has died. Hundreds of people gathered for a smoking ceremony and marched to Parliament House honouring 21-year-old Jayda Allen Bonner, who was allegedly murdered by her partner. At least 300 people gathered on Saturday afternoon at Cardigan Street, Carlton, in front of a growing memorial with dozens of bouquets and messages of love, for an emotional smoking ceremony, where family, friends and community members remembered Bonner and called for change. Jayda’s family at the smoking ceremony in memory of Jayda Allen in Carlton. Simon Schulter The 21-year-old, who was born in Melbourne’s inner north, was found dead in an apartment complex on Cardigan Street at about 1.45am on Saturday, October 10. A 31-year-old man turned himself into police on Wednesday and was charged with murder.



The young woman with a “heart of gold” – who dreamed of moving to Queensland to help Indigenous children – had allegedly been kept isolated in the unit on Cardigan Street for months. Earlier this week, Bonner’s aunt, Kellie Carter-Bell, said the family was not allowed to see her body to say goodbye due to the nature of the injuries. But Bonner’s mother was granted one last embrace. Related Article Crime Jayda’s body was so badly injured, her mum couldn’t look as she held her hand one last time “Enough is enough,” yelled Wurundjeri woman Kathleen Terrick, a treaty assembly member for the metro region who was performing the ceremony. After a minute of silence, some in the crowd called “justice for Jayda”. As they walked through the smoke and had ash applied to their faces, family and friends sobbed, comforting each other. They invited other mourners to share in their cultural tradition



“Let’s take a stand today against domestic violence, for this young woman who deserved so much better,” Terrick said. As gatherers marched along Lygon Street, down to the State Library and then back up to parliament they chanted “not one more” and called for men to “stop killing our women”. On parliament steps, Carter-Bell said there was something about Bonner that was “difficult to explain”. “She had a special aura, a presence, a light that you felt when she was around you, and that light should not be dimming today. Jayda Allen Bonner’s aunt, Kellie Carter-Bell, at the smoking ceremony. Simon Schluter



“Our family will spend the rest of our lives carrying the pain of knowing that someone we love so dearly is never coming home.” Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation Djirra said in a statement, endorsed by Jayda’s family and co-signed by leading Victorian Aboriginal organisations, that it was “a horrifying disgrace”. “Jayda’s death was entirely preventable, not inevitable,” the statement said. “While her death is now a criminal investigation, it is also a widespread systems failure, especially of the management of high-risk family violence offenders, the management of offenders leaving prison and how we support Aboriginal women and their families to be heard and believed.” Related Article Editorial

Domestic violence DV killings are our failure to protect the most vulnerable The Herald's View Editorial



There have been 55 women killed as a result of gendered violence in Australia in 2026, of whom Bonner was the seventh Indigenous woman allegedly murdered, according to advocacy body Australian Femicide Watch. Carter-Bell said that she thought Bonner would have been “very embarrassed but extremely proud” by the number of people who turned out to remember her. “I just wish we could have let her know how much we loved her, and [how much] he didn’t love her. “If victims just had the chance to realise how many people care, because the perpetrator’s biggest goal is to make us feel like no one cares.” If you or anyone you know needs support, you can contact the National Sexual Assault, Domestic and Family Violence Counselling Service on 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732), Lifeline 131 114, 13YARN (13 92 76), Yarning Safe’N’Strong (1800 959 563), or Beyond Blue 1300 224 636.
